abstract:
AIMS: This meta-analysis assessed the long-term impact of beta-blocker therapy on all-cause mortality and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who continued beta-blocker use for a minimum of 1 year after hospital discharge.
METHODS: Electronic databases were searched through September 2024 to identify studies comparing long-term outcomes in patients treated with beta-blockers versus those untreated. A random-effects model was used to estimate Hazard Ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 21 studies involving 270 566 patients were included. In pooled analyses, extended beta-blocker was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality in STEMI patients [HR: 0.74 (0.66, 0.83); P < 0.0001] and showing non-significant trend toward reducing cardiac death [HR: 0.77 (0.56, 1.04); P = 0.09], an effect observed predominantly in observational studies. However, in randomized controlled trials (N = 3), no significant benefit was demonstrated (all-cause mortality: P = 0.67; cardiac death: P = 0.62). No meaningful differences were found for major adverse cardiovascular events [HR: 0.90 (0.76, 1.07); P = 0.22], myocardial infarction, hospitalization for heart failure, or revascularization.
CONCLUSION: Long-term beta-blocker use is associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality among STEMI patients, though this benefit was not seen in RCTs. Effects on other cardiovascular outcomes remain uncertain, highlighting the need for further large-scale trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis; 21 studies involving 270 566 patients, of which 3 were RCTs.
appraisal.main_limitation: The apparent benefit comes predominantly from observational studies, which are open to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis suggests that long-term beta-blocker use after STEMI was associated with lower mortality in observational studies but not in randomised trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In pooled analyses, extended beta-blocker was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality in STEMI patients [HR: 0.74 (0.66, 0.83); P < 0.0001]; in randomized controlled trials (N = 3), no significant benefit was demonstrated (all-cause mortality: P = 0.67; cardiac death: P = 0.62).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Duration of beta-blocker therapy after MI is a debated decision.

title: Prognostic impact of long-term beta-blockers post-stemi: a meta-analytic review.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: The incidence rate of paraganglioma stands at approximately 1 case per 300 000 person-years. Symptoms resembling anxiety and panic attacks are prevalent within the general populace, rendering the identification of individuals afflicted with pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma a formidable task for healthcare practitioners.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 43-year-old presented with ischemic signs that turned into necrosis at his left foot due to diffused thrombosis in his main arteries, furthermore Echodiagram indicated the presence of left ventricular thrombosis, through which the diagnosis of paraganglioma was made and confirmed through histological examination.
CLINICAL DISCUSSION: Paragangliomas are rare tumors originating from extra-adrenal chromaffin cells, typically found in areas such as the carotid body and aortic arch. These tumors can cause cardiovascular issues like hypertension, tachycardia, and thrombus formation. In this case, a paraganglioma was detected below the renal arteries, an uncommon location, with extensive arterial and left ventricular thrombi. Paragangliomas induce a hypercoagulable state due to catecholamine excess, vasospasm, and vascular compression, as seen in this patient, who had thrombi in the lower extremities and aortic artery, increasing embolization risks. Diagnosis involves clinical evaluation, biochemical testing, and imaging studies, with surgical resection as the primary treatment. Preoperative management focuses on controlling blood pressure and glucose, while postoperative care includes anticoagulation therapy. This case highlights the multifaceted vascular complications of paragangliomas, emphasizing the need for a comprehensive diagnostic and treatment approach.
CONCLUSION: Increasing follow-up sessions with this patient to prevent recurring issues, including the consideration of coronary vascular imaging and administrating anti-coagulant drugs.
title: Left ventricular thrombus formation in paraganglioma: a rare but serious complication - a case report.

abstract: Phaeochromocytoma crisis is a rare, life-threatening endocrine emergency characterised by profound haemodynamic instability and multiorgan dysfunction. We report the case of a previously healthy 31-year-old woman who presented with sudden-onset cardiopulmonary decompensation, marked blood-pressure variability, pulmonary oedema, and cardiogenic shock, with biochemical evidence of myocardial injury. Echocardiography demonstrated apical hypercontractility with akinesia of the basal and midventricular segments and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%, consistent with reverse takotsubo cardiomyopathy. Cross-sectional imaging revealed a large 9 cm left adrenal mass, which, together with markedly elevated plasma and urinary metanephrines, confirmed the diagnosis of phaeochromocytoma crisis. The patient required mechanical ventilation, vasoactive support, and intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation. Following successful resuscitation and stabilisation with α- and β-adrenergic blockade, she underwent elective laparoscopic left adrenalectomy. Histopathological examination confirmed a high-risk phaeochromocytoma, while genetic testing was negative. Postoperatively, metanephrine concentrations normalised and bi-ventricular cardiac function recovered completely. This case highlights the importance of considering phaeochromocytoma crisis in patients presenting with otherwise unexplained haemodynamic instability and stress cardiomyopathy. Early recognition, multidisciplinary critical care, appropriate adrenergic blockade, and timely definitive surgery are essential and can be lifesaving.
title: Phaeochromocytoma Crisis Presenting As Inverted Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy in a Young Woman: A Successful Outcome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients surviving acute myocardial infarction (AMI) complicated by ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) are at high risk of early post-discharge readmissions due to multiple complications. These readmissions worsen clinical outcomes and add substantial financial strain to the U.S. healthcare system. This study investigates the prevalence, causes, and predictors of 30-day readmissions following hospitalization for AMI complicated by VAs.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Hospitalizations for AMI complicated by VAs were identified from the 2016-2017 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Independent predictors of 30-day readmission were analyzed using multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression in the R statistical software (version 4.5.0). Among 93 588 index hospitalizations, 8154 (8.7%) resulted in 30-day readmissions. In-hospital mortality occurred in 16.43% of index admissions and 5.92% of readmissions. Significant predictors of readmission included older age (OR: 1.01; P < 0.001), female sex (OR: 1.13; P = 0.002), prior heart failure (OR: 1.28; P < 0.001), peripheral vascular disease (OR: 1.18; P = 0.002), COPD (OR: 1.43; P < 0.001), atrial fibrillation (OR: 1.24; P < 0.001), diabetes (OR: 1.29; P < 0.001), previous MI (OR: 1.12; P = 0.009), end-stage renal disease (ESRD) (OR: 1.52; P < 0.001), stroke (OR: 1.52; P < 0.001), and hospital stay >4 days (OR: 1.94; P < 0.001). Higher income quartiles were associated with lower readmission risk. The mean index charges were $151 722, whereas charges per readmission were $64 122.
CONCLUSIONS: AMI complicated by VAs is associated with high 30-day readmission rates, driven mainly by noncardiac and select cardiac causes such as heart failure and atrial fibrillation. Enhanced monitoring of high-risk groups may improve outcomes and reduce healthcare costs.
title: Prevalence, causes, and predictors of 30-day readmissions after acute myocardial infarction with ventricular arrhythmias: a cohort study using the 2016-2017 national readmissions database.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome leads to disturbances in physiological parameters and reduces patient comfort due to the nature of the disease and its associated complications. This study examined the effect of local heat therapy on the comfort and physiological parameters of patients with acute coronary syndrome.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This clinical trial utilized a block randomization method to allocate 80 patients with acute coronary syndrome into two groups of 40 participants each. In the intervention group, a heat pack warmed in water to 75 °C was wrapped in a special towel and applied to the posterior thoracic region (T4-T11 vertebrae). During the intervention, the patient lay in the supine position on the heat pack. Each heat therapy session lasted 23 minutes. In the control group, a similar heat pack was used at a temperature of 37°C. Heat therapy was performed every 12 hours for 2 days (a total of four sessions). The Kolkaba Comfort Questionnaire and physiological parameters were assessed pre- and post-intervention. Data analysis was performed with statistical significance established at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Before the intervention, no significant differences were found between the groups. However, at the end of the intervention, heat therapy in patients with acute coronary syndrome significantly increased comfort, regulation of physiological parameters was observed, and enhanced oxygen saturation (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Heat therapy can be used as a safe and complementary intervention alongside modern medicine to enhance comfort and regulate physiological parameters in patients with acute coronary syndrome.
journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research
title: The Impact of Local Heat Therapy on Comfort and Physiological Parameters in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; the abstract gives no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract describes a narrative synthesis and does not state how evidence was graded.
appraisal.one_line: An American Heart Association scientific statement on multidisciplinary antiplatelet management in acute and chronic coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It sets out a team-based framework for antithrombotic stewardship and is likely to be cited in practice and guideline discussion.

title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

abstract: Fractional flow reserve (FFR) assessment represents the most widely used revascularisation strategy of the last two decades. However, many FFR (+) lesions, particularly those in the grey zone, can be safely treated medically, while other lesions carrying vulnerable plaque (VP) features can cause future events despite the absence of ischaemia. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) can identify lesions with VP morphology. The objective of this study is to determine whether a combined revascularisation strategy - targeting only severely ischaemic lesions (FFR ≤0.75) and extending treatment to OCT-assessed VP, even in the absence of ischaemia (FFR>0.80) - could reduce future adverse events compared with the current revascularisation practice based exclusively on the presence of ischaemia (FFR ≤0.80). The COMBINE-INTERVENE Trial is a global, prospective, randomised, single-blinded, sham-controlled, superiority trial. A total of 1,223 all-comer patients with multivessel disease (≥2 lesions with a diameter of stenosis ≥50%) will be randomised 1:1 to revascularisation if the FFR is ≤0.75 or a VP is present (experimental arm) versus FFR ≤0.80 in the comparative arm. The primary endpoint is a composite of cardiac death, any myocardial infarction, or any clinically driven revascularisation within 24 months. The trial has already completed enrolment in 50 centres worldwide. COMBINE-INTERVENE is the first trial evaluating the impact of a revascularisation strategy that targets lesions that are either severely ischaemic or carry an OCT-assessed VP versus revascularisation based on ischaemia alone. The trial is powered for superiority. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05333068).
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
title: Combined ischaemia and vulnerable plaque percutaneous coronary intervention to reduce cardiovascular events: design and rationale of the COMBINE-INTERVENE Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between intraoperative trigemino-cardiac reflex (TCR) and postoperative myocardial injury in patients undergoing skull base tumor resection remains unclear.
METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled patients undergoing elective skull base tumor resection between April 2023 and September 2024. The primary outcome was postoperative myocardial injury, defined as a cardiac troponin I level >16 ng/L within 24 hours after surgery. Patients were categorized into TCR and non-TCR groups. Logistic regression analyses were performed to explore factors associated with intraoperative TCR and postoperative myocardial injury.
RESULTS: Among 476 included patients, intraoperative TCR occurred in 27.9%, and postoperative myocardial injury occurred in 4.83%. Patients experiencing TCR had a higher rate of myocardial injury (8.3% vs. 3.5%, P=0.029). Multivariable analysis suggested that brainstem compression (adjusted OR=1.86; 95% CI: 1.19-2.91; P=0.007) and larger tumor diameter (adjusted OR=1.04; 95% CI: 1.02-1.07; P<0.001) independently associated with intraoperative TCR. TCR (adjusted OR=2.70; 95% CI: 1.12-6.53; P=0.028), older age (adjusted OR=1.06; 95% CI: 1.02-1.10; P=0.003), lower BMI (adjusted OR=0.80; 95% CI: 0.70-0.93; P=0.003), and tumor recurrence (adjusted OR=4.07; 95% CI: 1.43-11.57; P=0.009) were associated with postoperative myocardial injury after adjusting for selected confounders.
CONCLUSION: Postoperative myocardial injury occurred in 4.83% of skull base tumor surgery patients. Intraoperative TCR increased the risk of this injury, though the link may relate to surgical complexity and patient characteristics. TCR may therefore serve as a potential clinical marker of patients at elevated perioperative cardiovascular risk rather than a direct causal mechanism.
title: Association of Intraoperative Trigeminal Cardiac Reflex With Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Skull Base Tumor Surgery: A Prospective Cohort Study.

abstract: Myocardial infarction before 30 years of age warrants evaluation beyond conventional atherosclerosis, particularly when a second arterial event occurs in another vascular bed. A 25-year-old man with a nine-pack-year history of tobacco smoking and occasional cannabis use presented with anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention of the left anterior descending artery. Left ventricular ejection fraction was 30%, with severe apical wall-motion abnormality. Twelve days after discharge, he developed acute left popliteal artery occlusion (Rutherford IIb), which improved to IIa and subsequently to I during therapeutic anticoagulation and was managed without revascularization. Fasting homocysteine measured on day 21 was 18.4 µmol/L, with a vitamin B12 level of 121 pg/mL and a folate level of 1.9 ng/mL. Vitamin B12 replacement and folic acid 5 mg/day were prescribed; fasting homocysteine remained mildly elevated at approximately 6 and 18 months (21.6 and 20.7 µmol/L, respectively), with follow-up folate levels of 5.2 and 4.7 ng/mL. Renal and thyroid function were not reassessed at these later measurements. Genotyping showed compound heterozygosity for MTHFR C677T (Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase) and A1298C, which was considered an accompanying finding rather than a causal thrombophilia. A missed or transient left ventricular apical thrombus represents a plausible, and possibly the most likely, explanation for the limb event. The patient remained free of recurrent thrombotic or bleeding events for 18 months while receiving an individualized warfarin regimen.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) progression is a recognized complication of cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantation, yet its prognostic impact on long-term clinical outcomes remains incompletely defined.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this single-center retrospective cohort, 303 patients undergoing CIED implantation between 2005 and 2023 were followed for a median of 4.8 years. TR severity was assessed echocardiographically at baseline and 12 months. The primary endpoint was TR progression (≥ 1-grade worsening); secondary endpoints were all-cause mortality, cardiovascular hospitalization, their composite, and progression to severe TR, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression. TR progressed in 103 patients (34.0%), regressed in 33 (10.9%), and remained stable in 167 (55.1%), a net rightward shift (p < 0.001). Progression differed by device type (p = 0.031): among the larger subgroups, VVI-ICD showed the greatest net progression (31.8% worsened vs. 6.9% improved; p < 0.001) and CRT-D the highest regression (18.8%). During follow-up, 67 patients (22.1%) died and 164 (54.1%) were hospitalized. Overall TR progression was not independently associated with mortality (HR 1.118, p = 0.693) but independently predicted cardiovascular hospitalization (HR 1.640, p = 0.003) and the composite endpoint (HR 1.480, p = 0.014). On unadjusted analysis, progression specifically to severe TR (n = 15) was associated with increased mortality (HR 1.99, p = 0.024) and cardiovascular hospitalization (HR 2.45, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: TR progression occurs in approximately one-third of CIED recipients within the first year and independently predicts cardiovascular hospitalization. Progression to severe TR identifies a higher-risk subset, supporting routine post-implant echocardiographic surveillance.
title: Progression of Tricuspid Regurgitation After Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Implantation and Its Impact on Mortality and Hospitalization: A Single-Center Cohort Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicating pregnancy is rare, with a maternal case-fatality rate of 4.5%. ST-elevation myocardial infarction in a near-term gravida requires revascularization, fetal radiation protection, and multidisciplinary coordination.
CASE SUMMARY: A 32-year-old woman at 38 weeks of gestation with no cardiovascular risk factors presented with anterior STEMI from total left anterior descending artery occlusion. Emergent radial-access percutaneous coronary intervention was performed without sedation; intravascular ultrasound confirmed wire position through a thrombus-laden occlusion. Overlapping drug-eluting stents restored TIMI flow grade-3, with air kerma below fetal thresholds. Uninterrupted dual antiplatelet therapy continued through cesarean delivery, with blood loss controlled by hemostatic agents. Mother and neonate were discharged in good health.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights the ambiguity between thrombotic occlusion and spontaneous dissection in pregnancy, the role of intravascular ultrasound when angiography is unreliable, and antiplatelet decision-making when surgery follows percutaneous coronary intervention.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Emergent intravascular ultrasound-guided percutaneous coronary intervention is feasible at 38 weeks of gestation. Multidisciplinary planning, radiation mitigation, and individualized antiplatelet strategy determine outcomes.
title: STEMI at Term Managed With IVUS-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Cesarean Delivery.
Anatomy Before Occlusion: When an Aorto-Right Ventricular Tunnel Replaces the RCA.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve leaflet perforation is generally considered unsuitable anatomy for transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER), with published experience largely limited to bailout treatment of iatrogenic perforations.
CASE SUMMARY: A 75-year-old man with severe symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR) was referred for TEER. Intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) unexpectedly revealed a large posterior mitral leaflet perforation. Guided by 3D multiplanar reconstruction imaging, 2 XTW MitraClip devices were deployed on both sides of the perforation, effectively "sandwiching" the defect between the clips and reducing MR from severe to mild.
DISCUSSION: This case supports the feasibility of MitraClip as a primary treatment for mitral leaflet perforation in carefully selected patients. TEE with 3D multiplanar reconstruction imaging enabled accurate anatomic characterization and facilitated precise device positioning, resulting in an excellent procedural outcome.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Mitral valve leaflet perforation may be amenable to TEER in select cases. 3D TEE imaging is critical for procedural planning and helps to facilitate precise device positioning.
title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair of Mitral Valve Leaflet Perforation Guided by 3D Multiplanar Reconstruction Imaging.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) often presents with eosinophilic myocarditis, but the spectrum of cardiac findings is scarcely reported. We describe a case of EGPA with an unusual presentation of acute left ventricular (LV) dysfunction associated with lymphocyte-predominant myocardial inflammation and Takotsubo-like syndrome with LV thrombus.
CASE SUMMARY: A 42-year-old woman with history of asthma presented with chronic cough, dyspnea, and rash. Findings of peripheral eosinophilia, cutaneous vasculitis, mononeuritis multiplex, and myocardial inflammation confirmed antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies-negative EGPA. Her course was complicated by transient severe LV systolic dysfunction with Takotsubo-like regional wall-motion abnormalities, lymphocyte-predominant myocardial inflammation on biopsy, and LV thrombus. Management included pulse-dosed steroids, rituximab, and mepolizumab.
DISCUSSION: Although EGPA frequently causes cardiac manifestations, typically eosinophilic myocarditis, an overlap phenotype of inflammatory myocardial injury, Takotsubo-like cardiomyopathy, and LV thrombus is exceedingly rare.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Cardiac involvement remains the leading cause of mortality in EGPA. This case highlights the heterogeneity of its cardiac phenotypes, illustrating the importance of early cardiology evaluation and diagnostics.
title: Cardiac Manifestations of EGPA: An Overlap Phenotype of Inflammatory Myocardial Injury and Takotsubo-Like Syndrome.

abstract: Within arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse (AMVP), a distinct subset of mitral valve prolapse (MVP), there is a small group that carries a higher risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death called malignant MVP. The malignant MVP phenotype is over-represented in young women with unexplained sudden cardiac death on autopsy. AMVP is defined by myxomatous, often bileaflet MVP with mitral annular disjunction, abnormal valvular-myocardial mechanics, complex ventricular ectopy, and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. Excessive mechanical force from systolic annular expansion, papillary muscle traction, and basal inferolateral "curling" promotes focal replacement and diffuse interstitial fibrosis, creating an arrhythmogenic substrate. Premature ventricular contractions act as triggers, whereas autonomic modulation influences the timing of ventricular arrhythmia initiation and progression to ventricular fibrillation or sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Baseline evaluation with an electrocardiogram and transthoracic echocardiography is necessary to identify AMVP, exclude severe mitral regurgitation, and identify high-risk markers. If no premature ventricular contractions are found on a resting electrocardiogram, exercise stress testing and extended rhythm monitoring can help bring out ventricular premature contractions, which are triggers of ventricular arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance provides incremental prognostic value with late gadolinium enhancement reflecting replacement fibrosis and T1 mapping identifying diffuse fibrosis, even in those with no late gadolinium enhancement. Machine-learning analysis may further refine risk stratification by integrating high-risk features such as mitral annular disjunction, fibrosis extent, and location that outperform symptom-based assessment. As transcatheter and surgical mitral interventions expand, accurate phenotyping of AMVP is increasingly important, as hemodynamic correction of mitral regurgitation alone does not eliminate the underlying arrhythmogenic substrate. Comprehensive multimodality imaging and integrated rhythm assessment are therefore central to individualized risk stratification and management in this vulnerable population.
title: Identifying the High-Risk Arrhythmic Mitral Valve Prolapse Phenotype by Imaging.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cangrelor reduces thrombotic events in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), with the advantage of rapid onset and offset. However, premature discontinuation may increase the risk of acute thrombosis for patients undergoing complex/high-risk PCI (CHIP).
AIMS: We evaluated the real-world administration of cangrelor and related health outcomes for CHIP patients.
METHODS: A US retrospective physician panel medical chart review (1/1/2020 to 6/26/2025) included patients 18+ years old who received cangrelor (1st dose = index date) during CHIP. We summarized patients' characteristics in the 6 months pre-index (baseline), cangrelor dosing and administration (IV bolus and/or infusion), and clinical outcomes within 48 h. We described MACE occurrence by dosing adherence.
RESULTS: Patients (n = 200) were mostly male (85.5%), had a mean age of 63 years, and had a BMI of 30.2 kg/m2. Most (87.5%) received a cangrelor bolus (30.0 µg/kg) and maintenance infusion (4.0 µg/kg/mins), aligned with intended use recommendations. Of patients analyzed for infusion duration (n = 134), 64.9% deviated from the recommendation of at least 2 h or PCI length. Forty (29.9%) received cangrelor for less than the recommended duration. Overall, 30 (15%) patients experienced MACE, with a higher proportion of MACE seen in those who deviated from the recommended duration (16.1% [95% CI: 3.5%-23.1%] vs. 10.6% [95% CI: 9.1%-25.5%]).
CONCLUSIONS: Our study provides real-world insight into cangrelor use and clinical outcomes in CHIP patients, highlighting notable variability in infusion duration and differences in MACE occurrence by dosing adherence. Further comparative effectiveness studies are warranted to examine the potential impact of deviation from intended dose/duration on clinical outcomes in CHIP.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Cangrelor Dosing, Administration, and Clinical Outcomes for Patients Undergoing Complex and High-Risk Percutaneous Coronary Interventions.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractional flow reserve (FFR)-guided coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) may reduce unnecessary grafts and improve outcomes. However, in the FARGO (Fractional Flow Reserve vs Angiography Randomization for Graft Optimization) trial, FFR was reduced significantly after 6 months in deferred lesions.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes after FFR-guided CABG compared to angiography-guided CABG.
METHODS: In this multicenter randomized clinical trial, 100 patients were randomized to FFR-guided (n = 50) or angiography-guided CABG (n = 50). Patients underwent a 6-month follow-up coronary angiography with FFR in deferred lesions. In this extended long-term follow-up revascularization, myocardial infarction, stroke, death, and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), a composite of the individual endpoints, were assessed.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 8.8 years (IQR: 8.3, 9.3), patients in the FFR-guided group had significantly more MACCE compared to the angiography-guided group, (26 [52%] vs 16 [32%], log-rank test P = 0.03). This difference was driven by significantly more long-term revascularization, FFR-guided CABG 32% vs angiography-guided 12%, log-rank test P = 0.01. The revascularization rate was significantly higher from 0 to 1 year (12 [24%] vs 3 [6%], log-rank test P = 0.01), whereas beyond 1 year, rates were similar (4 [8%] vs 3 [6%], log-rank test P = 0.47). Most patients had stable symptoms, and revascularization was symptom-driven. Myocardial infarction (6 [12%] vs 3 [6%]), death (10 [20%] vs 7 [14%]), and stroke (6 [12%] vs 6 [12%]) did not differ significantly between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: FFR-guided CABG was associated with a significantly higher rate of MACCE after CABG, driven by more revascularization within the first year.

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of a randomised trial; median follow-up of 8.8 years; the abstract does not state the total sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Very small sample, and revascularisation was largely symptom-driven.
appraisal.one_line: A long-term follow-up of a randomised comparison of FFR-guided and angiography-guided CABG.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients in the FFR-guided group had significantly more MACCE compared to the angiography-guided group, (26 [52%] vs 16 [32%], log-rank test P = 0.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It adds long-term randomised data on physiology-guided surgical revascularisation, though the small size limits inference.

title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes After Physiology-Guided vs Angiography-Guided Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: From the FARGO Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) exhibits marked clinical heterogeneity, limiting the performance of conventional risk stratification tools like the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) staging system. Machine learning (ML) has identified reproducible CS phenotypes that improve risk prediction, but their temporal consistency across the progression of shock remains incompletely described.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the temporal evolution of ML-derived CS phenotypes across the first 3 intensive care unit (ICU) days and determine whether phenotype trajectories enhance mortality stratification beyond SCAI staging.
METHODS: In a multicenter retrospective registry of 2,906 adults with CS admitted to ICUs between 2016 and 2022, hierarchical agglomerative clustering was applied independently to clinical variables on ICU days 1, 2, and 3.
RESULTS: On day 1, 3 phenotypes emerged: Cardiac (younger, acute myocardial infarction-predominant, preserved renal function; 15% mortality), Cardio-Renal (older, non-acute myocardial infarction-predominant, isolated renal extracardiac impairment, predominantly SCAI A and B on admission; 27% mortality), and Cardio-Metabolic (severe renal and tissue malperfusion, predominantly SCAI D and E on admission; 55% mortality). Similar phenotypes persisted on day 2 and day 3. These ML-derived phenotypes enhanced mortality stratification within each SCAI stage across days 1 to 3.
CONCLUSIONS: Hierarchical clustering reproduced previously identified CS phenotypes that were consistent across the first 3 days of ICU stay, providing an enhanced framework for early risk stratification. Prospective validation is required for clinical implementation.
title: Enhanced Early Risk Stratification in Cardiogenic Shock Using Machine Learning: A Hierarchical Clustering Analysis.

abstract: Transient troponin elevation is a common observation in various nonischemic cardiovascular diseases, the origin of which remains widely unknown. We hypothesized that troponins enclosed in extracellular vesicles (EVs) and released by cardiomyocytes into circulation account for distinct disease-specific compartmental troponin signatures. In vitro, hypoxic cardiomyocytes secreted EVs enriched with cardiac troponin T (cTnT). Mice after myocardial infarction showed increased blood EV concentration, and pigs under induced atrial fibrillation showed distinct EV-cTnT signatures. These specific EV-cTnT and cardiac troponin I compartmental patterns were verified in 2 patient cohorts of myocardial infarction and atrial fibrillation, introducing relative EV-cardiac troponin as a novel biomarker to discriminate cardiovascular pathologies.
title: A Circulating Extracellular Vesicle-Bound Fraction of Cardiac Troponin Discriminates Myocardial Homeostasis and Disease States.
Rethinking Troponin Release: The Hidden Vesicular Compartment in Cardiovascular Medicine.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) is an established therapy for severe cardiac failure, but femoral decannulation remains associated with significant morbidity. Percutaneous decannulation has emerged as an alternative to surgical cutdown; however, published experience remains limited. This study evaluates a fully percutaneous VA-ECMO decannulation strategy using the Abbott ProStyle vascular closure device compared with open surgical cutdown.
METHODS: A retrospective single-centre matched cohort study identified all patients undergoing intended percutaneous VA-ECMO decannulation between November 2023 and January 2026 and matched them to a surgical cutdown cohort according to age and sex. Outcomes were assessed by intention-to-treat, with technically successful cases evaluated secondarily.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients underwent intended percutaneous VA-ECMO decannulation. Technical success was achieved in 82% (n = 23), with five conversions to open cutdown. On intention-to-treat analysis, procedural duration was shorter (94.1 ± 26.3 vs 121.7 ± 46.9 minutes, p = .063) and groin wound complications were less frequent (7.1% vs 25.0%, p = .077), although neither reached statistical significance. Among technically successful percutaneous decannulations, procedural duration was significantly shorter (88.0 ± 28.7 vs 120.8 ± 50.0 minutes, p = .020) and groin wound complications significantly lower (4.3% vs 30.4%, p = .047). Survival to discharge was similar between groups (p = .78).
CONCLUSION: Percutaneous VA-ECMO decannulation achieved 82% technical success, with numerically shorter procedural duration and fewer groin wound complications on intention-to-treat analysis. Among technically successful cases, both outcomes were significantly improved compared with surgical cutdown.
title: Mid-Term Outcomes of Percutaneous Decannulation for Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Weaning: A Single-Centre Experience.

abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Women with cardiogenic shock (CS) under VA-ECMO face excess mortality, yet the pharmacological basis of this disparity remains poorly understood. Arginine vasopressin (AVP) is increasingly used as a non-adrenergic vasopressor in this setting, but whether sex modifies the hemodynamic response to AVP is unknown.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort of VA-ECMO-supported CS patients, we assessed whether sex was independently associated with successful vasopressor de-escalation at 48 hours (norepinephrine equivalent dose [NEE] <0.25 µg/kg/min) after AVP initiation. Multivariable logistic regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate sex differences in treatment response and NEE trajectories over time.
RESULTS: Among 193 eligible patients, 32% of women achieved successful de-escalation versus 49% of men (p = 0.023). Male sex was independently associated with treatment success (aOR 2.08, 95% CI 1.07-4.15, p = 0.033). A significant sex-by-time interaction was observed in NEE trajectories (p = 0.041), with divergence emerging at 48 hours (NEE 0.24 vs. 0.01 µg/kg/min, p = 0.008). The excess failure risk was confined to postmenopausal women aged ≥55 years (aOR 2.75, 95% CI 1.32-5.93, p = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: Female sex, particularly in a postmenopausal context, was independently associated with impaired vasopressor de-escalation following AVP in CS on VA-ECMO. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that hormonal status may modulate vascular responsiveness to AVP and support the need for prospective studies incorporating hormonal profiling.
title: Sex Differences in Vasopressor De-escalation With Arginine Vasopressin in Mixed Cardiogenic-Vasodilatory Shock Under VA-ECMO.

abstract: This letter describes the derivation and internal validation of an assay-specific hs-cTnI-SPINCHIP 0/2h-algorithm for rapid triage of patients with suspected myocardial infarction (MI) in the emergency department (ED). The algorithm provided very high safety for rule-out, high accuracy for rule-in, and enabled definitive triage within 2 hours in approximately 80% of patients. These findings support the clinical potential of the novel point-of-care hs-cTnI-SPINCHIP assay for accelerated ED decision-making.
title: A 0/2-Hour Algorithm Using a Novel Point-of-Care High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Assay for Suspected Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although operative mortality after open thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair is well characterized, only limited data describe 1-year survival among patients who survive the index hospitalization. This study sought to further characterize 1-year mortality among operative survivors of open TAAA repair.
METHODS: From January 1986 through July 2025, 3838 open TAAA repairs were performed within our single practice. After operative deaths and patients lacking 1-year follow-up were excluded, 3378 early survivors comprised the study cohort. Demographic, operative, and postoperative data were compared between patients who survived ≥1 year after repair and those who did not. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 1-year mortality.
RESULTS: Among early survivors, 328 (9.7%) died within 1 year. One-year mortality was associated with older age, prior percutaneous coronary intervention, prior stroke, and chronic kidney disease. Postoperative complications-namely paraplegia (odds ratio [OR] 1.96, P=.03), dialysis dependence (OR 2.00, P=.001), arrhythmia (OR 1.48, P=.01), tracheostomy (OR 2.17, P<.001), and 1-year repair failure (OR 5.13, P<.001)-independently predicted death, whereas elective repair (OR 0.57, P<.001) and discharge home (OR 0.38, P<.001) predicted 1-year survival. Model discrimination was good (C-statistic=0.77 [0.74-0.81]). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed markedly greater 1-year survival in patients initially discharged home (94%) versus elsewhere (73%; P<.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Among operative survivors of open TAAA repair, 1-year mortality remains considerable and is primarily determined by persistent postoperative complications and repair durability rather than intraoperative variables. Vigilant surveillance, structured rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary follow-up may be needed to ensure success beyond the perioperative period.
title: Characterizing One-Year Mortality in Early Survivors of Open Thoracoabdominal Aortic Repair.

abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in patients with small aortic annuli presents unique challenges related to prosthesis-patient mismatch, residual gradients, conduction disturbances, and lifetime valve management. Recent observational data have suggested potential differences in mid-term survival between self-expanding valve and balloon-expandable valve platforms; however, these findings have not been consistently supported by other observational studies or long-term randomized evidence. Importantly, both severe prosthesis-patient mismatch and permanent pacemaker implantation may carry prognostic implications, underscoring the competing risks involved in valve selection. In conclusion, current evidence does not establish the clinical superiority of one transcatheter valve platform over another, supporting an individualized approach to valve selection.
title: Evidence on Valve Selection for Small Aortic Annuli in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the existing literature on antithrombotic strategies employed after transcatheter valve-in-valve (ViV) and valve-in-ring (ViR) procedures across all valve groups and to provide recommendations for areas of further research.
DESIGN: We conducted a scoping review reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines.
DATA SOURCES: We systematically searched CENTRAL, EMBASE and MEDLINE from database inception until 19 January 2026. Reference lists of included studies were also manually screened.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised-controlled trials, cohort or case-control studies reporting efficacy and/or safety outcomes of antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing transcatheter ViV or ViR procedures involving aortic, mitral, tricuspid and/or pulmonary valves were included.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Records were screened for eligibility and data were extracted using a structured charting form. Results were synthesised descriptively and grouped according to valve type.
RESULTS: Of 444 studies screened, 41 were included (10 aortic ViV, 27 mitral ViV/ViR, 1 pulmonary ViV, 1 tricuspid ViV and 2 aortic and mitral ViV). Median sample size was 32 (IQR 14–91; range 5–4243). Ten studies reported a uniform antithrombotic strategy; 30 reported variable strategies, and 1 reported only a protocol-recommended strategy without observed use or adherence. Anticoagulation, with or without antiplatelet therapy, was commonly reported following mitral ViV/ViR, while regimens reported following aortic ViV were highly variable but antiplatelet therapy predominated slightly over anticoagulant therapy. Thrombotic and bleeding outcomes were reported in a highly heterogenous manner.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence guiding antithrombotic therapy after ViV is heterogeneous and largely observational, underscoring the need for high-quality studies to inform optimal management.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: This scoping review is registered on the Open Science Framework and can be accessed at: https://osf.io/exvc2/overview?view_only=aeb99d7b79734510826a8ce408e70b03.
title: Antithrombotic therapy regimens after transcatheter valve-in-valve and valve-in-ring procedures: a scoping review.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Previous studies have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can achieve performance comparable to multidisciplinary heart teams (HTs) in coronary revascularisation decision-making but limited by population bias. We aimed to assess LLMs’ performance in complex coronary artery disease (CAD) decision-making using a real-world cohort and to explore the potential improvement strategy.
METHODS: Patients with stable CAD and angiographically confirmed three-vessel or left main disease randomly selected from a consecutive angiography registry study were included in this cross-sectional study. ChatGPT-4.1 was used to provide five-category treatment decisions based on inputted patient information and a prompt most commonly used by real-world patients. The primary outcome was the agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations. Three predefined prompting strategies were further evaluated for their potential to enhance agreement rates.
RESULTS: A total of 564 patients were included. The agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations was 47.0% based on initial prompt. LLM performed poorly in further testing (sensitivity=0.0%) decision. LLM performed well in patients with Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery score ≥33 (94.1%) but poorly in 23–32 (61.7%) and 0–22 (20.9%). After using prompting strategies, the agreement rate increased significantly (79.3%, p<0.001).
DISCUSSION: Simple patient-style queries cannot independently generate reliable decisions for real-world complex revascularisation scenarios. While prompt engineering and subgroup analysis can partially improve LLM’s performance, the potential safety risk remains emphasised.
CONCLUSION: Among a real-world cohort of patients with complex CAD, the agreement rate of decision-making between LLM and HTs was only half, but could be improved with appropriate prompts.
title: Performance of large language models in complex coronary artery disease decision-making and potential improvement strategy in a real-world cohort.
