abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Extracellular volume (ECV) quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is a key indicator of myocardial fibrosis and strongly linked to outcomes after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). This research focused on the development and validation of an interpretable machine learning (ML) model that incorporates ECV to predict 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE) in patients with STEMI following percutaneous coronary intervention.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: MACE prediction models were developed using clinical variables combined with CMR-ECV parameters and validated in a prospective cohort. Feature selection was conducted through Boruta algorithms and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator algorithms, and eight ML algorithms were trained. Model performance was assessed by discrimination and calibration. The top performer was interpreted by Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. An interactive online nomogram was deployed to facilitate personalized perioperative risk management.
RESULTS: Among 673 STEMI patients (derivation: n = 398; prospective validation: n = 275), five key predictors were identified: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), myocardial infarction ECV (MI-ECV), age, and creatine kinase-MB. The random forest model achieved the highest discriminative performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.825, 95% confidence interval: 0.763-0.876). SHAP analysis identified NT-proBNP as the most impactful feature, with LVEF class and MI-ECV ranking next.
CONCLUSION: Integration of CMR-derived ECV into an interpretable machine learning framework enables accurate 1-year MACE risk prediction following STEMI. This approach combines robust discriminative performance with clinical transparency through SHAP-based explanations, offering a proof-of-concept tool for precision cardiovascular care.
title: Development and Prospective Validation of an Interpretable Machine Learning Model Integrating Cardiac MRI Extracellular Volume for 1-Year MACE Prediction Post-STEMI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Phase 3 programs are evaluating Lp(a)-lowering therapies using high entry thresholds; however, the real-world prevalence of trial-aligned Lp(a) thresholds in secondary prevention remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence of trial-aligned Lp(a) thresholds, national apheresis criteria, and the prognostic impact of elevated Lp(a) in a contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) cohort.
METHODS: Patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary center with Lp(a) reported in nmol/L were analyzed. The proportion meeting trial-aligned thresholds (≥150, ≥175, ≥200 nmol/L) and the European Society of Cardiology/European Atherosclerosis Society risk-enhancing threshold (≥105 nmol/L) was estimated. National apheresis criteria were applied. 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and target lesion failure (TLF) were assessed.
RESULTS: Among 5942 patients with PCI, 25.2% had Lp(a) ≥105 nmol/L, with progressively smaller proportions meeting higher thresholds: 18.4% ≥150 nmol/L, 14.8% ≥175 nmol/L, 11.6% ≥200 nmol/L. Lp(a) concentrations were similar in chronic and acute coronary syndrome (CCS and ACS) (CCS, median 28.0 [IQR 9.0-118.5] vs ACS, 25.0 [IQR 9.0-96.5] nmol/L; P = .117). 1.8% to 6.1% met national apheresis criteria. Over 5 years, higher Lp(a) was independently associated with risk of MACE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1 SD 1.06 [95% CI 1.01-1.12]; P = .015) and TLF (adjusted HR per 1 SD 1.05 [95% CI 1.00-1.10]; P = .044).
CONCLUSION: Elevated Lp(a) was highly prevalent and independently predicted adverse 5-year outcomes in a contemporary PCI cohort. While a substantial proportion met trial-aligned Lp(a) thresholds for emerging therapies, few fulfilled apheresis criteria. Systematic Lp(a) testing may improve risk stratification and identify patients meeting trial-aligned Lp(a) thresholds for emerging therapies.
title: Real-world threshold-based eligibility for emerging lipoprotein(a)-targeted therapies in chronic and acute coronary syndrome.

abstract: Invasive coronary angiography is the reference standard for diagnosing coronary artery disease, yet assessment is subjective, and existing artificial-intelligence tools typically assess stenosis in individual frames or videos and do not integrate the full multiview angiographic study. Here we show that DeepCORO-CLIP, trained on 203,808 angiographic videos and reports from 28,117 patients, interprets whole multiple-video angiograms at once. It detects obstructive stenoses (≥70%), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.89 internally and externally, and identifies chronic total occlusion (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.95), intra-coronary thrombus and calcification (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.91). It also predicts 1-year cardiovascular events (AUROC = 0.79, 95% CI of 0.74 to 0.84, versus 0.65 for a model derived using clinical variables) and left ventricular ejection fraction (mean absolute error 7.3% versus 8.8% for a previous model), both achieved using coronary angiography alone. In a blinded review of 365 evaluations across 288 angiograms, its reports were clinically usable in 76% of evaluations versus 88% for cardiologists, with comparable false positives (17% versus 14%, P = 0.38); residual missed stenoses reflected an adjustable threshold rather than an absent signal.
title: A multiview video-text model detects obstructive coronary stenosis and predicts 1-year cardiovascular events from angiography.

abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a well-established risk factor in acute myocardial infarction (AMI); however, the clinical relevance of admission estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)-based categories remains unclear. We analyzed 10,870 patients from a prospective multicenter AMI registry in Japan. Patients were stratified into stages 1 (≥ 90), 2 (60-89), 3a (45-59), 3b (30-44), 4 (15-29), and 5 (< 15 mL/min/1.73 m2) based on the admission eGFR. The primary endpoint was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke. Bleeding was defined as BARC type 3 or 5. More advanced admission eGFR stages were associated with a higher risk of adverse events. After multivariable adjustment, stages 4 and 5 were associated with a significantly higher risk of MACE compared with the reference group of stages 1 and 2 (stage 4: HR 2.12, 95% CI 1.03-4.33; stage 5: HR 4.14, 95% CI 1.54-11.09), whereas stages 3a and 3b were not significantly associated with MACE. In patients with AMI, clinical outcomes varied across admission eGFR categories, with more advanced renal dysfunction, particularly stages 4 and 5, associated with a higher risk of short-term MACE. Detailed categorization of admission eGFR may provide additional prognostic information for early risk assessment.
title: Clinical impact of admission estimated glomerular filtration rate categories in patients with acute myocardial infarction.

abstract: Krishnan and colleagues report that 91% of STEMI patients at a large Indian tertiary centre received primary PCI within the 90-minute door-to-balloon (D2B) target, a meaningful achievement in contemporary STEMI care. Their analysis of the 9% who missed the target is equally valuable: delays distributed almost evenly across three categories, delayed informed consent, hemodynamic instability, and diagnostic ambiguity. We argue these categories are not interchangeable quality-improvement targets. They are mechanistically distinct problems requiring different solutions. We propose a conceptual, hypothesis-generating framework rather than a validated taxonomy. Future STEMI quality improvement efforts should categorize residual delays by domain rather than reporting them in aggregate, and should match interventions to the specific mechanism of delay.
title: Three doors, three locks: a domain-specific framework for the residual door-to-balloon gap in STEMI care : Matters Arising, commentary on Krishnan et al., Int J Emerg Med 2026;19:113.

abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a heterogeneous syndrome associated with persistently high mortality despite advances in temporary mechanical circulatory support. One recent randomized controlled trial suggested a mortality benefit of a percutaneous microaxial flow pump in a cohort of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by CS, whereas routine veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in populations with acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS has not improved survival and is associated with higher complication rates. These findings underscore the importance of phenotype-driven patient selection, incorporating the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) and Shock Academic Research Consortium (SHARC) classifications to guide device selection, timing, escalation, and de-escalation. This clinical consensus statement from the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) and the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC) of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) updates the 2020 expert consensus document and provides updated practical guidance based on the recent evidence on the use of temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS. Emphasis is placed on patient/device selection according to recent evidence, multidisciplinary shock teams, regionalized hub-and-spoke systems, structured protocols for escalation and futility, and the integration of contemporary trial data and best practices to optimize outcomes in this high-risk population.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical consensus statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus built on a small number of randomised trials in a heterogeneous syndrome.
appraisal.one_line: EAPCI and ACVC clinical consensus statement updating the 2020 document on temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets contemporary guidance on device selection, escalation, de-escalation and shock team systems after recent microaxial pump and VA-ECMO trials.

title: Temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across an expanding risk spectrum. As indications extend to younger and lower-risk patients, post-treatment complications with implications for survival, quality of life, and valve durability require attention.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review discusses major post-TAVI complications with direct implications for procedural planning and lifetime management, including cerebrovascular events, conduction abnormalities, coronary obstruction and aortic root injury, bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, valve thrombosis, residual regurgitation, and TAVI-associated infective endocarditis. Evidence was reviewed from pivotal randomized trials, contemporary registries, consensus documents, systematic reviews, and mechanistic studies addressing incidence, pathophysiology, predictors, prognosis, prevention, diagnosis, and management of these complications.
EXPERT OPINION: Post-TAVI risk reduction should move beyond reactive complication management toward individualized prevention. Meticulous computed tomography-based planning, optimized valve selection and implantation technique, rational antithrombotic therapy, structured rhythm and valve surveillance, selective use of cerebral embolic protection, timely correction of clinically or hemodynamically significant residual regurgitation, and infection-prevention pathways are central components of contemporary care. Future progress will depend on better risk stratification, longer-term durability data, and targeted preventive strategies adapted to lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy.
title: Post-treatment risks of transcatheter aortic valve implantation: should we be increasing preventative measures?

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting approximately 197 million people and causing over 9 million deaths annually. Although percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves survival, medication non-adherence affects more than one-quarter of patients after myocardial infarction. Validated instruments assessing multidimensional adherence barriers in post-PCI patients remain limited. This study developed and validated the Post-PCI Barrier Scale for Adherence to Prescribed Medication Regimens (PCI-BSAR).
METHODS: A methodological cross-sectional study was conducted in a tertiary care cardiology outpatient department. Questionnaire items were generated through literature review, patient interviews, and the WHO multidimensional adherence framework. Content validity, pilot testing (n = 50), exploratory factor analysis, reliability testing, and measurement model assessment were performed in 253 post-PCI patients.
RESULTS: The final 23-item PCI-BSAR demonstrated excellent content validity (S-CVI/Ave = 0.92). Exploratory factor analysis identified four domains: patient- and clinical-related, treatment and healthcare interaction-related, socioeconomic, and healthcare access and system-related barriers, explaining 69.6% of the variance. The questionnaire showed high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.909), composite reliability (0.848-0.938), AVE >0.50, and HTMT <0.85.
CONCLUSION: PCI-BSAR is a reliable and valid instrument for identifying multidimensional medication adherence barriers in post-PCI patients and may support individualized adherence assessment during routine outpatient follow-up.
title: Development and psychometric validation of a barrier assessment tool for adherence to prescribed medication regimens in post-PCI patients.

abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the 12-month clinical outcomes of short-term versus extended dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) in diabetic patients following drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation.
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort study, 536 diabetic patients undergoing DES implantation were categorized into short-term (< 6 months, n = 312) or extended (≥ 6 months, n = 224) DAPT groups based on actual treatment duration. Primary endpoints were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and target vessel revascularization) and BARC type 2, 3, or 5 bleeding events at 12 months.
RESULTS: Extended DAPT significantly reduced the incidence of MACE compared to short-term therapy (7.8% vs. 10.5%; HR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.53-0.98, p = 0.033), primarily driven by lower rates of target vessel revascularization (3.1% vs. 5.1%; p = 0.030). While overall bleeding rates did not differ significantly between groups (8.1% vs. 6.2%; p = 0.192), extended DAPT was associated with a significantly higher risk of recurrent bleeding in patients with a prior bleeding history (HR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.20-3.60, p = 0.011).
CONCLUSION: Extended DAPT effectively mitigates ischemic risks in diabetic patients following stent implantation without significantly increasing overall clinically significant bleeding. However, clinicians should prioritize individualized DAPT durations, specifically avoiding extended regimens in patients with a history of bleeding to minimize the risk of hemorrhage recurrence.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: The Impact of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy on Bleeding and Thrombotic Risks in Diabetic Patients Following Coronary Stent Implantation: A Prospective Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transaxillary (TAxA) approach has been developed as a simplified direct-vision minimally invasive access for heart valve surgery. We report a large single-center cohort of patients undergoing TAxA minimally invasive mitral valve surgery and evaluate early safety, procedural efficacy, recovery and mid-term outcomes.
METHODS: Consecutive patients who underwent TAxA mitral valve surgery at the University Hospital of Marche, Ancona, Italy, between January 2017 and April 2026 were included. Mitral repair or replacement procedures were considered with or without concomitant tricuspid valve repair, atrial fibrillation ablation or left atrial appendage occlusion. Early outcomes were analyzed in the overall cohort. Mid-term survival and reoperation were assessed in patients undergoing repair for degenerative mitral regurgitation.
RESULTS: The study included 763 patients. Mitral valve repair was performed in 640 patients and replacement in 123. The repair rate was 89% in patients with mitral regurgitation and 92% in patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation. Concomitant tricuspid repair, atrial fibrillation ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion were performed in 17%, 5% and 10% of patients, respectively. Mean cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were 103 and 63 minutes. Thirty-day mortality was 0.4%, stroke or transient ischemic attack occurred in 0.7%, and conversion to sternotomy was required in 0.7%; no conversion was due to poor exposure. Median ventilation time was 2 [interquartile range (IQR), 0-6] hours, 54% of patients were extubated in theatre and 80% were extubated within 6 hours. Median intensive care unit and hospital stays were 24 (IQR, 22-48) hours and 7 (IQR, 6-9) days. In the degenerative repair cohort, Kaplan-Meier survival was 97.0% at 5 years, and cumulative incidence of reoperation was 4.3% at 5 years.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large contemporary experience, TAxA minimally invasive mitral valve surgery was associated with low early mortality and morbidity, reasonable operative times, frequent ultra fast-track extubation, and satisfactory mid-term results.
title: Transaxillary minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: early and mid-term outcomes in 763 patients.
Transaxillary triple valve surgery and left atrium appendage occlusion.
Combined transfemoral TAVI and direct-vision valve-in-MAC through the transaxillary approach.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transaxillary (TxA) approach for minimally invasive aortic valve replacement (MICS-AVR) is a sternum-sparing technique that combines surgical valve replacement with virtually no visible scarring. We report institutional outcomes of the first 1,848 consecutive TxA MICS-AVR procedures.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included all consecutive patients undergoing isolated TxA MICS-AVR between January 2019 and June 2026. Patients with active endocarditis, redo surgery, or concomitant procedures were excluded. Primary endpoints were 30-day mortality and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression explored associations with adverse outcomes.
RESULTS: Mean age was 67.7±8.1 years, Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Operative Mortality (STS-PROM) 1.39%±2.90%, and European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II) 1.65%±1.12%. TxA use among surgical treatments for isolated aortic valve disease rose from 18.8% in 2019 to 99.2% in 2025. Mean operative, cardiopulmonary bypass, and cross-clamp times were 132±34, 69±23, and 43±16 minutes. No intraoperative death occurred; 1.6% required conversion to sternotomy. Thirty-day mortality was 0.5%, and MACCE occurred in 1.6%, including stroke in 0.9% and myocardial infarction in 0.5%. In multivariable analysis, mortality associations were strongest for insulin-treated diabetes [odds ratio (OR) 8.56], left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <40% (OR 8.45), and intraoperative transfusion (OR 17.86); corresponding MACCE associations included insulin-treated diabetes (OR 3.06), coronary artery disease (OR 2.46), peripheral arterial disease (OR 3.23), sternotomy conversion (OR 5.33), and transfusion (OR 5.49). These outcomes accompanied rapid institutional adoption of the technique, while operative efficiency remained favorable and the need for sternotomy conversion stayed low throughout the cohort. Given only 10 deaths and 30 MACCEs, multivariable findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.
CONCLUSIONS: Across 1,848 consecutive procedures, TxA MICS-AVR showed excellent reproducibility and safety. As long-term evidence increasingly supports surgical valve replacement in patients with extended life expectancy, TxA uniquely combines durable surgery with a cosmetic result comparable to transcatheter therapy, offering a scalable and strategically relevant platform for contemporary aortic valve care.
title: Surgery that looks like transcatheter aortic valve implantation: the transaxillary concept for minimally invasive aortic valve replacement in 1,848 consecutive patients.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary no-reflow after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) reflects failure of myocardial reperfusion despite treatment of the culprit epicardial lesion. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and immunothrombosis provide a plausible link between sterile inflammation, thrombus biology, and microvascular obstruction. We evaluated whether a clinically measurable NET-associated immunothrombotic phenotype (NET-IP) was associated with no-reflow and myocardial injury after primary PCI.
METHODS: This single-center translational cohort included 742 patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary PCI. NET-IP was calculated in 725 patients from five admission or pre-PCI variables-neutrophil count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and platelet-neutrophil product-by averaging log-transformed component z scores when at least four components were available, followed by standardization of the composite score. The primary endpoint was angiographic no-reflow, defined as final thrombolysis in myocardial infarction flow grade < 3 in the absence of mechanical epicardial obstruction. A case-enriched nested enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) biomarker subcohort was used to measure MPO-DNA, citrullinated histone H3 (H3Cit), and double-stranded DNA.
RESULTS: Angiographic no-reflow occurred in 110 of 742 patients. NET-IP was calculable in 725 patients, and the fully adjusted complete-case models included 700 patients. Patients with no-reflow had higher admission NET-IP scores than those with normal reflow (0.73 [0.24, 1.25] vs. -0.06 [-0.77, 0.54]; P < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, NET-IP remained associated with angiographic no-reflow (OR per SD, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.46-2.62; P < 0.001) and tissue-level reperfusion failure (OR per SD, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.32-2.02; P < 0.001). In the case-enriched ELISA subcohort, adjusted associations with no-reflow were observed for MPO-DNA (OR per SD log2, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.26-2.81; P = 0.002) and H3Cit (OR per SD log2, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.33-3.02; P < 0.001), whereas double-stranded DNA was weaker after adjustment (P = 0.074). NET-IP was also associated with higher peak high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I, higher peak creatine kinase-MB, lower discharge left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), large myocardial injury, and discharge LVEF < 50%.
CONCLUSION: A NET-IP was linked to impaired coronary reperfusion and myocardial injury after primary PCI in STEMI. The findings support NET-associated immunothrombosis as a clinically measurable immune phenotype but do not establish direct NET burden, causal mediation, or immediate clinical treatment guidance.
title: A NET-associated immunothrombotic phenotype is associated with coronary no-reflow and myocardial injury after primary PCI in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a real-world translational cohort.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: While injectable GLP-1 receptor agonists like semaglutide have demonstrated clear cardiovascular benefits in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), the role of oral incretin-based therapies, including oral semaglutide and DPP-4 inhibitors-remains less well defined. Comprehensive evaluation of their cardiovascular efficacy is warranted.
RESEARCH QUESTION: What are the cardiovascular outcomes associated with oral incretin-based therapies, specifically oral semaglutide and DPP-4 inhibitors, in patients with T2DM compared to placebo or standard care.
METHODS: We searched electronic databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Meta-analysis was conducted in R version 4.4.3 using the "meta" and "metasens" packages. Statistical analysis was performed using R software and RStudio (version 4.4.2). We calculated pooled estimates using risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 9 studies comprising 67,679 patients were included, of which two evaluated oral semaglutide and the remaining seven assessed DPP-4 inhibitors. There was no significant reduction in all-cause mortality (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.90-1.04, p = 0.35) or cardiovascular death (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91-1.05, p = 0.48). Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) showed a non-significant reduction overall (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-1.00, p = 0.06), with oral semaglutide demonstrating a significant benefit (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.78-0.95, p = 0.003). Non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI) (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.88-1.09) and non-fatal stroke (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.83-1.03) were not significantly affected. Hospitalizations due to heart failure (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.84-1.13) and unstable angina (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.15) remained unchanged. Coronary revascularization was slightly reduced with oral semaglutide (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.91). Adverse events leading to discontinuation were higher with oral semaglutide (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.15-1.98), while serious adverse events were significantly reduced (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.99, p = 0.003). Sensitivity analyses were conducted due to significant heterogeneity in key outcomes. While omitting certain studies reduced heterogeneity, the overall results remained consistent.
CONCLUSION: Oral incretin-based therapies were not associated with significant reductions in all-cause mortality, cardiovascular death, or MACE overall, though oral semaglutide showed a significant MACE benefit and reduced coronary revascularization on subgroup analysis. Non-fatal MI, fatal or non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, fatal or non-fatal stroke and hospitalization due to heart failure or unstable angina were unaffected, and oral semaglutide carried a higher risk of treatment discontinuation. These findings suggest no clear class-wide cardiovascular benefit of oral incretins, with signals specific to oral semaglutide warranting confirmation in dedicated trials.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251113835.
title: Cardiovascular outcomes of oral incretin-based drugs in type 2 diabetes: a GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of 67,679 patients.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radial artery dimensions before and after intra-arterial vasodilator administration remain incompletely characterized along the vessel. This study used optical coherence tomography (OCT) to assess paired changes in mean lumen diameter.
METHODS: Twelve patients underwent baseline OCT 5 min after limited sheath insertion and post-administration OCT after intra-arterial nitroglycerin and verapamil, before coronary angiography. The full OCT-imaged radial artery span was divided into equal proximal, middle, and distal thirds before selecting anatomically matched analyzable portions. Analysis included 1,482 matched cross-sectional pairs (2,964 frames), with a cumulative matched analyzable length of 1,404.4 mm. Measurements at matched 1-mm intervals were aggregated within patients. Mean lumen diameter was the representative lumen metric; area and volume were supportive measurements.
RESULTS: Mean lumen diameter increased from 3.06 ± 0.49 to 3.35 ± 0.56 mm (mean paired change, 0.29 mm; 95% CI, 0.20-0.39; P < 0.001). The mean patient-level relative increase was 9.6%. Mean increases were observed in all three thirds in exploratory analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Mean radial artery lumen diameter was greater after intra-arterial nitroglycerin and verapamil than at baseline.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/hvshowproject.html?id=270,922&v=1.1, Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) ChiCTR2500097574.
title: Radial artery characteristics before and after intra-arterial administration of nitroglycerin and verapamil: an optical coherence tomography study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) radiomics may complement coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-based anatomical and physiological assessment. This study aimed to evaluate its incremental diagnostic value for identifying hemodynamically significant coronary stenosis.
METHODS: This retrospective study screened 21,438 consecutive patients and included 81 patients with 107 target vessels who underwent CCTA, invasive coronary angiography, and invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR) measurement within 30 days. Patients were allocated at the patient level to training and validation cohorts in a 7:3 ratio. A radiomics score (Radscore) was developed from lesion-specific PCAT features using training-only preprocessing and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression. Models incorporating diameter stenosis (DS), CCTA-derived FFR (CT-FFR), fat attenuation index (FAI), and Radscore were evaluated against invasive FFR ≤0.80 using patient-cluster bootstrap inference.
RESULTS: The training and validation cohorts comprised 57 and 24 patients with 75 and 32 vessels, respectively, without patient overlap. In validation, Radscore alone had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.684 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.451-0.873). CT-FFR+ Radscore showed higher discrimination than CT-FFR alone (AUC, 0.879 vs. 0.762; difference, 0.117; 95% CI, 0.005-0.229; P = 0.041), as did DS+ Radscore vs. DS alone (AUC, 0.812 vs. 0.619; difference, 0.193; 95% CI, 0.018-0.367; P = 0.030). The FAI comparison was not significant (P = 0.238). At training-derived cutoffs, CT-FFR+ Radscore had lower sensitivity (50.0% vs. 78.6%) and negative predictive value (69.6% vs. 81.3%) but higher specificity (88.9% vs. 72.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: Adding Radscore was associated with higher discrimination for CT-FFR and DS in internal validation but did not uniformly improve threshold-dependent classification. Independent external validation is warranted.
title: Incremental diagnostic value of coronary CT angiography-derived pericoronary adipose tissue radiomics for identifying hemodynamically significant coronary stenosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are among the most frequently prescribed medications and are generally considered to have a favourable safety profile. Nevertheless, immediate hypersensitivity reactions may occur and, in exceptional circumstances, can precipitate Kounis syndrome (KS), an acute coronary syndrome resulting from the activation of inflammatory pathways. We describe an elderly patient who developed severe anaphylaxis with Type I KS shortly after intravenous pantoprazole administration in the presence of an unsuspected myocardial bridge, and discuss the potential clinical implications.
CASE SUMMARY: An 85-year-old woman with a 30-year history of well-controlled bronchial asthma was admitted with community-acquired pneumonia. During hospitalization, she received intravenous pantoprazole (40 mg) for acid reflux. Within five minutes of the infusion, she developed a widespread erythematous rash, severe bronchospasm, profound hypotension (74/56 mmHg), and ST-segment elevation of approximately 0.3 mV in leads I, aVL, and V₁ to V₄. Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated no obstructive coronary artery disease but identified a myocardial bridge involving the mid-left anterior descending artery, producing nearly 90% systolic compression. Serial cardiac troponin and NT-proBNP concentrations remained within the normal range. Assessment using the Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale yielded a score of six, indicating a probable causal relationship between pantoprazole and the adverse event. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone (80 mg). The recovery occurred within 2 h.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights that intravenous pantoprazole may rarely trigger life-threatening Type I Kounis syndrome. It also raises the possibility that a pre-existing myocardial bridge can accentuate coronary vasospasm during severe allergic reactions, thereby contributing to the clinical presentation. Based on this experience and the available literature, we propose a practical management algorithm to facilitate timely diagnosis and treatment in similar clinical settings.
title: Pantoprazole-induced anaphylactic asthma and Type I Kounis syndrome: a case report and literature review.
Augmented temporary mechanical support in cardiogenic shock: do improved hemodynamics translate to recovery?

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) combined with left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has long been used in the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is now increasingly adopted due to its great precision and improved safety profile. This report presents a rare case of PFA performed for persistent AF and atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT), along with LAAC, under non-intubated general anesthesia.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 36-year-old male patient presented with a 10-year history of recurrent chest tightness and palpitations, which had worsened during the week prior to admission. He was diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy and AF 4 months ago and had a previous cerebral infarction, with a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 3 and a HAS-BLED score of 1. A one-stop procedure combining PFA and LAAC was planned. During ablation at the roof of the right superior pulmonary vein, AF converted to sinus rhythm and subsequently developed spontaneous tachycardia, suspected to be AVRT due to a left-sided accessory pathway near CS1-2. Therefore, ablation of the accessory pathway and mitral isthmus was performed, and atrioventricular separation and mitral isthmus block were confirmed. A total of 78 discharges were delivered throughout the procedure, and repeated high-frequency atrial stimulation did not induce atrial flutter or AF. LAAC was then completed as planned. Electrocardiogram (ECG) showed sinus rhythm, and echocardiography demonstrated improved cardiac remodeling at 3-month follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: AVRT is a type of supraventricular tachycardia caused by the presence of an accessory pathway due to congenital structural abnormalities. Our case reports an AVRT occurrence during PFA for AF and provides significant evidence that PFA is effective and safe for accessory pathway ablation during AF ablation.
title: Pulsed field ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation with atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia under tubeless general anesthesia: a case report.

abstract: Mechanical circulatory support devices (MCSDs) have evolved from rescue therapy for refractory cardiogenic shock (CS) to an essential component of advanced heart failure management, spanning temporary support, bridge strategies, durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD), and total artificial heart (TAH). This structured narrative review summarizes the historical evolution, current indications, device classification, major short-term and long-term platforms, adverse events, and future directions of MCSDs. Literature was selected in a structured narrative manner with emphasis on contemporary guidelines, randomized or comparative studies, major registries, and representative Chinese experience. Available evidence shows that MCSDs can improve hemodynamics and, in selected populations, survival and quality of life; however, these benefits must be balanced against bleeding, stroke, infection, right heart failure, device malfunction, cost, and major ethical and access constraints. Current practice thus necessitates careful patient selection, stage-based therapeutic escalation, and rigorous evaluation of mixed evidence pertaining to temporary MCSDs, LVAD and TAH, instead of merely describing individual devices.
title: Mechanical circulatory support devices in heart failure: a narrative review of current evidence, clinical applications, complications, and future directions.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Penetrating cardiac injuries from firearms are highly lethal, with the majority of victims dying at the scene from exsanguination. A minority of patients who reach hospital alive harbor a retained intracardiac or pericardial projectile, posing a clinical dilemma: while extraction has historically been favored to prevent migration, embolization, infective endocarditis, conduction abnormalities, and lead toxicity, contemporary evidence supports selective conservative management in hemodynamically stable patients without active hemorrhage, structural cardiac injury, or arrhythmia. Bullets retained within the atrioventricular (AV) groove are particularly hazardous to extract because of adjacent coronary arteries and conduction tissue, and reports of conservatively managed AV-groove projectiles are rare. This case adds to the limited literature describing successful non-operative management of a retained AV-groove bullet.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 25-year-old previously healthy man sustained a single gunshot wound to the right chest and remained hemodynamically stable throughout inter-hospital transfer. Imaging suggested a projectile near the right atrium, but localization was limited by metal artifact. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated mild apical pericardial effusion with preserved biventricular function and no valvular injury. Right video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) with pleuro-pericardial window drained 100 mL of serosanguineous fluid but did not identify the projectile. Conversion to median sternotomy revealed a bullet within the right AV groove without active hemorrhage. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated normal biventricular function with no regional wall motion abnormality and no tricuspid regurgitation. Following multidisciplinary discussion, the family elected to forgo extraction. The pericardium was closed and chest drains placed. Postoperative echocardiography, electrocardiography, and serial serum lead levels remained within normal limits. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 7 and remained well at 6-month follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Conservative management of a retained bullet within the AV groove is a reasonable option in hemodynamically stable patients with intact cardiac function, no active bleeding, and no evidence of mechanical or electrical compromise. Avoidance of extraction in this anatomically sensitive region minimizes procedural risk to the right coronary artery and conduction tissue, but mandates structured long-term surveillance for migration, infection, conduction abnormalities, and lead toxicity.
title: Conservative management of a retained bullet in the right atrioventricular groove following a penetrating thoracic gunshot wound: a case report.

abstract: Dozens of agents that limit reperfusion injury preclinically have failed clinically. These failures are architectural, not biological: the right biology reaches the wrong place, as the wrong molecule, at the wrong time, judged by the wrong end point. We recast each as a design constraint and specify a staged regimen anchored at first medical contact.
title: Cardioprotection Is a Delivery Problem: A First-Medical-Contact Framework for Acute Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare outcomes of coronary revascularization with coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) or complex or multivessel percutaneous coronary intervention (MV PCI) in patients with dementia.
METHODS: We compared outcomes of Medicare fee-for-service (FFS) beneficiaries 66 years or older with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) or MV PCI from January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2019. The primary clinical outcome was 1-year mortality, and secondary clinical outcomes were inpatient and 90-day complications and 90-day readmissions. Patient-centered outcomes were time-at-home ratio and discharge to higher level of care.
RESULTS: 8,939 patients with ADRD undergoing revascularization with CABG MV PCI met study criteria. Of these, 3,510 (39.3%) underwent CABG and 5,429 (60.7%) underwent MV PCI. Patients with ADRD who underwent MV PCI were more likely to be older (81.0 vs. 76.7, P < 0.001), women (44.1% vs. 29.4%, P < 0.001), frail (82.4% vs. 75.0%, P < 0.001), and have moderate to severe dementia (64.4% vs. 54.6%, P < 0.001). One-year mortality was higher among patients undergoing MV PCI (OR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.8-2.3) but inpatient and 90-day major complications were lower (OR = 0.3, 95% CI: 0.3-0.3 and OR = 0.5, 95% CI: 0.4-0.5, respectively). Patients with ADRD undergoing MV PCI were less likely to be discharged to a higher level of care (OR = 0.2, 95% CI: 0.2-0.2) and had higher time-at-home ratios (Mean Difference 4.2, 95% CI: 2.4-6.0).
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with ADRD undergoing MV PCI demonstrate higher 1-year mortality but lower short-term complications. Patient-centered outcomes of time-at-home ratio and risk for discharge to a higher level of care were more favorable with MV PCI compared to CABG. These data should be used by patients, their families, and physicians to facilitate goal-concordant care especially when optimization of patient-centered outcomes is desired.
title: Complex or multivessel PCI is associated with higher 1-year mortality but better patient-centered outcomes when compared to CABG in patients with dementia.

abstract: Pulmonary tumor thrombotic microangiopathy (PTTM) is a rare cause of acute cor pulmonale, typically associated with advanced solid tumors; its occurrence as the initial presentation of multiple myeloma (MM) has not been described. A 45-year-old woman developed acute right heart failure on postoperative day 1 after uterine myomectomy. Echocardiography showed a pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 86 mmHg with a d-shaped left ventricle and right ventricular dysfunction (TAPSE 10 mm); CTPA excluded pulmonary embolism but revealed bilateral ground-glass opacities. Platelet count fell from 115 × 109/L preoperatively to 30 × 109/L. An overlooked preoperative globulin of 67 g/L prompted serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation, which identified an IgG κ M-protein; bone marrow aspiration revealed 14% morphologically abnormal plasma cells. Presumed MM-associated PTTM was treated with heparin and sildenafil. The platelet count recovered, and a follow-up echocardiogram on day 7 showed normalized cardiac structure and function. The patient self-discontinued rivaroxaban 1 week after discharge and died 3 months later from progression of untreated MM. In CTPA-negative acute cor pulmonale with unexplained thrombocytopenia, an elevated globulin on routine biochemistry may be the only early clue to a plasma cell disorder, and timely anticoagulation with pulmonary vasodilation may buy time for definitive therapy.
first_author_country: Department of Critical Care Medicine Liangxiang Hospital Beijing China
last_author_country: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College Beijing China
title: Acute Cor Pulmonale Caused by Pulmonary Tumor Thrombotic Microangiopathy as the Initial Presentation of Multiple Myeloma: A Case Report.

abstract: Acute myocarditis is a rare but potentially life-threatening inflammatory disease that may mimic acute myocardial infarction, particularly in septic patients where myocardial injury may have other causes. We report the case of a 46-year-old man with sepsis secondary to a massive perianal abscess who underwent emergency surgical drainage under general anesthesia. Postoperatively, persistent respiratory deterioration and elevated cardiac biomarkers prompted further cardiac evaluation. Echocardiography showed newly reduced left ventricular (LV) systolic function, with an ejection fraction (EF) of 35%, and moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (MR). Although acute myocardial infarction was initially suspected, coronary angiography showed non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), with only a 40% right coronary artery stenosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) demonstrated elevated T2 values and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of the interventricular septum, with additional enhancement of the LV lateral wall, consistent with myocardial edema and inflammation and supportive of acute myocarditis. The patient received source control, broad-spectrum antibiotics, intravenous diuretics, norepinephrine and dobutamine, oxygen therapy, and heart failure-directed therapy. EF improved to 45% at 10 days, with complete recovery of cardiac function and resolution of MR at the 3-month follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of acute myocarditis in septic surgical patients and suggests that early multidisciplinary assessment, coronary evaluation, and CMR may help clarify the diagnosis and guide management.
keywords: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries
title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Supported Diagnosis of Acute Myocarditis Mimicking Acute Coronary Syndrome in a Patient With Sepsis Due to a Massive Perianal Abscess.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The influence of sleep duration on vulnerable coronary plaques, as evaluated via optical coherence tomography (OCT), has not been clearly defined in coronary artery disease (CAD). Here, the relationships between habitual sleep duration and thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA) detected by OCT were investigated in individuals with CAD. We further investigated whether systemic inflammation, represented by the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), represents a mediator of this association.
METHODS: Overall, 1,178 patients with angiographically confirmed CAD who underwent OCT imaging and completed standardized sleep questionnaires were enrolled. Participants were categorized according to reported sleep duration. Multivariable logistic regression modeling was employed to assess the link between sleep duration and TCFA. Linear regression analyses assessed the association between sleep duration and NLR. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) modeling was applied as a means of detecting possible nonlinear associations between NLR and TCFA. Mediation analyses were then conducted to determine whether NLR functioned as an intermediate variable linking sleep duration and plaque vulnerability.
RESULTS: These results offer the first clinical evidence of the link between sleep duration and TCFA presence in individuals with CAD, with the TCFA risk in the abnormal sleep duration group being 2.16 times that of the normal group (95% CI: 1.63-2.88, P < 0.001). Sleep duration was also independently correlated with NLR, and RCS analysis highlighted a nonlinear relationship between NLR levels and TCFA risk (P < 0.001). Importantly, mediation analysis demonstrated that NLR partially mediated the effect of sleep duration on TCFA, supporting the existence of a sleep-inflammation-plaque vulnerability axis.
CONCLUSION: The sleep duration has been shown to be significantly associated with the risk of developing TCFA. In addition, a partial mediating effect of NLR on this relationship has been found.
title: Sleep-inflammation-coronary plaque phenotype axis: clinical validation and inflammation-mediated mechanisms based on optical coherence tomography.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Little is known about the current scenario of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) under primary angioplasty; Transferred by emergency medical services and self-referred patients in Iran.
METHODS: The study population consisted of AMI patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who were consecutively admitted with Emergency Medical Services (EMS) or directly in the first six months of 2021 in 2 PCI-capable selected hospitals in Tehran. We analyzed the pattern of transfer by emergency medical services and compared in-hospital treatments and outcomes between transferred patients and self-referred patients in Tehran. Statistical comparisons were performed using chi‑square, t‑tests, or Mann-Whitney U tests, and multivariable logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with in‑hospital mortality, with significance set at P<0.05.
RESULTS: In-hospital mortality was higher in the self-referred than in patients transferred by EMS (9.8% versus 5.2%) (P=0.014). The average door-to-balloon (DTB) time in the self-referred patients was significantly higher (60.26±59.0 minutes vs 49.30±48.82 minutes) (P=0.020). Results show that the average DTB time of patients who died in the hospital was higher than that of patients who were alive in the self-referred patients. The average time from pain onset to Balloon (OTB) in the self-referred patients and those transferred by EMS was 348.74±316.07 minutes and 226.26±183.15 minutes, respectively (P<0.001). Multivariable logistic regression models the chance of in-hospital mortality in patients who self-referred is 2.17 times that of patients who were transferred by EMS, which is statistically significant (P=0.008).
CONCLUSION: Our results indicated that there are significant differences in treatment delay and use of early revascularization, such as time of first medical contact (FMC) to the device, time of pain onset to Balloon (OTB), and DTB time between transferred-by-EMS patients and self-referred patients.
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
title: Evaluation of Effective Factors in the Prognosis of Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction Transferred by Emergency Medical Services and Self-Referred Patients in Tehran.

abstract: Aortic root thrombosis (ART) is a rare but serious complication of continuous-flow left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support that can result in coronary artery occlusion. We present a 66-year-old man with a HeartMate 3 LVAD who presented with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Urgent coronary angiography revealed an aortic root thrombus with complete ostial right coronary artery (RCA) occlusion. He underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement. His course was complicated by ventricular fibrillation and right ventricular shock, followed by clinical recovery. This case highlights ART as an uncommon cause of acute myocardial infarction in LVAD-supported patients and emphasizes the importance of prompt recognition and management of ischemic complications in this population.
title: ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Secondary to Aortic Root Thrombosis in a Patient With a Left Ventricular Assist Device.

abstract: Anterior leaflet prolapse remains a challenging lesion in mitral valve repair, particularly in the presence of asymmetric degenerative disease. We present the case of a 59-year-old patient with severe mitral regurgitation due to asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse in the setting of Barlow's disease, treated through a totally endoscopic right minithoracotomy. Intraoperative valve analysis demonstrated prolapse of the A2M2 and A3 segments with elongated secondary chordae. Mitral valve repair was performed using secondary chordae transfer, followed by asymmetric edge-to-edge repair at the A2-P2 scallops and ring annuloplasty. Intraoperative assessment showed satisfactory leaflet coaptation with trivial residual regurgitation. Postoperative echocardiography confirmed the absence of residual mitral regurgitation and no evidence of clinically significant mitral stenosis. This report describes the technical aspects of endoscopic secondary chordae transfer combined with asymmetric edge-to-edge repair and ring annuloplasty for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse, demonstrating the feasibility of this repair strategy in a complex mitral valve anatomy.
journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
title: Endoscopic secondary chordae transfer and edge-to-edge repair for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse.

abstract: Severe aortic stenosis (AS) and chronic pressure overload may impair frequency-dependent myocardial reserve despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). We investigated whether acute afterload reduction with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) restores force-frequency relationships (FFR) and relaxation frequency relationships (RFR). In this prospective study, patients with severe normal-flow, high-gradient AS and preserved LVEF underwent invasive left ventricular pressure recording during incremental atrial pacing at 80 and 100 beats/min before and immediately after TAVI. Systolic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmax and preload-adjusted indices [dP/dtmax/left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) and left ventricular peak systolic pressure (LVSP)/LVEDP], whereas lusitropic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmin, the relaxation constant τ, and LVEDP. Echocardiography was performed at baseline and 3 mo. Forty-six patients completed the pacing protocol. Before TAVI, pacing produced only a modest increase in dP/dtmax (Δ + 150 mmHg/s; P = 0.004), without improvement in dP/dtmin (P = 0.329) or τ (P = 0.182). Immediately after TAVI, pacing increased dP/dtmax (P < 0.001), dP/dtmax/LVEDP (P = 0.004), and LVSP/LVEDP (P = 0.031), while improving dP/dtmin (Δ + 56 mmHg/s; P = 0.050) and τ (P = 0.033) and reducing LVEDP (P = 0.017). Correlation analyses supported the emergence of physiological FFR and RFR after valve implantation. At 3 mo, echocardiography showed lower pulmonary artery systolic pressure (P = 0.002), improved left atrial reservoir strain, and lower diastolic dysfunction grade (P = 0.006). Thus, acute afterload relief with TAVI reveals preserved dynamic systolic and lusitropic reserve in severe AS, with subsequent group-level improvement in diastolic function.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study provides direct invasive human evidence that frequency-dependent myocardial reserve is acutely restored after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis. Controlled atrial pacing revealed blunted force-frequency and relaxation-frequency responses before valve replacement, despite preserved ejection fraction, with rapid recovery after afterload relief. These findings show that impaired myocardial reserve in pressure-overload remodeling is functionally reversible and tightly linked to loading conditions.
journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal_abbrev: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
title: Restoration of frequency-dependent myocardial reserve after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis: an invasive hemodynamic study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiotoxic ingestions of calcium-channel blockers and beta-adrenergic antagonists are highly lethal, often causing refractory vasoplegic shock and noncardiogenic pulmonary edema. While venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a recognized rescue therapy for cardiogenic shock, the roles of venovenous ECMO and albumin dialysis-specifically the molecular adsorbent recirculating system (MARS)-as well as the effectiveness of linking patients to therapy through a coordinated referral process remain underexplored.
CASE SUMMARY: We describe five consecutive patients with severe cardiotoxic ingestions managed via a regionally triggered transfer pathway. Patients presented with profound hypotension and respiratory failure despite standard therapies. All five patients received MARS for drug clearance and vasoplegia management; two required venovenous ECMO for refractory hypoxemia. One patient died due to profound myocardial poisoning; four survived to discharge. Complications included continuous renal replacement therapy filter clotting and catheter-associated thrombosis.
CONCLUSIONS: A coordinated regional protocol enabling early access to ECMO and MARS is feasible in massive cardiotoxic ingestions.
title: Integrated Use of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation and Molecular Adsorbent Recirculating System for Refractory Cardiotoxic Ingestion: A Single-Center Case Series.

abstract: Sedation is essential in critically ill mechanically ventilated patients, yet conventional intravenous agents carry risks of accumulation, organ-dependent clearance, and adverse effects. Volatile anesthetics offer several pharmacokinetic advantages, but their adoption in the intensive care unit has historically been limited by technical constraints. This review offers an updated, clinically focused overview of volatile- based sedation in adult intensive care units, covering pharmacological mechanisms, delivery systems, clinical outcomes, safety, and practical application. This review was conducted through systematic searching of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2016 and December 2025. Sevoflurane and isoflurane achieve sedation primarily via γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor modulation and offer organ-independent clearance, rapid onset/offset, and real-time end-tidal monitoring. Modern delivery systems, including reflection devices (Sedaconda-ACD) and automated platforms (MIRUS), have improved intensive care unit feasibility. Clinical evidence suggests volatile sedation may reduce awakening times and duration of mechanical ventilation compared with intravenous agents; however, results across randomized trials and meta-analyses are heterogeneous. Potential benefits have been reported in acute respiratory distress syndrome, post-cardiac arrest care, neurocritical illness, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and refractory agitation, but robust evidence is lacking across all settings. Limitations include hemodynamic effects, increased circuit dead space, renal safety concerns with sevoflurane, infrastructure requirements, occupational exposure, environmental impact, and cost. Volatile sedation is a feasible and pharmacologically rational option for selected mechanically ventilated intensive care unit patients, particularly those requiring prolonged sedation or with organ dysfunction limiting conventional agents. Current evidence does not support universal superiority over intravenous sedation. Inhaled anesthetics should be incorporated into individualized, multimodal sedation strategies within structured institutional frameworks. Large multicenter trials are needed to clarify effects on mortality, long-term neurological outcomes, and quality of life.
title: Clinical application of volatile sedation in adult intensive care units: pharmacological mechanisms, delivery systems, and safety.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD.
METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year.
RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year.
CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

abstract: Acute heart failure (AHF) is among the most common causes of emergency department, intermediate care, and intensive care unit admission and remains associated with substantial early mortality despite advances in contemporary therapy. The first 120 min of management are particularly critical, as this period determines not only respiratory and hemodynamic stabilization, but also trigger identification, decongestion strategy, and the foundation for subsequent prognostic improvement. This CME article provides a practical, phenotype-based approach to the early management of AHF. The proposed strategy is centered on the rapid classification of patients according to congestion ("wet" vs. "dry") and perfusion ("warm" vs. "cold") status. Stabilization and diagnostic work-up must occur simultaneously. Early assessment should focus on identifying acute coronary syndrome, clinically relevant arrhythmias, hypertensive crisis, pulmonary embolism, structural heart disease, and infectious triggers. In addition to clinical examination, electrocardiography, blood gas analysis, and biomarkers, point-of-care ultrasound with lung ultrasound and focused echocardiography play a pivotal role in the first-line evaluation. From a therapeutic perspective, early noninvasive ventilation in cardiogenic pulmonary edema, prompt vasodilation in hypertensive presentations, and effective decongestion with intravenous loop diuretics constitute the core interventions. In cases of insufficient response, escalation strategies such as sequential nephron blockade or selective use of vasoactive agents should be considered. Structured reassessment at short intervals is essential to detect persistent congestion, evolving hypoperfusion, inadequate therapeutic response, or overlooked differential diagnoses. The article emphasizes that successful acute management must already establish the transition toward guideline-directed long-term therapy during the first hours of hospitalization, including early initiation of evidence-based heart failure medication once hemodynamic stabilization has been achieved.
title: [Acute heart failure-management during the first 120 min : Approach for early stabilization and decongestion].

abstract:
PURPOSE: Post-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) left bundle branch block (LBBB) is the most common post-TAVR cardiac conduction abnormality (CCA), particularly in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Prior computational studies evaluated generalized CCA risk but did not quantify LBBB-specific mechanical injury or compare self-expanding (SE) and balloon-expandable (BE) devices in BAV. This proof-of-concept study established a patient-specific computational framework to (1) quantify mechanical stretch in the left bundle branch (LBB)-adjacent region, (2) identify a preliminary, cohort-specific strain-based separation value associated with post-TAVR LBBB, and (3) compare device-related LBBB risk trends between SE and BE devices.
METHODS: Cardiac CT scans from six type I BAV TAVR patients were analyzed (two with LBBB and four without CCA). Patient-specific finite element models incorporated anatomy and leaflet calcification. The LBB region was defined using membranous septum length and anatomical landmarks. Simulations reproduced implantation of deployed SE devices and virtual BE devices at standardized depth. Area-weighted logarithmic strain (LE), contact pressure, oversizing index, eccentricity index, and expansion metrics were computed.
RESULTS: LBB-adjacent LE showed clear separation (0.15-0.24 in LBBB vs. 0.03-0.11 without CCA), with 0.11 as a preliminary cohort-specific separation value. Mean LE was higher with SE than BE devices (0.11 vs. 0.08). Contact pressure showed no consistent association with outcome, suggesting that LE differences reflect multiple contributing factors.
CONCLUSION: In this six-patient cohort, LBB-adjacent strain clearly separated LBBB from No-LBBB cases, whereas contact pressure showed no consistent relationship with outcome. Larger cohorts and sensitivity analyses are needed to establish its clinical utility for BAV TAVR risk stratification or device selection.
title: Strain-Based Assessment of Post-TAVR Left Bundle Branch Block in Bicuspid Aortic Valve Using Patient-Specific Computational Modeling.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Despite clinical benefits and guideline recommendations, uptake of exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CR) following coronary artery disease remains suboptimal, with barriers including transportation issues, travel distance, and geographic location. To overcome these barriers, decentralization strategies that move health care to local settings have been developed across several countries.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether CR uptake improved following decentralization, and whether geographic and social inequalities were reduced.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This register-based cohort study used data from 2013 to 2022, with data analysis performed from April to August 2025. This population-based study was conducted within 21 Danish municipalities. All participants were patients aged 30 years or older discharged alive after acute myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass grafting. Patients were identified in the Danish National Patient Register. Patients were excluded if they had a previous diagnosis or procedure or did not reside within the study area.
EXPOSURES: Travel distance from home to nearest CR facility and educational level.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Uptake (attending at least 1 training session within 180 days from discharge) was analyzed using modified Poisson regression to quantify differences in proportions before and after decentralization with adjustment for relevant covariates.
RESULTS: A total of 19 375 patients were eligible for the study, and 295 patients with missing information on exposures or covariates were excluded. Among the included 19 080 patients, 13 355 (70.0%) were male, and 10 868 (57.0%) were aged 60 to 79 years. The median (IQR) travel distance was reduced from 15.1 (5.9-25.7) km to 7.2 (2.8-14.8) km after decentralization, and uptake increased by 16% (risk ratio [RR], 1.16; 95% CI, 1.12-1.19). Among the 20% of patients with the longest travel distance, uptake increased by 45% (RR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.33-1.58), and geographic inequality was significantly reduced. Among patients with short education, uptake increased by 27% (RR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.20-1.35), and social inequality was significantly reduced.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of 19 080 patients, there was increased uptake of CR after decentralization to primary care, accompanied by significant reductions in geographic and social inequalities. The findings support decentralized delivery of CR as a feasible and equitable model, but ongoing monitoring of quality and safety remains essential.
title: Uptake and Inequalities in Exercise-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation After Decentralization.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Permanent pacemaker implantation is a common complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Leadless pacemakers (LPs) may reduce lead- and pocket-related complications, but their clinical outcomes after TAVR remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety and effectiveness of LPs compared with transvenous pacemakers (TVPs).
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Randomized and observational studies were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled proportions, risk ratios (RRs), and mean differences (MDs). Reconstructed Kaplan-Meier data were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: Ten studies involving 10,809 patients (1030 LP and 9779 TVP recipients) were included. The pooled procedural success rate of LP implantation was 98% (95% CI 95%-99%). Implantation success was comparable between LP and TVP (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.98-1.02). Sensitivity analysis demonstrated a shorter hospital stay with LP (MD -1.37 days, 95% CI -2.33 to -0.41) and a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.37, 95% CI 0.14-0.96). Overall survival did not differ between groups (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.44-1.23), although reconstructed survival curves showed late separation favoring LP. Device-related and vascular complications were comparable between LP and TVP.
CONCLUSIONS: LP implantation after TAVR demonstrates excellent procedural success and clinical outcomes comparable to TVPs. LPs may reduce hospital stay and heart failure hospitalization, supporting their use as an alternative pacing strategy in appropriately selected patients.
title: Leadless Pacemakers After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Meta-analysis With Time-to-Event Analysis.

abstract: Ebstein anomaly is a rare congenital malformation of the tricuspid valve and right ventricle characterized by marked heterogeneity in anatomy, physiology, and clinical presentation. This broad phenotypic spectrum strongly influences the natural history of the disease, the timing and type of intervention, and ultimately long-term outcomes. Patients range from critically ill neonates with severe hemodynamic compromise and circular shunts to asymptomatic children and adults with progressive tricuspid regurgitation, right ventricular dysfunction, or arrhythmias, as well as survivors of previous surgical interventions. Accordingly, long-term outcomes are best understood within the context of the presenting phenotype and its associated management pathway rather than as a single aggregate measure of survival. Contemporary management therefore requires phenotype-specific decision-making. This review summarizes long-term outcomes across the major clinical and therapeutic subgroups, including critically ill neonates managed with the Starnes procedure, stable neonates and infants undergoing biventricular repair, patients treated with historical repair techniques, contemporary cone reconstruction, and tricuspid valve replacement. Particular emphasis is placed on transplant-free survival, valve durability, ventricular remodeling, arrhythmia burden, functional status, quality of life, and the need for reintervention.
title: Beyond the label: Long-term outcomes after surgical management of Ebstein anomaly.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) on the electrocardiogram (ECG) can present as ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), non-STEMI, ST depression, or other patterns (eg, de Winter T waves and hyperacute T waves), posing a diagnostic challenge. Even experienced physicians may overlook OMI on ECG, leading to delays in catheterization laboratory activation. Recently, smartphone apps using AI have been shown to exhibit promising accuracy in ECG interpretation in large datasets.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of our study was to retrospectively compare the diagnostic performance of an AI-based application (PMCardio) with that of interventional cardiologists in interpreting nonpathognomonic ECGs that generated debates about diagnosis.
METHODS: In total, 33 ECGs that were diagnostically challenging upon patient admission to the emergency department were included. A group of 3 interventional cardiologists, blinded to the final diagnosis, independently assessed whether the ECG suggested OMI requiring immediate invasive coronary angiography. The diagnostic performance of the cardiologists was compared to that of the AI application, using the results of coronary angiography as the gold standard and considering any lesion with ≥90% stenosis as positive.
RESULTS: Of the 33 patients, 29 (88%) had a final diagnosis of cardiac origin for their chest pain, including 23 acute coronary syndromes, of which 13 (57%) were OMI. The 3 cardiologists achieved sensitivities of 62%, 85%, and 62%; negative predictive values (NPVs) of 74%, 83%, and 69%; specificities of 70%, 50%, and 55%; and positive predictive values (PPVs) of 57%, 52%, and 47%. Their overall misclassification rates were 33%, 36%, and 42%. In contrast, AI analysis demonstrated a sensitivity and NPV of 100%, a specificity of 60%, a PPV of 62%, and an overall misclassification rate of 24%.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study of challenging ECGs, an AI application demonstrated better diagnostic performance of OMI as compared to cardiologists. These findings highlight the potential of AI to enhance diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making.
title: Human vs Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Coronary Occlusions in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Retrospective Study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare characteristics and in-hospital outcomes of dialysis vs non-dialysis patients undergoing chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO PCI).
METHODS: The authors analyzed 18 572 patients undergoing CTO PCI between 2012 and 2026. Outcomes were compared using multivariable logistic regression and propensity score-matching weights. Mortality was evaluated by cumulative center-enrollment category.
RESULTS: Overall, 447 patients (2.4%) were receiving dialysis. Compared with non-dialysis patients, they more often had diabetes mellitus (70.5% vs 43.1%), hypertension (93.5% vs 87.1%), heart failure (52.7% vs 27.0%), cerebrovascular disease (17.9% vs 9.1%), peripheral arterial disease (29.1% vs 12.7%), and moderately or severely calcified CTOs (68.2% vs 47.0%; all P < .001). Technical success (85.2% vs 87.4%; P = .190) and procedural success (83.9% vs 86.2%, P = .192) were similar. Retrograde approach (31.1% vs 31.3%; P = .90) and antegrade dissection re-entry (21.3% vs 19.8%; P = .40) were used similarly. In-hospital major adverse cardiac events (MACE) did not differ (2.9% vs 1.9%; P = .11), whereas in-hospital mortality was higher (1.8% vs 0.5%; P = .001) in dialysis patients. The mortality odds ratio (OR) was 2.36 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70-5.90; P = .106) in multivariable analysis and 2.42 (95% CI, 1.13-5.16; P = .022) after propensity score weighting. The dialysis-mortality association did not vary across center-enrollment categories (interaction P = .522).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite greater clinical and angiographic complexity, dialysis patients had no significant differences in procedural success or MACE but had higher in-hospital mortality. The mortality association remained imprecise, and residual confounding cannot be excluded.
title: Chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary interventions in dialysis patients.

abstract: En México, las enfermedades cardiovasculares constituyen la principal causa de mortalidad de acuerdo con los datos del Inegi, registrándose anualmente cerca de 200 000 defunciones; la cardiopatía isquémica predomina y concentra un promedio de 75% de los decesos. Cerca de 50% de las muertes por cardiopatía isquémica ocurren como un paro cardíaco extrahospitalario, cuya atención tardía puede derivar en muerte súbita cardíaca. La legislación e implementación de espacios cardioprotegidos dotados de recursos humanos, técnicos y organizativos, para iniciar precozmente la cadena de supervivencia y traslado directo a las redes hospitalarias especializadas, pueden duplicar o hasta triplicar la supervivencia ante estos eventos. En México, donde persisten demoras críticas en el reconocimiento, traslado y reperfusión, articular modelos integrados de atención cardiovascular puede mejorar la equidad y reducir las brechas entre los tiempos de actuación, optimizando la cadena de supervivencia y el acceso oportuno a terapias de reperfusión con la red Código Infarto. Fortalecer la continuidad de la atención prehospitalaria mediante la articulación de los espacios cardioprotegidos con la red tiene como objetivo disminuir la carga epidemiológica asociada con el paro cardíaco extrahospitalario y el infarto agudo de miocardio, eventos vinculados con 60 a 80% de las muertes súbitas de origen cardíaco. Por ello, su atención constituye una prioridad de salud pública en México.

abstract: Kounis syndrome (KS) is an uncommon acute coronary syndrome triggered by allergic or hypersensitivity reactions. Bee stings are a recognized precipitant, although the available evidence is largely limited to case reports and small case series. We present a 44-year-old man with probable bee sting-associated KS and systematically review published cases, including an exploratory age-based comparison using ≤45 years as the cutoff for myocardial infarction in younger individuals. PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE) and Scopus were searched in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 recommendations. A total of 47 patients were included, comprising 46 previously reported cases and our index case. The mean age was 55.7+-13.0 years, and 39/47 patients (83.0%) were male. Symptoms developed within 30 minutes in 29/47 patients (61.7%), and chest pain occurred in 41/47 (87.2%). Type II KS predominated (29/43, 67.4%), while ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) occurred in 37/47 patients (78.7%), and revascularization was performed in 27/47 (57.4%). Cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest, and rhythm or conduction disturbances occurred in 11/46 (23.9%), 5/46 (10.9%), and 7/46 patients (15.2%), respectively. Recovery at the last reported assessment was documented in 45/46 patients (97.8%), with no reported deaths. No follow-up data were available after the index patient left the hospital against medical advice approximately five hours after presentation. Thirteen patients (27.7%) were aged ≤45 years; age-stratified descriptive analyses did not reveal clear differences in most clinical characteristics; however, interpretation was limited by the small number of younger patients. Bee sting-associated KS may cause severe acute coronary presentations, including in younger individuals. Given the case-based and heterogeneous nature of the evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in systematically collected cohorts.
