abstract: Suicide left ventricle (SLV) is a rare cause of hemodynamic collapse due to dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, usually after surgical or transcatheter aortic valve replacement. We report a 54-year-old man with hereditary hemochromatosis undergoing bilateral lung transplantation. Following the weaning of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, he developed acute severe hypotension refractory to norepinephrine, vasopressin, and epinephrine. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated a small left ventricular cavity, systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve, and LVOT obstruction, consistent with SLV. Subsequent treatment with very high-dose phenylephrine reversed and stabilized his hemodynamics, and the patient was ultimately discharged home with recovery of cardiac and pulmonary function. This case report presents an unusual occurrence of SLV in the absence of aortic valve intervention and highlights the key importance of clinical vigilance, early detection, and prompt appropriate treatment in this rare but life-threatening situation.
keywords: systolic anterior motion of mitral valve leaflet
title: Suicide Left Ventricle During Lung Transplantation in a Patient With Hereditary Hemochromatosis.

abstract: Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a potentially life-threatening arrhythmia associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients with structural heart disease. Over the past several decades, the management of VT has evolved significantly with the development of catheter-based and noninvasive ablation strategies aimed at eliminating arrhythmogenic myocardial substrates. This review provides a comprehensive overview of global advances in VT ablation, highlighting historical foundations, current therapeutic modalities, and emerging technologies shaping the future of ventricular arrhythmia (VA) management. Radiofrequency ablation remains the cornerstone of VT ablation and has undergone substantial technological refinement through innovations such as irrigated-tip catheters, high-density electroanatomic mapping, contact force sensing, and strategies for achieving deeper myocardial lesions. Alternative catheter-based energy modalities, including cryoablation and the emerging nonthermal technique of pulsed field ablation, provide additional therapeutic options with distinct mechanisms of action and safety profiles. In parallel, procedural advancements such as remote magnetic navigation have improved catheter stability and access to complex ventricular substrates. Beyond traditional catheter ablation, the therapeutic landscape has expanded to include neuromodulatory approaches targeting the cardiac autonomic nervous system, including thoracic epidural anesthesia, stellate ganglion blockade, cardiac sympathetic denervation, and renal denervation. These strategies play an important role in the management of refractory VAs and electrical storm. Furthermore, stereotactic body radiation therapy has emerged as a promising noninvasive treatment for patients with VT who are not candidates for or have failed catheter-based interventions. Additional investigational technologies including laser ablation, microwave ablation, and high-intensity focused ultrasound have been explored in preclinical and limited clinical settings but remain experimental in the context of VT management. Collectively, these evolving technologies underscore the increasingly multimodal approach required to treat complex VAs. In conclusion, VT ablation has progressed from early surgical and direct-current approaches to a sophisticated field incorporating advanced catheter techniques, neuromodulation, robotic navigation, and noninvasive therapies. Continued technological innovation, improved substrate characterization, and integration of emerging tools such as artificial intelligence are expected to further enhance procedural efficacy and patient outcomes. Individualized treatment strategies tailored to patient-specific arrhythmogenic substrates and clinical characteristics remain central to optimizing the management of VT.
journal: The Journal of innovations in cardiac rhythm management
title: Global Advances in Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCAs) and angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCAs) present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We assessed the frequency of coronary microvascular disease (CMD) and its subtypes in MINOCA compared with ANOCA and evaluated long-term cardiovascular outcomes.
METHODS: Patients with nonobstructive coronary arteries undergoing invasive coronary function testing from 2012 to 2022 were prospectively enrolled and retrospectively classified as MINOCA or ANOCA (reference group). Myocardial infarction due to atherothrombosis, myocarditis, and Takotsubo syndrome were excluded. Invasive provocation testing was performed. CMD was classified as endothelium-independent (coronary flow reserve <2.5 with adenosine) and endothelium-dependent (<50% increase in coronary blood flow with acetylcholine). Major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiac death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, urgent revascularization, stroke) were recorded over 8 years.
RESULTS: Of 622 patients, 73 (12%) had MINOCA (69% female, median age 56 years) and 549 (88%) ANOCA (72% female, median age 53 years). CMD was common in both groups (71% versus 64%; P=0.271), while endothelium-independent CMD was more frequent in MINOCA (41% versus 21%; P<0.001). Over a median follow-up of 4.5 years, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred more often in MINOCA (40% versus 11%; adjusted hazard ratio, 2.4; P=0.001). CMD predicted higher major adverse cardiovascular events in both MINOCA (hazard ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-12.0]; P=0.038) and ANOCA (hazard ratio, 7.9 [95% CI, 2.9-21.8]; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: CMD is common in both MINOCA and ANOCA. The higher prevalence of endothelium-independent CMD in MINOCA suggests a potential mechanistic role in infarction. Patients with MINOCA have a worse prognosis than ANOCA, particularly when CMD is present.
title: Classification and Outcomes of Coronary Microvascular Disease in Myocardial Infarction and Angina With Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries.

abstract: Background: The clinical value of physiological assessment after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. We evaluated clinical outcomes associated with post-PCI physiology and temporal trends in its adoption. Methods: PROPHET-FFR (NCT05056662) is an ambispective observational study of patients undergoing invasive physiological assessment of intermediate coronary stenoses. Patients were categorized into three strategies: deferred revascularization based on non-ischemic physiology (deferred PCI), PCI for ischemic lesions without post-PCI physiological assessment (conventional PCI), and physiology-guided PCI with post-PCI assessment and optimization when indicated (post-PCI physiology). Temporal trends in the use of post-PCI physiology and physiology-guided optimization were evaluated, together with the incidence of 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising cardiovascular death, spontaneous myocardial infarction, and target-vessel revascularization (TVR). Propensity score matching between conventional PCI and post-PCI physiology was performed to confirm the primary findings. Results: Among 1,986 patients, 1,307 underwent deferred PCI, 331 conventional PCI, and 348 post-PCI physiology. At 12 months, MACE occurred in 4.1%, 7.6%, and 3.4%, respectively (p=0.011). Compared with conventional-PCI, post-PCI physiology had lower MACE (3.4% vs 7.6%; p=0.019), primarily driven by reduced TVR (2.6% vs 5.4%; p=0.057), with consistent findings after propensity score matching (226 patients/group; 2.7% vs 8.0%; p=0.0114). Post-PCI physiology increased from 11.8% to 22.8% across registry phases (p<0.001), with a numerical increase in physiology-guided optimization (11.6% vs 18.1%; p=0.08). Conclusions: In this observational study, post-PCI physiology appears to be associated with lower 12-month MACE compared with conventional PCI, with consistent findings after propensity score matching.
title: Clinical Impact of Physiology-Guided PCI: 1-year Results of the Post-Revascularization Optimization and Physiological Evaluation of Intermediate Lesions using Fractional Flow Reserve (PROPHET-FFR) Study.

abstract: Hepatitis E virus infection is endemic in Nepal and commonly presents as an acute self-limiting hepatitis. Cardiac involvement is extremely rare and may be life-threatening. We report a case of a young female who presented with fever, jaundice, progressive dyspnea and hypotension. Laboratory assessment confirmed acute hepatitis E infection. Chest radiography revealed cardiomegaly with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated left ventricular dysfunction. Other infectious causes of myocarditis were excluded. The patient improved with inotropic support, heart failure treatment and other supportive management, with complete clinical recovery on follow-up. This case highlights the importance of early cardiac evaluation in patients with acute hepatitis E with features of heart failure.
title: Acute hepatitis E presenting with fulminant myocarditis and cardiogenic shock: A case report from Nepal.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with impaired coronary collateralization in patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO), but circulating biomarkers reflecting defective collateral remodeling remain poorly defined.
METHODS: Olink proteomic profiling was performed in a discovery cohort of 88 CTO patients with T2DM stratified by collateral status. Candidate proteins were prioritized using nominal differential expression and partial least squares-discriminant analyses. Secretoglobin family 3A member 2 (SCGB3A2) was selected for validation by ELISA in an independent cohort of 832 CTO patients (425 with T2DM and 407 without diabetes). Associations with collateralization and incremental predictive value beyond clinical risk factors were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 265 proteins, eight showed nominal differential expression, with SCGB3A2 exhibiting the strongest signal and highest variable importance. In the T2DM cohort, serum SCGB3A2 levels were significantly higher in patients with poor collateralization and inversely correlated with Rentrop grades (both p < 0.001). SCGB3A2 remained independently associated with poor collateralization after multivariable adjustment (OR per 10 ng/mL increase, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.39-1.94; p < 0.001). Addition of SCGB3A2 to a clinical model improved discrimination with an increase in C-statistic from 0.73 to 0.78 and reclassification (NRI 0.62; IDI 0.08). Similar associations were observed in patients without diabetes.
CONCLUSIONS: Circulating SCGB3A2 is independently associated with impaired coronary collateralization in CTO patients. It may reflect biological processes underlying collateral failure and improve risk stratification, particularly in patients with T2DM.
title: Circulating SCGB3A2 Is Associated With Impaired Coronary Collateralization in Patients With Chronic Total Occlusion and Type 2 Diabetes: A Proteomic Discovery and Validation Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock following acute myocardial infarction (AMI-CS) is associated with high mortality. Short-term mechanical circulatory support (ST-MCS) is frequently used after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to stabilize hemodynamics. However, balancing anticoagulation (AC) and antiplatelet therapy in this setting poses substantial bleeding risk.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate real-world antithrombotic strategies and associated ischemic and hemorrhagic complications in AMI-CS patients receiving ST-MCS.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included all consecutive AMI-CS patients who underwent PCI and required ST-MCS between January 2017 and October 2024. AC and antiplatelet regimens were recorded from ST-MCS initiation until shock resolution. Ischemic and hemorrhagic events during this period were analyzed. The primary composite clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of ischemic events and all-cause mortality occurring during the period of cardiogenic shock.
RESULTS: Among 71 patients with AMI-CS who underwent PCI and required ST-MCS (mean age 62 ± 13 years, 69% male), in-hospital mortality was 56%, and MACE occurred in 42%. At ST-MCS initiation, 79% received triple therapy, decreasing to 39% by Day 7. Ischemic events were infrequent (8%) and mainly cerebrovascular. No cases of recurrent myocardial infarction or stent thrombosis were observed. Major bleeding (BARC ≥ 3) occurred in 32% of patients, typically within the first 48 h, and was more frequent in those supported with VA-ECMO.
CONCLUSION: In AMI-CS patients requiring ST-MCS, ischemic events were uncommon, whereas major bleeding was frequent and occurred early. These findings underscore the need for individualized antithrombotic strategies in this high-risk population.
title: Antithrombotic strategies and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock requiring short-term mechanical circulatory support.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Diagnostic workup of patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no acute myocardial infarction (AMI) criteria is challenging. Cardiac CT angiography (CCTA) rules out obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). Adding late iodine enhancement and extracellular volume fraction (CCTA + LIE/ECV) provides insights into myocardial injury. However, the impact on working diagnosis, agreement with discharge diagnosis, and mid-term safety of implementing CCTA + LIE/ECV in the emergency department remains uncertain.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prospective study on consecutive patients presenting, from June 2018 to February 2025, with acute chest pain or equivalents, elevated troponin, and no AMI diagnosis, excluding previously revascularized patients. Patients underwent CCTA to rule out obstructive CAD (≥ 50% stenosis). CCTA-negative patients underwent myocardial tissue characterization with LIE; if negative, ECV was quantified.
PRIMARY ENDPOINT: modification of working diagnosis by CT. Secondary endpoints: agreement between CT and discharge diagnoses after standard-of-care assessment; mid-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in CT-negative patients.
RESULTS: Among 191 patients (age 70 [55-79] years; 53% men), CCTA identified obstructive CAD in 76/191 (40%). LIE/ECV were positive in 58/106 (55%) of CCTA-negative cases, revealing myocarditis in 32/106 (30%), AMI with non-obstructive CAD in 8/106 (8%), Takotsubo in 14/106 (13%), amyloidosis in 3/106 (3%), and dilated cardiomyopathy in 1/106 (1%). CT modified the working diagnosis in 91/191 (48%) patients. Agreement between CT and discharge diagnosis was 0.94 (95% CI 0.89-0.97). In patients with negative CCTA + LIE/ECV, no MACEs occurred after 24 [interquartile range, 19-29] months.
CONCLUSION: In patients with acute symptoms, elevated troponin, and no AMI, a protocol combining CCTA + LIE/ECV enables etiologic assessment of coronary and myocardial conditions, refines working diagnosis, and entails a favorable prognosis when negative.
KEY POINTS: Question Patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no evidence of acute myocardial infarction represent a diagnostic challenge: cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement may have diagnostic and prognostic implications. Findings CT angiography with late iodine enhancement provided a diagnosis in 75% of patients and modified the working diagnosis in 48%. In the 25% CT-negative patients, no adverse events occurred at mid-term follow-up. Clinical relevance A CT protocol including coronary artery evaluation and myocardial tissue characterization may provide a rapid etiological diagnosis in patients with acute symptoms and troponin elevation, potentially supporting earlier clinical decision-making and reducing the need for additional downstream testing.
title: The role of cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement in patients with acute cardiac symptoms and troponin elevation in the era of high-sensitivity assays.
PREOPERATIVE MANAGEMENT OF RENIN ANGIOTENSIN SYSTEM INHIBITORS AND THE INCIDENCE OF POSTOPERATIVE MYOCARDIAL INJURY.

abstract: Intracoronary imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography and intravascular ultrasound, provides detailed insights into plaque morphology and facilitates the precise planning and guidance of percutaneous coronary interventions, especially in patients with complex coronary lesions. Based on the results of multiple randomized clinical trials, current clinical guidelines recommend the use of intracoronary imaging for the treatment of complex coronary lesions. However, the appropriate application of both imaging modalities requires a thorough understanding of their technical principles, as well as their respective strengths and limitations. This article therefore reviews the technical fundamentals of optical coherence tomography and intravascular ultrasound, illustrates their clinical application through selected case examples, and summarizes the current evidence supporting their use.
title: [Invasive intracoronary imaging : Role in routine cardiology].

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the rule-out yield of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-h high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) algorithm for 30-day major adverse cardiac events (MACE) in emergency department (ED) patients aged ≥ 80 years, and explore whether frailty modifies performance.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included patients aged ≥ 80 undergoing 0/1-h hs-cTnI sampling for suspected acute coronary syndrome. Frailty was defined using the Clinical Frailty Scale (≥ 5). The prespecified primary outcome was the 30-day MACE miss rate in the rule-out stratum against a 1% threshold.
RESULTS: Of 1,136 screened encounters, 800 were analyzed (median age 83 years; 56.9% female); 312 (39.0%) were frail. Blinded re-abstraction of 80 records yielded kappa 0.82 (0.71-0.93) for frailty and agreement ≥ 0.71 across variables. The algorithm classified 120 patients (15.0%) as rule-out (prespecified target, 236); two had 30-day MACE (miss rate 1.7%; wide 95% Wilson CI, 0.5%-5.9%), an imprecise estimate whose upper bound exceeds the 1% threshold. A post hoc bounding analysis counting all 11 rule-out patients with incomplete nonfatal ascertainment as events raised the upper bound to 10.8% (6.4%-17.7%). Sensitivity was 99.0% and negative predictive value 98.3%. In prespecified exploratory analysis, no statistically significant independent association was observed between frailty and 30-day MACE (average marginal effect + 1.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.05 to + 7.20; p = 0.744).
CONCLUSIONS: The ESC algorithm ruled out only 15% of octogenarians, potentially reflecting baseline age- and renal-related troponin elevations. Limited rule-out sample size, wide confidence intervals, and incomplete follow-up prevent a definitive safety conclusion.
title: Rule-Out yield of the European society of cardiology 0/1-Hour troponin protocol in frail and non-frail octogenarians.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Low socioeconomic status is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease, yet it remains unclear whether this association has changed over time. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) are key contributors to cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, and health care costs and, thus, are indicators of the overall cardiovascular burden.
OBJECTIVE: To describe temporal trends in incident MACE by equivalized income groups in the Danish population from 1988 to 2023.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide, population-based open cohort study using data from Danish national registries included all residents of Denmark aged 30 years or older who were alive in each year between January 1, 1988, and January 1, 2023, and had available income observations in the current or preceding 5 years. Individuals were followed up to December 31 of each year, to death, or to emigration. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to July 2026.
EXPOSURE: Equivalized disposable household income.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: Incident MACE, defined as the first hospital admission for acute myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke, or heart failure. Age-standardized incidence rates were calculated annually, stratified by income quartile and sex.
RESULTS: A total of 5 932 672 individuals aged 30 years or older were registered in the Danish Civil Registration System from 1988 to 2023. The annual study population increased from 3.06 million in 1988 to 3.85 million in 2023. Most residents in 1988 were female (52.1%), and most in 2023 were male (51.1%); the median age increased from 50.8 years (IQR, 40.2-65.6 years) in 1988 to 55.8 years (IQR, 43.3-68.8 years) in 2023. Age-standardized incidence rates of MACE decreased across all income groups from 1988 to 2023 but remained highest in the lowest income quartile. For males, the rate decreased from 191.1 (95% CI, 186.3-196.0) per 10 000 person-years to 119.6 (95% CI, 116.0-123.2) per 10 000 person-years in the lowest income quartile, while in the highest quartile it decreased from 153.5 (95% CI, 142.9-164.0) per 10 000 person-years to 85.9 (95% CI, 81.2-90.6) per 10 000 person-years. For females, the rate decreased from 116.0 (95% CI, 113.0-118.9) per 10 000 person-years to 70.4 (95% CI, 68.1-72.6) per 10 000 person-years in in the lowest income quartile and from 89.5 (95% CI, 81.9-97.2) per 10 000 person-years to 53.1 (95% CI, 49.0-57.1) per 10 000 person-years in the highest.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of Danish residents aged 30 years or older from 1988 to 2023, the incidence of MACE declined across all socioeconomic groups. Although individuals with lower income generally experienced higher incidence rates, the overall decline occurred in all socioeconomic groups.
title: Socioeconomic Inequality and Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) with inferior vena cava (IVC) tumor thrombus is associated with substantial perioperative risk and frequent recurrence despite nephrectomy and thrombectomy. No established neoadjuvant local therapy exists for this high-risk population.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, clinical outcomes, and exploratory biomarker effects of neoadjuvant stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) targeting IVC tumor thrombus before nephrectomy and thrombectomy.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center prospective phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial enrolled patients with newly diagnosed RCC and Mayo level II to IV IVC tumor thrombus eligible for neoadjuvant SABR and definitive surgery from July 2015 to January 2024. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to August 2026.
INTERVENTION: Neoadjuvant SABR to the radiographically defined IVC tumor thrombus, delivered as 40 Gy in 5 fractions or 36 Gy in 3 fractions, followed by radical nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was 1-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared with a prespecified historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7%. Secondary outcomes included 90-day perioperative morbidity and mortality, adverse events, pulmonary embolism, overall survival, and cancer-specific survival. Exploratory analyses included Ki-67 immunohistochemistry and tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA.
RESULTS: Of 23 patients who received neoadjuvant SABR, 22 completed surgery, and 21 were included in the primary RFS analysis. Of 21 included patients, 12 (57%) were male, and the median (IQR) age was 62.5 (54.0-73.2) years. A total of 19 patients had clear-cell RCC; all tumors were grade 3 or 4, and 3 patients had metastatic disease at enrollment. At a median (range) follow-up of 108.6 (2.0-127.2) months, 1-year RFS was 71.4% (80% CI, 56.6-82.0; 95% CI, 47.2-86.0), meeting the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion based on comparison with the historical surgery-alone benchmark of 55.7% (P = .09). One-year overall survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3) and cancer-specific survival was 95.2% (80% CI, 83.9-98.7; 95% CI, 70.7-99.3). No 90-day perioperative mortality occurred; 4 grade 4 treatment-attributed events occurred, but no grade 4/5 radiation-attributed toxic effects occurred. Ki-67 expression was reduced in patients with irradiated tumor thrombus compared with nonirradiated controls. Tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA was detected in all patients with available plasma and declined after treatment.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this nonrandomized clinical trial, neoadjuvant SABR before nephrectomy and IVC thrombectomy appeared feasible with an acceptable safety profile. RFS met the prespecified phase 2 screening criterion but remains exploratory and warrants further evaluation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02473536.
title: Neoadjuvant Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy Before Inferior Vena Cava Thrombectomy for Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Phase 2 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.

abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) before the age of 40 years is uncommon and warrants a comprehensive evaluation of potential etiologies. Chronic nonmedical anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use has been associated with endothelial dysfunction, accelerated atherosclerosis, and a prothrombotic state, all of which may contribute to premature coronary artery disease. A 29-year-old man with no known medical history and approximately two years of nonmedical testosterone and stanozolol use presented with acute chest pain. Electrocardiography revealed an anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated a thrombotic total occlusion of the mid-left anterior descending coronary artery. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention restored coronary blood flow. The patient presented with Killip class II acute heart failure requiring temporary continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) and inotropic support. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30-35%, with anterior and apical hypokinesia. Admission laboratory tests revealed marked atherogenic dyslipidemia (total cholesterol, 302 mg/dL; low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, 250 mg/dL; high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, 29 mg/dL; triglycerides, 113 mg/dL; and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, 273 mg/dL). In addition to the culprit lesion, nonobstructive atherosclerotic plaques were identified in other coronary segments. At the one-month follow-up, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol had decreased to 85 mg/dL following statin therapy and the reported discontinuation of AAS use. At three months, the patient remained clinically stable, although LVEF remained at 30%. AAS exposure may have contributed to accelerated atherosclerosis and coronary thrombosis in a susceptible young individual. However, alternative causes of MI at a very young age should be systematically considered.
journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
title: Very Young ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Associated With Chronic Nonmedical Anabolic-Androgenic Steroid Use: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI (NSTEMI) are very similar regarding pathophysiology and clinical treatments, especially NSTEMI comprises a much more heterogenic group of patients and underlying diseases. We therefore aimed to assess the treatments and outcomes of both entities in a large contemporary cohort.
METHODS: Patients with STEMI and NSTEMI between 01/01/2010-31/12/2018 were identified from the largest German health insurance (AOK, ≈ 26 million members). Patient demographics, their hospital course, adherence to guideline-directed drug therapy and overall survival were assessed.
RESULTS: In total 544,529 patients (mean age 74, IQR 62-82), one third of whom had a STEMI. Chronic kidney disease, peripheral arterial disease, and heart failure were more common in patients with NSTEMI. Patients with STEMI were more likely to get coronary angiograms and percutaneous coronary interventions. Although STEMI more frequently led to cardiogenic shock, the rate of serious cardiac events was lower. Mortality was higher for STEMI only within the first 30 days, whereas long-term survival rates were better. The combination of statins, angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors/angiotensin receptor blockers, beta blockers, and oral anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents was associated with higher overall survival in patients with STEMI (hazard ratio [HR] 0.21; 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 0.20-0.23; p < 0.001) or NSTEMI (HR 0.40; 95%CI 0.38-0.42; p < 0.001). Nevertheless, the prescription rates decreased over time, particular in patients with NSTEMI.
CONCLUSION: Clear differences between STEMI and NSTEMI were observed regarding short- and long-term survival. Guideline-recommended therapy improved long-term survival, but decreased during the follow-up period.
title: Differences in treatment and outcome of patients with ST- elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI in Germany.

abstract: Cardiac arrest complicating acute coronary syndromes requires immediate coronary reperfusion; however, performing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) during active manual cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) presents significant technical challenges. The Lund University Cardiac Arrest System (LUCAS) provides automated mechanical chest compressions and enables uninterrupted CPR during coronary angiography and PCI. Existing evidence is primarily limited to case reports and small observational studies, mechanical CPR has emerged as a practical adjunct in catheterization laboratories where manual compressions are unsafe or logistically challenging. We report two cases from our center in which LUCAS-assisted PCI was performed during ongoing cardiac arrest in the setting of cardiogenic shock and acute coronary syndromes, alongside a structured narrative synthesis of contemporary literature addressing feasibility, procedural considerations, and clinical outcomes. Mechanical chest compressions allowed uninterrupted angiography and successful revascularization in both cases, with return of spontaneous circulation achieved in one patient. Despite procedural success, survival remained poor, reflecting severe global ischemia and metabolic derangement. LUCAS-assisted PCI is a technically feasible strategy that facilitates coronary reperfusion in carefully selected patients. Evidence of survival benefit remains limited and derives predominantly from observational studies and case reports rather than randomized controlled trials. The role of extracorporeal CPR (ECPR) as a complementary or alternative strategy warrants explicit consideration at appropriately resourced centers. Improved patient selection and integration into structured resuscitation pathways may enhance clinical outcomes.
journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
title: Mechanical CPR - Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention During Cardiac Arrest: Feasibility and Outcomes.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a complication of severe aortic stenosis. Its prevalence after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and prognostic significance are understudied, as are the post-TAVI trajectories of microvascular indices.
AIMS: The aims of this study were to determine the pooled prevalence of CMD, the influence of the diagnostic modality, the post-TAVI coronary flow reserve (CFR) and microvascular resistance changes, and the prognostic impact of baseline CMD on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI.
METHODS: Five databases were searched from January 2010 to December 2025 for studies involving adults with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI in which CMD was assessed by wire-based thermodilution, angiography-derived indices, Doppler measurements, or stress cardiac magnetic resonance. The risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE, respectively. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird) pooled CMD prevalence (stratified by modality), CFR change (mean difference; before-after design), and prognostic hazard ratios (HRs). Change in microvascular resistance was synthesized narratively. The protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD42025143775) and reported per the PRISMA 2020 guidance.
RESULTS: Eleven primary studies were analyzed, 10 of which (n = 1,212) contributed to the prevalence analyses. An additional study (n = 126) was included in the sensitivity analyses only. CMD prevalence was 46.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] [34.0, 59.9]; I2 = 72%) and 38.4% (95% CI [35.3, 41.7]; I2 = 0%) when assessed using wire-based thermodilution (k = 6, n = 324) and angiographic (k = 4, n = 888) indices, respectively. CFR increased post-TAVI by a pooled mean difference of +0.49 (95% CI [+0.27, + 0.71]; I2 = 72%; k = 5, n = 103 paired observations). Reductions in microvascular resistance were confined to pressure-to-velocity and reserve ratio indices, and absolute minimal microvascular resistance was unchanged (k = 4, n = 85). The HR for MACE was 3.22 (95% CI [0.98, 10.60]; I2 = 78%; k = 2, n = 585). Substantial heterogeneity reflected non-equivalent CMD definitions.
CONCLUSION: The prevalence of CMD pre-TAVI is influenced by the diagnostic method. CFR tends to improve after TAVI, likely due to reduced resting demand rather than structural repair. The CMD-MACE association should be viewed as hypothesis-generating due to limited studies, varied CMD definitions, and incompatible HR calculations. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized CMD definitions are required.
title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

abstract: Impaired microcirculation predicts mortality in cardiogenic shock independent of systemic hemodynamics, yet current treatment strategies focus primarily on restoring macrocirculatory markers. We studied whether full-support microaxial flow pump (mAFP) therapy improves sublingual microcirculation in cardiogenic shock. A prospective, single-arm, observational study of serial sublingual microcirculation imaging via incident darkfield handheld videomicroscopy was performed in 18 cardiogenic shock patients undergoing Impella 5.5 (mAFP) placement. Microvascular flow index (MFI), microvascular heterogeneity index (MHI), proportion of perfused vessels (PPV), and perfused vessel density (PVD) were measured. Eighteen patients were enrolled. Microvascular flow index (p = 0.004), MHI (p = 0.055), PPV (p = 0.003), and PVD (p = 0.067) improved immediately on support, including when adjusted for vasoactive-inotropic score. Improvement in MFI, MHI, PPV, or PVD was most pronounced in those with impaired baseline microcirculatory hemodynamics (all p < 0.05), whereas those with preserved baseline values demonstrated no change. Improved agreement between systemic and microcirculatory hemodynamics was observed in association with mAFP support, and none experienced worsening microcirculatory function. These exploratory findings suggest full-support mAFPs may improve impaired microcirculation during cardiogenic shock, although device-specific effects cannot be isolated from overall clinical improvement; validation in larger studies is warranted. Although agreement between systemic and microcirculatory hemodynamic markers improved, no macrohemodynamic marker proved sufficient to ensure adequate microcirculatory perfusion.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance improves percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) outcomes, yet recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) challenged these findings.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI in complex coronary lesions, incorporating recent large-scale trials with divergent findings.
METHODS: The authors conducted a meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI among patients with complex coronary lesions. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cardiac death. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using frequentist random-effects models and complementary Bayesian analyses. The analysis was complemented by several sensitivity and subgroup analyses.
RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients were included. IVI guidance was associated with significant reductions in MACE (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83), cardiac death (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.76-0.998), clinically driven target lesion revascularization (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-0.999), and stent thrombosis (RR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.35-0.78). A significant geographic interaction was identified for MACE, with benefit predominantly driven by Asian trial populations (Pinteraction < 0.01). In subgroup analysis, patients achieving imaging-defined stent optimization were associated with lower event rates than those who did not (RR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.26-0.62).
CONCLUSIONS: IVI guidance reduces the risk of adverse events for complex lesions. The benefit was in part driven by achieving imaging-defined stent optimization.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; 18 RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Geographic heterogeneity, with benefit concentrated in Asian trials, and subgroup comparison by stent optimisation is not randomised.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials found intravascular imaging guidance associated with fewer adverse events than angiography guidance in complex lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACE RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83; cardiac death RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97. Significant geographic interaction for MACE (Pinteraction < 0.01), with benefit predominantly in Asian trial populations.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates the pooled evidence for imaging-guided PCI after recent large trials with divergent findings and flags possible transportability limits.

title: Intravascular Imaging-Guided Drug-Eluting Stenting for Complex Coronary Lesions: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

abstract: The purpose of this article is to summarize pharmacotherapy-related emergency medicine (EM) literature indexed in 2025. Articles were selected using a modified Delphi approach. The table of contents from predetermined journals were reviewed and independently evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system by paired authors. Pharmacotherapy-related publications deemed to be GRADE 1A and 1B were reviewed by the collective group for inclusion in the review. This article synthesizes and evaluates findings from 7 randomized controlled trials, 10 guidelines, clinical policies, position statements, or consensus recommendations, and 11 meta-analyses, providing critical insight into their potential clinical impact. Covered topics include guideline or policy updates on advanced cardiac life support, rapid sequence intubation, tranexamic acid in trauma, acute coronary syndromes, and hypertension. Randomized controlled trials covering sedative use in rapid sequence intubation, treatment of sexually transmitted infections and bacterial vaginosis, sodium bicarbonate for severe acidemia and acute kidney injury in the critically ill, and thrombolytic therapy beyond traditional time windows for ischemic stroke are also reviewed. Additional topics include nebulized and low-dose ketamine for analgesia, erector spinae plane block for renal colic, two-bag versus three-bag acetylcysteine regimens for acetaminophen overdose, QT prolongation in antipsychotic overdose, and naltrexone for opioid dependence.
journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
title: Emergency medicine pharmacotherapy literature of 2025.

abstract: Bivalirudin is a synthetic oligopeptide used as an anticoagulant for the treatment of acute coronary syndromes and for the prevention of thrombosis in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. As peptides are complex molecules that may exhibit inherently complex impurity profiles, three orthogonal ultra-performance liquid chromatographic methods were developed in this work, in accordance with Analytical Quality-by-Design principles, to ensure the safety and efficacy of the bivalirudin drug product. Starting from a structure-driven theoretical assessment of bivalirudin, which anticipates the formation of peptide fragments, deamidation and oxidation products, as well as covalent oligomers under stress conditions, method development was directed into three orthogonal chromatographic modes-size-exclusion (SEC), reversed-phase (RP) and hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC) - enabling a comprehensive evaluation of its degradation pathways. For the first time, bivalirudin oligomers (dimers and trimers) were detected and characterized using size-exclusion chromatography. The combination of HILIC and RP chromatography methods ensured separation of 10 non-oligomeric bivalirudin impurities. The developed methods employed MS-compatible mobile phases to facilitate structural elucidation of bivalirudin degradation products by high-resolution mass spectrometry. Stress conditions included acid and base hydrolysis, oxidation with H₂O₂, thermal decomposition, and light exposure, as regulated by ICH guidelines. Extensive risk assessment was conducted using Ishikawa diagrams and heat maps. Method development was carried out using Design of Experiments methodology, supported by Fusion AE software. The developed ultra-performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) methods were validated, confirming their suitability for analyzing bivalirudin and its related impurities.
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
title: Comprehensive analysis of peptide pharmaceutical: Development of three orthogonal chromatographic methods and characterization of bivalirudin degradation products by high-resolution mass spectrometry.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is characterized by chronic immune-inflammatory activation. The relationship between the peripheral CD4+/CD8+ T-cell ratio and coronary stenosis severity remains unclear. We investigated its association with SYNTAX score and potential as a complementary marker.
METHODS: CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell counts were measured by flow cytometry in 297 patients with CAD and 181 controls. Coronary stenosis was assessed by angiography and SYNTAX score. Multivariable linear regression was used for SYNTAX score, and logistic regression for moderate-to-severe stenosis (SYNTAX > 23). Models were adjusted for age, sex, BMI, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, HbA1c, hs-CRP, creatinine, and medications. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR was applied. ROC analysis assessed incremental value beyond risk factors.
RESULTS: CD4+ counts and the CD4+/CD8+ ratio were higher, and CD8+ counts lower, in CAD patients, especially in acute coronary syndromes. In unadjusted analyses, SYNTAX score correlated positively with CD4+ count and the CD4+/CD8+ ratio and negatively with CD8+ count (weak to moderate). After adjustment, the CD4+/CD8+ ratio remained independently associated with SYNTAX score (β = 4.88, 95% CI 1.42-8.30, p = 0.006). For SYNTAX > 23, the ratio showed limited discrimination (AUC = 0.598, 95% CI 0.526-0.670; sensitivity 0.587, specificity 0.552 at cutoff 1.90). Adding the ratio to conventional risk factors showed no substantial incremental value (ΔAUC = 0.010, DeLong p = 0.43, NRI = 0.082, IDI = 0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral T-cell imbalance is associated with greater angiographic coronary complexity in CAD. However, the CD4+/CD8+ ratio has limited discriminatory ability and should be considered a complementary candidate marker, not a standalone diagnostic or predictive tool. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required.
title: Association of peripheral CD4⁺/CD8⁺ T-cell ratio with SYNTAX score and coronary stenosis severity in patients with coronary artery disease.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chest pain is a frequent reason for Emergency Department (ED) visits, although only a minority of patients ultimately present an Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS). Current diagnostic strategies rely heavily on troponin testing, but a new clinical tool requiring no blood sampling, the HEAR score, has recently been proposed. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of the HEAR score for identifying low-risk patients presenting with chest pain, using 45-day Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE) as the primary outcome.
METHODS: All patients presenting with chest pain to the ED of Dijon University Hospital in 2019 were retrospectively analyzed in this single-center study. Patients were stratified as "low risk" (HEAR < 2) or "high risk" (HEAR ≥ 2). Outcomes assessed at 45-days included MACE (defined as a composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and urgent coronary revascularization) and recurrence of ED consultation for chest pain.
RESULTS: Among 2177 patients presenting with chest pain, 1807 met inclusion criteria. Of these, 653 (36%) were classified as low risk (HEAR < 2). At 45-days, 22 (3%) low-risk patients reconsulted for chest pain compared with 64 (6%) in the high-risk group (p = 0.037). No MACE was identified among low-risk patients within the available follow-up data. The negative predictive value of a HEAR score < 2 was 100% (95% CI: 99.5%-100%), with an upper 95% confidence bound for the event rate of 0.46%.
CONCLUSION: A HEAR score < 2 identifies a substantial proportion of ED chest pain patients at very low risk of short-term adverse cardiovascular events. However, given the limitations of retrospective follow-up and potential under-ascertainment of events, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. The HEAR score may contribute to early clinical risk stratification rather than replace troponin-based strategies.
title: Chest pain in the emergency room: value of the new HEAR score identifying patients with low risk of acute coronary syndrome without troponin testing.

abstract: BackgroundThe role of prophylactic preoperative intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the safety and outcomes of preoperative IABP insertion in high-risk CABG patients.MethodsA retrospective review of outcomes of patients who had preoperative IABP insertion undergoing isolated CABG at a single United Kingdom quaternary centre was conducted between January 2015 and June 2025. Indications for IABP insertion were divided into prophylactic (critical coronary anatomy) and non-prophylactic insertion (haemodynamic instability and persistent angina). Primary outcome was 30-day mortality, and secondary outcomes included 90-day mortality, incidence of postoperative complications, specific complications related to IABP insertion and postoperative length of stay. Comparative analysis was performed between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed.Results610 patients underwent isolated CABG with preoperative IABP; 302 (49.5%) received prophylactic IABP and 308 (50.5%) had non-prophylactic insertion. There were 14 (2.3%) 30-day mortality and 20 (3.3%) 90-day mortality, with no significant difference in mortality between the two groups. Mean postoperative length of hospital stay was 11 ± 7 days; this was significantly longer in the non-prophylactic group (12 ± 8 vs 10 ± 7 days, p < 0.01). Postoperative neurological dysfunction occurred in 42 patients (6.9%) and dialysis in 5 (0.8%), with no differences between the two groups. There were 25 (4.1%) IABP-related complications; 8 localised haematoma managed conservatively, 4 wound infections treated with intravenous antibiotics, 5 lower limb ischaemia (3 required surgical re-vascularisation), 2 fatal bowel ischaemia, 2 renal and splenic malperfusion, 2 localised femoral artery dissection and 2 retroperitoneal haematoma (1 required emergency laparotomy).ConclusionThis study supports the selective use of prophylactic IABP in patients undergoing high-risk CABG. In this selected cohort, preoperative IABP use was associated with low early mortality, favourable long-term survival and an acceptable complication profile.
title: Outcomes of preoperative intra-aortic balloon pump insertion in high-risk coronary artery bypass grafting: A decade of single-centre experience.

abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) are increasingly prescribed for glycemic control and weight management, but their association with postoperative thrombotic events after total knee arthroplasty remains unclear. We performed a retrospective cohort study using deidentified data from the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network, including adults who underwent primary total knee arthroplasty between December 1, 2006 and June 1, 2025. Patients with prior myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, venous thromboembolism, or pulmonary embolism were excluded. Exposure was defined as a prescription for a GLP-1 RA within 1 year and 1 day before surgery. A 1:1 propensity score match was performed on demographics, relevant comorbidities, and medications, yielding 11,765 patients in each cohort. Outcomes were postoperative myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, venous thromboembolism, and pulmonary embolism. Compared with matched controls, patients prescribed GLP-1 receptor agonists had a significantly lower risk of myocardial infarction (25/11,246 vs 47/11,171; risk ratio [RR] 0.528; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.325 - 0.858). GLP-1 RA use was also associated with a reduced risk of deep vein thrombosis (74/11,319 vs 103/11,308; RR 0.718; 95% CI, 0.533 - 0.966) and venous thromboembolism (133/11,040 vs 172/11,027; RR 0.772; 95% CI, 0.617 - 0.967). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in the incidence of pulmonary embolism between groups (49/11,352 vs 58/11,382; RR 0.847; 95% CI, 0.580 - 1.238). Overall, preoperative GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with a significantly lower postoperative risk of myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, and venous thromboembolism following total knee arthroplasty in this large, nationally representative cohort.
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use Before Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Lower Postoperative MI, DVT, and VTE Rates.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual cardiovascular risk remains substantial in patients with established coronary artery disease despite contemporary secondary prevention strategies. Conventional approaches focused on isolated risk factors may fail to capture the multidimensional heterogeneity of this population.
PURPOSE: To identify distinct clinical phenotypes using an unsupervised analytical approach and to explore their association with recurrent cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter observational study based on the INTERASPIRE registry, including 592 Latin American patients with prior acute coronary syndrome or coronary revascularization. Variables from a standardized interview were grouped into demographic, clinical, metabolic, and psychosocial domains. After variable selection, clustering was performed using Partitioning Around Medoids with Gower distance. Associations with 12-month cardiovascular events were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression models.
RESULTS: Three phenotypes were identified. Cluster 1 (42%) included younger patients with lower comorbidity burden and lower psychosocial vulnerability. Cluster 2 (27%) showed greater psychosocial burden and an adverse lipid profile, defining a higher-risk phenotype. Cluster 3 (31%) included older patients with multiple comorbidities and greater renal dysfunction. During 12-month follow-up, 7% experienced cardiovascular events. Event rates differed across clusters (3%, 10%, and 9%; log-rank p = 0.02). Compared with cluster 1, only cluster 2 showed increased risk (HR 2.66; 95% CI 1.11-6.39; p = 0.029).
CONCLUSIONS: Unsupervised phenotyping identified three clinical profiles with distinct prognostic implications. Residual cardiovascular risk appears to reflect the interaction of lipid, renal, and psychosocial domains beyond traditional risk factors.
title: Residual risk in coronary artery disease: Identification of cardio-reno-metabolic and psychosocial phenotypes in a Latin American cohort of the INTERASPIRE registry.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evolving transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) technology warrants updated comparisons of the most commonly used current generation self-expanding (SE) versus balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THV).
METHODS: This 9-center retrospective analysis stratified patients undergoing TAVR from 2021-2024 into SE-THV and BE-THV cohorts balanced via propensity score matching. Primary outcomes were all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, stroke, and permanent pacemaker (PPM) need. Secondary outcomes were paravalvular leak (PVL) and acute kidney injury. All outcomes were assessed perioperatively and at 30 and 400 days. Analyses were repeated within LVEF , aortic valve area, and center-level strata.
RESULTS: The total cohort included 2,594 BE-THV and 1,058 SE-THV patients. Matching yielded 680 patients per cohort. After matching , SE-THV patients had higher risk for ischemic stroke (p<0.05) and PPM (p<0.05) during index hospitalization, with no difference in mortality. At follow-up, the SE-THV cohort had higher risk of mild (p<0.05) and moderate (p<0.05) paravalvular leak, stroke (p<0.05) and PPM (p<0.05). PPM after SE-THV was significantly lower in high-volume compared to low-volume centers. Kaplan-Meier survival did not differ. Among patients with LVEF ≥45%, SE-THV was associated with higher stroke risk (p<0.05); BE-THV patients with LVEF < 45% were associated with increased all-cause mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, SE-THV correlated with higher rates of ischemic stroke, PPM need, and PVL during index hospitalization and increased mild and moderate PVL upon follow-up. Mortality did not differ during index hospitalization or at follow-up. The normal LVEF SE-THV cohort was associated with higher stroke risk compared to all other groups.

abstract:
AIMS: To quantify the excess acute coronary syndrome (ACS) burden and post-ACS mortality associated with diabetes and assess LDL-C target attainment, focusing on sex differences.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 5,361 patients with the first ACS admission identified during the study period (2016-2024) in a Spanish healthcare department. Hospitalization trends were analyzed using population-based regression models. Long-term mortality was assessed by Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression. LDL-C target attainment was evaluated according to ESC/EAS recommendations.
RESULTS: Diabetes was present in 36.9 % of patients. ACS hospitalization rates declined by 8.3 % annually (95 % CI 6.1-10.4), with no diabetes-by-time interaction (p = 0.17). In-hospital case fatality was 6.3 % and did not differ by diabetes status. During a median 4.9-year follow-up, diabetes was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.22, 95 % CI 1.11-1.33), with a stronger association in women than men (interaction p = 0.009). Only 28.9 % achieved LDL-C < 55 mg/dL, with no temporal improvement; female sex independently predicted poor LDL-C control (adjusted OR 1.65, 95 % CI 1.38-1.97).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite declining ACS hospitalizations, DM remained associated with increased long-term mortality, particularly in women. LDL-C target attainment remained suboptimal, highlighting persistent gaps in secondary prevention.
title: Diabetes, Long-Term mortality, and LDL-C target attainment after an acute coronary syndrome: A population-based cohort study (2016-2024).

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prevalence of perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI), the quality-of-care patients receive and their outcomes, and how this varies across different operations.
METHODS: We included adults from England with AMI between Jan 2010 and March 2023 from the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project registry, linked to Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). Cox-regression models compared risk of all-cause mortality at thirty-days and five-years, subgroup analyses compared operation type (orthopaedic, vascular, upper (UGI) and lower gastrointestinal (LGI) and urological).
RESULTS: We identified 2,821 episodes of type 1 PMI in 533,026 eligible patients (0.5%). Orthopaedics were the largest contributing speciality (45%). Risk of thirty-day mortality was significantly higher in PMI patients at thirty-days (adjusted Hazard Ratio):1.34 [95% CIs 1.21-1.49]) and five-years (1.36 [1.29-1.43]) (both P<0.001). For thirty-day mortality, risk was not significant in orthopaedics and urology but was for vascular (1.75 [1.40-2.18]), UGI (1.95 [1.43-2.66) and LGI surgery (1.94 [1.50-2.51]) (all P<0.001). For those who survived to hospital discharge, PMI patients had higher mortality risk at five-years (1.26 [1.19-1.34), especially high in the UGI (1.76 [1.44-2.13]), LGI (1.34 [1.13-1.59]) and urology groups (1.61 [1.34-1.93]) (all P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: PMI mortality is significantly higher than AMI all-comers, seen across all subspecialties up to five-years, with variation in the risk of mortality from PMI according to operation type. PMI may identify a high-risk vulnerable group of patients, whose increased mortality risk persists long term, even in those who survive to discharge.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort (Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project linked to Hospital Episode Statistics); 2,821 episodes of type 1 PMI in 533,026 eligible patients (0.5%).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data restricted to type 1 PMI recorded in the audit, with residual confounding and likely under-ascertainment of perioperative events.
appraisal.one_line: Registry-linked cohort of type 1 perioperative MI after non-cardiac surgery in England, reporting short- and long-term mortality by operation type.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Risk of thirty-day mortality was significantly higher in PMI patients at thirty-days (adjusted Hazard Ratio):1.34 [95% CIs 1.21-1.49]) and five-years (1.36 [1.29-1.43]) (both P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the long-term mortality associated with type 1 perioperative MI and its variation by surgical specialty, relevant to invasive management pathways after noncardiac surgery.

title: The Burden of Type 1 Peri-Operative Myocardial Infarction After Non-Cardiac Surgery: Insights From the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project From 2010-2023.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are differences in acute coronary syndrome (ACS), with a worse prognosis in women.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate sex differences in presentation, management of the myocardial infarction code and in-hospital mortality in the National Registry of Acute Coronary Syndromes.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A total of 62,118 adults (74% men and 26% women) with ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or non ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) treated in 177 hospitals were included. Treatment and prognosis were compared.
RESULTS: Women had higher comorbidity and lower smoking rates. STEMI was more prevalent in men (73.0% vs. 63.6%), and Non ST Elevation-Acute Coronary Ayndrome (NSTE-ACS) was more prevalent in women (36.4% vs. 27.0%). Under the heart attack code, reperfusion rates were higher in men: percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) 28.3% vs. 27.9%, fibrinolytic therapy (FT) 36.4% vs. 31.9%, and pharmaco-invasive strategy (PIS) 7.9% vs. 7.2%, respectively; non-reperfusion rates were higher in women (27.3% vs. 33%; p < 0.0001). Complications were more frequent in women, and mortality was also higher in women (15.3% vs. 10.4%; OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.48-1.65). In logistic regression, female sex, age, diabetes, and hypertension independently predicted in-hospital death.
CONCLUSIONS: Women received less reperfusion, greater comorbidity and mortality, therefore timely and equitable care in the myocardial infarction code must be guaranteed.
title: Sex differences in hospital mortality with the myocardial infarction code.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the prognostic factors of patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) complicated with moderate to severe chronic kidney disease (CKD) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and to establish a risk predictive model.
METHODS: The medical records of 148 ACS patients with moderate to severe CKD who received PCI in the Department of Cardiology, Peking University Third Hospital from September 2021 to January 2023 and completed 12-month follow-up were retrospectively analyzed. According to whether the patients had a major adverse cardiovascular disease (MACE) 12 months after PCI, they were divided into MACE group and non-MACE group. Binary Logistic regression analysis was performed on the general clinical data, clinical test results, echocardiography, coronary angiography and PCI data of the two groups of patients, the prognostic factors were analyzed by backward stepwise regression, and the risk prediction model was established. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was drawn to test the predictive efficiency of the model.
RESULTS: A total of 148 patients with ACS combined with moderate to severe CKD were included in the study, including 50 patients in the MACE group and 98 patients in the non-MACE group, and the incidence of MACE 12 months after PCI was 33.8%.Binary Logistic analysis of hospitalization data of the two groups showed that white blood cell (OR＝1.145; 95%CI: 1.017-1.290; P＝0.026), age (OR＝1.032; 95%CI: 1.001-1.065; P＝0.046) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; OR＝0.962; 95%CI: 0.934-0.990; P＝0.009) were independent influencing factors for MACE 12 months after PCI (P < 0.05), CKD stage was not associated with the occurrence of MACE 12 months after PCI. The risk prediction model for MACE was Logit(P) = 0.032× age +0.136× leukocyte－0.039×LVEF. ROC curve analysis showed that this model had good prediction efficiency, and the area under the curve (AUC) predicted by the prediction model was 0.749, 95%CI was 0.666 to 0.832. The sensitivity and specificity were 72% and 68%.
CONCLUSION: The incidence of MACE was higher in ACS patients with moderate to severe CKD 12 months after PCI, and white blood cells, age and LVEF were independent factors influencing the occurrence of MACE in these patients after PCI.
journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
journal_abbrev: Beijing Da Xue Xue Bao Yi Xue Ban
title: [Analysis of prognostic factors in patients with acute coronary syndrome complicated with moderate to severe chronic kidney disease after percutaneous coronary intervention].

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the correlation between angio-based microvascular resistance (AMR) and impaired left ventricular systolic function in patients with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and to assess its predictive value for left ventricular systolic function.
METHODS: A study was conducted, enrolling consecutive STEMI patients who underwent primary PCI at the Department of Cardiology, Peking University Third Hospital from May 2023 to June 2024. Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) and AMR were calculated from coronary angiography images immediately after PCI, and myocardial biomarker or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) assessed by echocardiography at half-year follow-up were collected. The correlation between AMR, QFR, myocardial biomarkers, and LVEF after half a year was analyzed. The STEMI patients were divided into normal or reduced left ventricular systolic function with LVEF 0.5 as the boundary. The accuracy of AMR in diagnosing reduced left ventricular systolic function was analyzed by receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC).
RESULTS: A total of 194 patients were enrolled, with an average age of (63.3±13.6) years, and the average AMR value was (246.99±57.18) mmHg·s/m. Age, peak creatine kinase (CK), troponin T (TnT), N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and AMR were identified as independent predictive factors for LVEF at half-year follow-up (β=-0.160, t=-2.533, P=0.012; β=-0.271, t=-3.068, P=0.002; β=-0.191, t=-2.157, P=0.032; β=-0.280, t=-4.515, P < 0.001; β=-0.162, t=-2.711, P=0.007). ROC curve analysis showed that AMR had a certain value in predicting reduced left ventricular systolic function [area under curve (95% confidence interval) was 0.631 (0.543-0.718), P=0.006], and the optimal cut-off value for predicting an LVEF < 0.5 was 250.5 mmHg·s/m.
CONCLUSION: AMR is an independent predictor of LVEF at half-year post-procedure and has significant predictive value for reduced left ventricular systolic function, potentially playing an important role in predicting the prognosis of STEMI patients.
journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
journal_abbrev: Beijing Da Xue Xue Bao Yi Xue Ban
title: [Prognostic value of angio-based microvascular resistance on left ventricular systolic function in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction].

abstract: Intracoronary imaging has become an important tool for the in vivo assessment of coronary atherosclerosis and for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention. By enabling high-resolution visualization of coronary anatomy, these modalities allow for more accurate lesion characterization, precise stent sizing, and optimized procedural strategies. In recent years, multiple randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention reduces major adverse cardiac events (including cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and repeat revascularization), particularly in complex clinical and anatomical settings. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting the use of intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography to guide percutaneous coronary intervention and improve clinical outcomes, drawing from recent trial data and current guideline recommendations. Special emphasis is placed on complex lesion subsets, such as left main coronary artery disease and other complex bifurcation lesions, calcified lesions, long lesions, and scenarios involving patients at heightened risk, such as those with acute coronary syndrome. Finally, this review considers the strengths and limitations of intracoronary imaging, as well as unresolved questions and priority areas for future research aimed at further improving patient outcomes.
title: Intracoronary imaging to assess atherosclerosis and to guide percutaneous coronary intervention.

abstract: Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure is now an established strategy for thromboembolic prevention in atrial fibrillation. However, the organizational requirements governing its performance remain heterogeneous across regulations and healthcare systems, particularly in France. In this context, it is relevant to assess whether, in experienced centers, an organizational model based on specific expertise and a rapid surgical referral pathway could provide a safe alternative to the presence of on-site cardiac surgery. This article is in favor of extension in France of percutaneous left atrial appendage closure in centres without on-site cardiac surgery.
title: [Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure: Towards enlargement of implantations in centres without on-site cardiac surgery].

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Mitral valve repair (MVr) is the ideal treatment strategy for degenerative mitral regurgitation. Mitral valve replacement (MVR) may be required if MVr is unsuccessful during the index surgery. The consequences of MVR following failed MVr during the same surgery are unclear.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.
SETTING: Single institution, university affiliated.
PARTICIPANTS: All patients who underwent MVR from 2010 through 2024 were included. Patients with concomitant surgeries were included.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were dichotomized into the intended repair (IR) or de novo replacement (DR) groups based on the intended procedure.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 1,661 patients (mean age, 64 years; 57% female) underwent MVR. MVr was attempted in 133 patients (8%, IR group), and 1,528 underwent planned MVR (92%, DR group). The mean ejection fraction was 55%. Female sex (58.0% in the DR group v 48.9% in the IR group, p = 0.04), history of infective endocarditis (23.8% v 15.0%, p = 0.02), history of cerebrovascular disease (32.1% v 19.5%, p = 0.03), and prior sternotomy (32.1% v 15.8%, p < 0.001) were more prevalent in the DR group. After propensity score matching, perioperative morbidity and mortality were similar. The median cardiopulmonary bypass time and cross-clamp time were longer in the IR group (207 minutes v 134 minutes in the DR group and 163 minutes v 102 minutes in the DR group, respectively). Kaplan-Meier curve analysis showed similar 5-year survival (p = 0.91).
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative outcomes were similar despite longer operative times in the IR group. Failure of initial MVr, leading to MVR, did not translate into adverse early or long-term outcomes. These findings suggest that repair may be more aggressively considered in patients with repairable anatomies.
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
title: Outcomes of Patients Undergoing Mitral Valve Replacement After Failed Attempt at Mitral Valve Repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is a major public health issue with rising hospitalizations and high mortality. This study was conducted to assess the clinical presentation, management and outcome of heart failure patients presenting to a tertiary care hospital.
METHODS: A prospective, observational study was conducted at a tertiary cardiac center in Nepal over a period of six months among admitted patients aged 18 years and above with heart failure. Data on demographics, etiology, treatment, and outcomes were collected via structured interviews, chart review, clinical observation, phone calls and follow-up. Etiologies were defined per standard criteria and patients were categorized according to the clinical and echocardiographic diagnosis.
RESULTS: Among 1523 patients included, the mean age of the cohort was 61.5 ± 14.9 years, and 62.0 % were male. Coronary artery disease (65.8%) was the most common etiology, followed by idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (15.0%) and rheumatic heart disease (7.2%). Acute coronary syndrome (39.9%) was the primary aggravating factor. Guideline-directed medical therapy use included Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor Blocker (68.5%), Beta-blockers (66.1%), and Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists (61.2%); however, the use of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 inhibitors was low (15.2%). Device therapy was rare (0.26%). The overall mortality rate was 12.7%, comprising 4.7% in-hospital mortality and 7.9% 90-day mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary artery disease is the commonest etiology, with Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitor or Angiotensin Receptor Blocker as the commonest prescription, followed by Beta-blockers and Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists, with device therapy being rare, with an overall mortality of 12.7%.
journal: Journal of Nepal Health Research Council
keywords: Coronary artery disease; dilated cardiomyopathy; guideline-directed medical therapy; heart failure.
title: Clinical Presentation, Management and Outcome of Heart Failure Patients.

abstract: Chest pain is a common high-risk complaint encountered by emergency medical services (EMS). Early identification and treatment of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) improve outcomes, yet prehospital evaluation remains constrained by limited diagnostic resources. This narrative review examines contemporary approaches to prehospital ACS risk stratification, diagnostic technologies, and decision-making. A targeted PubMed search of peer-reviewed publications and selected grey literature published between 2020 and 2025 was supplemented by targeted searches and citation review. Relevant literature published after the initial search period was incorporated during manuscript preparation and revision. Studies addressing prehospital ACS risk stratification, electrocardiogram (ECG) assessment, point-ofcare biomarkers, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted diagnostics, and systems-level cardiac triage were included and synthesized thematically. Biomarker-integrated pathways, particularly HEART-derived approaches combined with point-of-care troponin testing, demonstrated the strongest evidence for safe prehospital risk assessment and reduced healthcare utilization. Biomarker-free approaches offered broader applicability but lower diagnostic certainty. ECG acquisition and transmission remained foundational for STEMI recognition and activation, while AI-assisted ECG interpretation and decision-support tools showed promising diagnostic performance but lacked prospective outcome-based validation. Gaps remain regarding atypical presentations, sex-specific strategies, and validation across diverse EMS environments. Overall, contemporary evidence supports structured prehospital risk stratification as decision support rather than definitive diagnosis. Implementation depends on provider training, protocol standardization, resources, and integration within regional systems of care. Future research should prioritize validation across diverse EMS settings, atypical and sex-specific presentations, and prospective evaluation of emerging diagnostic technologies.
title: Contemporary Approaches to Prehospital Acute Coronary Syndrome Risk Stratification: A Narrative Review.

abstract: Background and Objectives: Although chronic total occlusion (CTO) often presents with varying degrees of coronary collateral circulation (CCC), the biological factors accompanying inadequate collateralization are not fully established. The Remnant Cholesterol Inflammation Index (RCII) is a composite metric integrating atherogenic lipid load and systemic inflammation. This study examined the association between RCII and CCC and the discriminative ability of RCII for identifying insufficient collateral networks in patients with CTO. Materials and Methods: This retrospective, single-center analysis evaluated 359 patients with at least one major epicardial CTO who underwent diagnostic coronary angiography between 15 January 2023 and 15 January 2026. Participants were stratified via the Rentrop scoring system into poor (grades 0-1; n = 168) and good (grades 2-3; n = 191) CCC cohorts. RCII was calculated as [remnant cholesterol (mg/dL) × high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP, mg/L)]/10, with remnant cholesterol derived as total cholesterol minus LDL-C and HDL-C. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models, together with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, were used to assess the association of RCII with poor CCC and its discriminative ability. Results: Patients with poor CCC exhibited significantly higher RCII values compared with the good CCC cohort (19.7 ± 4.7 vs. 6.5 ± 2.4, p < 0.001). Following multivariable adjustment, higher RCII remained independently associated with poor collateralization (OR 1.120, 95% CI 1.052-1.199; p < 0.001), alongside right coronary artery (RCA) CTO and the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII). RCII showed discriminative ability for poor CCC (AUC 0.792, 95% CI 0.745-0.835; p < 0.001), which was greater than that of remnant cholesterol, hs-CRP, or SII considered separately. In this cohort, an RCII threshold above 12.3 identified poor CCC with 80% sensitivity and 71% specificity. Conclusions: In this retrospective cohort, higher RCII was independently associated with inadequate coronary collateralization in the setting of CTO. RCII may represent a candidate marker of the combined residual lipid and inflammatory burden; prospective studies and external validation, together with formal assessment of clinical utility, are required before any clinical application can be considered.
title: The Relationship Between the Remnant Cholesterol Inflammation Index and Coronary Collateral Circulation in Patients with Chronic Total Occlusion.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Low-flow time (LFT) is a major prognostic factor in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR), but chronological LFT may not fully reflect ischemic burden when transient return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) occurs. We investigated whether the association between transient ROSC and outcomes varies according to LFT. Methods: This nationwide retrospective cohort study included 810 adults with witnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest who underwent ECPR. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge, and the secondary outcome was good neurological outcome. A prespecified subgroup analysis compared LFT ≤90 versus >90 min, followed by an exploratory analysis using <60, 60-90, and >90 min categories. Multivariable logistic regression and interaction analyses were performed. Results: Among 810 patients, 450 (55.6%) experienced transient ROSC. In the prespecified analysis, transient ROSC was associated with survival in patients with LFT ≤90 min (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 2.375; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.076-5.241; p = 0.032), but not in those with LFT >90 min (AOR, 0.884; 95% CI, 0.595-1.315; p = 0.543), with a significant interaction (p = 0.036). The exploratory three-category analysis showed a significant association in the 60-90-min subgroup (AOR, 3.399; 95% CI, 1.021-11.316; p = 0.046), although the global interaction was not significant (p = 0.126). No significant interaction was observed for good neurological outcome. The prespecified survival interaction remained significant in sensitivity analyses. Conclusions: The association between transient ROSC and survival after ECPR differed according to LFT using the prespecified 90-min cutoff. Transient ROSC may provide prognostic information complementary to chronological LFT, whereas the three-category findings should be considered exploratory.
title: Prognostic Impact of Transient Return of Spontaneous Circulation According to Low-Flow Time in Patients with Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Undergoing Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation: A Nationwide Cohort Study.

abstract: Cardiac computed tomography (CCT) has emerged as a central imaging modality in the workflow for left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), as accurate anatomical assessment is vital for successful intervention. CCT provides superior three-dimensional (3D) anatomical detail and isotropic spatial resolution compared to traditional trans-esophageal echocardiography, enabling precise pre-procedural planning, device sizing, and identification of optimal fluoroscopic projections.
