abstract:
PURPOSE: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a frequent complication in patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG), which can cause deterioration of renal function and adverse clinical outcomes. This study aimed to explore the relationships between the hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score and CA-AKI risk, as well as all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients undergoing CAG.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study enrolled patients undergoing CAG, including those receiving concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and stratified them according to the quartiles of the HALP score. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between HALP score and CA-AKI, and the Cox regression model was adopted to evaluate the relationship between HALP score and mortality.
RESULTS: This study included 42554 patients undergoing CAG. Among these, 5130 patients (12.1%) experienced CA-AKI. HALP score showed a significant inverse association with CA-AKI, with lower HALP score linked to higher CA-AKI risk. After adjusting for all the potential confounding variables, participants in the highest quartile of HALP score had the lowest risk of CA-AKI (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.73-0.90, p < 0.001). In Cox regression models, patients undergoing CAG with the highest HALP score exhibited the lowest risks of all-cause mortality (HR=0.65, 95% CI: 0.60-0.70, p < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality. (HR=0.65, 95% CI: 0.58-0.73, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The HALP score was independently associated with CA-AKI, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular mortality among patients undergoing CAG.
title: Association of the Hemoglobin, Albumin, Lymphocyte, and Platelet Score with Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury and Mortality in Patients Underwent Coronary Angiography: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.

abstract: Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) enables advanced micron-scale characterization of biological tissues. However, its quantitative diagnostic utility is fundamentally limited by the presence of speckle and associated polarimetric noise. Conventional spatial filtering techniques suppress speckle effects yet compromise spatial resolution and can introduce severe coordinate-transformation artifacts in catheter-based applications. To address these challenges, we present the Retardance2Retardance (R2R) network, a physics-constrained, self-supervised deep learning framework for robust polarimetric speckle suppression. R2R exploits spectral binning to obtain independent speckle realizations from existing data and train the model in a Noise2Noise fashion without ground truth. A physics-informed regularization in the loss function enforces that the denoised polarization effects correspond to retardance. Additionally, a physics-informed data augmentation (PIDA) strategy prevents the network from overfitting to the static polarimetric system effects inherent to the training data. Applied to independent human coronary artery pullbacks acquired in vivo, R2R effectively suppresses speckle-induced polarimetric noise while preserving fine polarimetric features. Furthermore, the model demonstrates robust generalization to unseen complex intravascular structures, including bifurcations and deployed stents. Our R2R framework establishes a highly adaptable approach for high-fidelity, quantitative PS-OCT, including intravascular polarimetry, through effective polarimetry noise suppression and better preservation of spatial resolution.
title: Retardance2Retardance: unsupervised denoising for polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography.

abstract: This review describes ventriculo-arterial coupling (VAC), its clinical relevance and how to access it at the bedside. VAC refers to the interaction between the contractility of the ejecting ventricles and the load exerted by the arteries. It integrates cardiac performance with the properties of the vascular system to assess cardiovascular efficiency and workload ending in a stroke volume and energy required to create that work. This relationship is quantitatively expressed as the ratio between arterial elastance (Ea) and end-systolic ventricular elastance (Ees). VAC offers valuable insights into hemodynamic status that go beyond traditional parameters like blood pressure, stroke volume or ejection fraction and independently predicts outcome from critical illness. Optimal VAC reflects maximal efficiency of stroke work and preserved cardiovascular reserve, while uncoupling indicates impaired reserve and is associated with worse prognosis. Uncoupling can occur in both acute and chronic settings, can affect either the right ventricle and pulmonary circulation or left ventricle and systemic circulation or both, and is observed across most forms of shock. While VAC has traditionally been analyzed through invasive pressure-volume methods, it can now be approximated at the bedside using echocardiography and simplified elastance calculations. These approaches allow for dynamic assessments of therapeutic interventions, including fluids, vasopressors, inotropes, and mechanical circulatory support. By incorporating VAC into clinical practice, healthcare professionals can enhance hemodynamic phenotyping and support individualized, physiology-guided management of critically ill patients.
title: Clinical relevance of ventriculo-arterial coupling and how to assess it at the bedside.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perivascular fat attenuation index (FAI) derived from coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a novel imaging biomarker of coronary inflammation. However, its incremental value in predicting functional myocardial ischemia, defined by CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR), beyond traditional cardiovascular risk factors and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume remains unclear.
METHODS: A total of 380 consecutive patients who underwent clinically indicated CCTA with CT-FFR evaluation were retrospectively analyzed. Functional ischemia was defined as CT-FFR ≤0.80. Patients were stratified into low and high FAI groups based on the optimal cutoff value of -81.32 Hounsfield Units (HU). Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of ischemia. The incremental diagnostic performance of adding FAI to a baseline clinical model was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Despite comparable baseline profiles for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, body mass index, and glycemic status (P > 0.05), patients in the high FAI group exhibited significantly lower CT-FFR values (0.75 ± 0.13 vs. 0.79 ± 0.12, P = 0.0017). After adjusting for age, gender, traditional cardiovascular risk factors, and EAT volume, average FAI remained a robust independent predictor of functional ischemia [Adjusted Odds Ratio [OR]: 1.056 per 1 HU increase; 95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 1.019-1.096; P = 0.004]. Notably, EAT volume did not reach statistical significance in the multivariate model (P = 0.584). The addition of FAI to the clinical model resulted in a modest, non-significant improvement in AUC (0.731 vs. 0.707, P = 0.087), but yielded significant improvement in risk reclassification (continuous NRI: 0.339, P = 0.001; IDI: 0.024, P = 0.002). Subgroup analysis demonstrated a consistent risk trend across varying degrees of stenosis, age, and body mass index categories (OR range: 1.03-1.07). DCA confirmed superior net clinical benefit for the FAI-integrated model across a wide threshold probability range (25%-75%).
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary perivascular FAI is an independent imaging marker for CT-FFR-defined functional ischemia and provides incremental value beyond traditional risk factors and EAT volume. These findings support FAI as a non-invasive marker of coronary inflammation that may refine risk stratification for functionally significant coronary artery disease. However, as CT-FFR mainly reflects epicardial physiology, the association between FAI and microvascular dysfunction remains to be determined.
title: Perivascular fat attenuation index improves the identification of functional myocardial ischemia beyond traditional risk factors: a coronary CT angiography-derived fractional flow reserve study.

abstract: Patients with cardiogenic shock and severe structural heart disease may poorly tolerate both general and neuraxial anesthesia. In selected cases, peripheral nerve blockade may reduce hemodynamic disturbance, but the block must be reliable when pain, sympathetic stimulation, or emergency conversion to general anesthesia could be poorly tolerated. We report a 62-year-old woman with cardiogenic shock, low-flow, low-gradient severe aortic stenosis, advanced dilated cardiomyopathy, pulmonary edema, orthopnea, and active femoral bleeding who required urgent femoral artery and vein repair. General anesthesia and neuraxial anesthesia were considered hazardous. Hematoma and anasarca distorted the femoral anatomy and prevented direct femoral nerve visualization. Combined ultrasound guidance and nerve stimulation were used to support safe needle advancement and functional nerve localization. Surgery proceeded with minimal sedation and without escalation of vasoactive support. This case highlights the role of reliability-focused peripheral nerve blockade when conventional anesthetic options are high risk and regional anatomy is distorted.
title: Achieving Reliable Peripheral Nerve Blockade in Cardiogenic Shock With Distorted Femoral Anatomy: A Case Report.

abstract: Delirium and aphasia exhibit overlapping clinical features, complicating the diagnosis of acute neurological disturbances in older adults. Both conditions impair communication and orientation, leading to incoherence; however, they arise from distinct pathophysiological mechanisms and require different management strategies. This case concerns an 83-year-old woman with a 48-hour history of acute-onset confusion and abnormal speech. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed an acute infarct in the inferior division of the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory, with cardioembolism considered the likely cause. Initial assessment attributed her fluent but semantically meaningless speech, inattention, and fluctuating responsiveness to hyperactive or mixed delirium superimposed on probable pre-existing cognitive impairment. New-onset atrial fibrillation (AF) with a controlled ventricular rate was identified, along with elevated high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I concentrations (1026.3 and 1060.5 ng/L) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (7451 pg/mL) in the context of severe ventricular dysfunction. Treatment for possible acute coronary syndrome was initiated but discontinued after cardiology review. Persistent and stereotyped language abnormalities prompted systematic neurological re-evaluation, which identified a Wernicke-type aphasia profile. Computed tomography (CT) of the head demonstrated a left parietotemporal infarct. Given the 48-hour clinical presentation, MRI was performed to further characterise the lesion and revealed left temporal diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) hyperintensity with corresponding apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) hypointensity, confirming acute restricted diffusion in the left temporal lobe. The MRI abnormality corresponded anatomically with the left temporal component of the CT finding, although movement artefact prevented precise lesion co-registration. Echocardiography demonstrated severe biventricular dysfunction with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 15% to 20%. This case underscores the clinical risks of misattributing a structured language disorder to delirium and highlights the importance of focused neurological assessment, including systematic language evaluation, in all older adults presenting with acute confusion.
title: The Mask of Delirium: Uncovering a Presumed Cardioembolic Stroke Through Comprehensive Clinical Evaluation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) combined with diabetes mellitus (DM) significantly increases the risk of vascular restenosis following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Despite advancements in stent technology, restenosis remains a concern, especially in diabetic patients. This study aims to predict restenosis risk using serum metabolites and risk factors.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 272 CAD and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients who underwent PCI between January 2020 and June 2023. Based on one-year angiographic follow-up, patients were divided into restenosis (n = 121) and non-restenosis groups (n = 151). Serum metabolites and biomarkers, including glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), were evaluated, together with procedure-related characteristics (including stent type and post-procedural percentage diameter stenosis) and medication use (including calcium antagonists). Logistic regression and correlation analysis identified significant predictors, and a nomogram prediction model was developed and internally validated using bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Lower HbA1c levels were associated with restenosis (rho = -0.142, P = 0.008; OR = 0.767, 95% CI [0.625-0.941]). Higher levels of IGF-I (rho = 0.328, P < 0.001; OR = 1.053, 95% CI [1.032-1.075]), LDL-C (r = 0.135, P = 0.025; OR = 1.682, 95% CI [1.107-2.555]), TNF-α (r = 0.172, P = 0.004; OR = 1.434, 95% CI [1.119-1.838]), and hsCRP (r = 0.179, P = 0.003; OR = 1.786, 95% CI [1.185-2.693]) were also significantly associated. Non-drug-eluting stents (DES) and higher percentage diameter stenosis (%DS) increased restenosis risk. Calcium antagonists use was negatively correlated with restenosis (r = - 0.185, P = 0.002; OR = 0.449, 95% CI [0.228-0.884]). The nomogram model demonstrated good discrimination for restenosis (apparent AUC = 0.833; bootstrap-corrected AUC = 0.808).
CONCLUSION: This study identified key predictive factors for post-PCI restenosis in CAD patients with DM through case-control analysis. The nomogram model showed good discrimination on internal bootstrap validation. Pending external validation, it may provide a useful exploratory tool to support risk stratification and inform management aimed at reducing the restenosis burden in high-risk cardiovascular populations.
title: Nomogram for predicting post-percutaneous coronary intervention restenosis in patients with coronary artery disease and diabetes: a retrospective study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular manifestations of thyrotoxicosis are common, typically presenting as tachyarrhythmias or high-output physiology. Coronary artery spasm (CAS) is an uncommon but increasingly recognized complication, usually causing transient ischaemia rather than malignant ventricular arrhythmias. Cardiac arrest due to thyrotoxicosis-induced CAS is exceedingly rare. Early recognition is vital because management differs from that of typical acute coronary syndromes (ACS).
CASE SUMMARY: A 63-year-old man suffered an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with an initial shockable rhythm, achieving return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after a single defibrillation. Initial evaluation revealed inferior ST-segment elevation, leading to urgent coronary angiography, which demonstrated severe right coronary artery spasm that resolved after intracoronary nitrate administration. Laboratory studies confirmed significant hyperthyroidism, and recurrent ST-segment changes in the intensive care unit further supported thyrotoxicosis-induced CAS as the underlying mechanism. The patient made a full neurological and cardiac recovery following temperature management, intensification of antithyroid therapy, and vasodilator treatment.
DISCUSSION: This case underscored an unusual presentation of cardiac arrest triggered by thyrotoxicosis-related CAS in the absence of underlying coronary artery disease. Elevated thyroid hormone levels can impair endothelial function and heighten vascular smooth muscle reactivity, creating a predisposition to diffuse, therapy-resistant vasospasm. Recognizing this reversible yet potentially fatal condition is crucial, as prompt initiation of antithyroid therapy and vasodilators can rapidly alleviate ischaemia and reduce the risk of recurrence. The favourable outcome in this patient illustrates how early identification of the underlying cause can guide swift and effective management.
title: Cardiac arrest as the first sign of thyrotoxicosis: a case report of angiographically proven coronary vasospasm.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extrinsic compression of the left main (LM) coronary artery by an aortic root pseudoaneurysm is an exceedingly rare but life-threatening cause of acute coronary syndrome following aortic valve surgery. Multimodality imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning.
CASE SUMMARY: A 52-year-old male underwent mechanical aortic valve replacement and aortic root reconstruction for infective endocarditis complicated by a 23 mm aortic root abscess. Following initial recovery, he re-presented 2 months later with persistent chest pain on a background of 10 days of intermittent symptoms, with anterior-lateral ischaemic changes on electrocardiography (ECG). Computed tomography (CT) aortography excluded dissection but was not formally reported. In the catheterization laboratory, fluoroscopy revealed abnormal prosthetic valve rocking consistent with dehiscence. Coronary angiography demonstrated absent antegrade flow in the left anterior descending artery, impaired flow in the left circumflex artery, and a pulsatile, systole-predominant LM lesion strongly suggesting extrinsic compression. No percutaneous intervention was performed. Urgent formal CT review confirmed a 5.2 × 4.4 × 4.0 cm left ventricular outflow tract pseudoaneurysm with the LM coursing within its fold and apparent systolic occlusion. Serial ECGs showed gradual improvement, supporting a dynamic mechanism. After multidisciplinary review, the patient underwent successful composite graft replacement and pseudoaneurysm repair at a quaternary centre, with full recovery at 4-month follow-up.
DISCUSSION: This case illustrates three key lessons: the dynamic, systole-predominant angiographic hallmark of extrinsic LM compression distinguishes it from fixed atherosclerotic disease and prevents inappropriate percutaneous intervention; dynamic angiography and CT play complementary roles, and single-phase systolic CT may, in this setting, overestimate the severity of LM occlusion; and early referral to a specialist quaternary surgical centre is essential for definitive repair.
title: Dynamic left main occlusion after aortic valve surgery: recognizing extrinsic compression by aortic root pseudoaneurysm-a case report.

abstract:
AIMS: Right-to-left (R-L) shunting through an iatrogenic atrial septal defect (iASD) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication. We aimed to identify factors associated with clinically relevant R-L shunting requiring emergency iASD closure.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analysed 444 consecutive patients undergoing successful M-TEER between 2017 and 2026. Clinical, echocardiographic, and invasive haemodynamic parameters were compared between patients requiring emergency iASD closure and the remaining cohort. Six patients (1.3%) required emergency iASD closure due to R-L shunting and acute deoxygenation. All presented with severe tricuspid regurgitation, RV dilatation, and impaired RV function. Following M-TEER, right atrial pressure exceeded left atrial pressure in five patients. Compared with controls, affected patients demonstrated reduced tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (15 ± 2 vs. 19 ± 4 mm), fractional area change (FAC) (27 ± 5% vs. 43 ± 6%), and RV free wall strain (-13 ± 2% vs. -22 ± 5%). Echocardiography underestimated invasively measured systolic pulmonary artery pressure (25.8 vs. 40.3 mmHg; P = 0.035). Oxygen saturation decreased by 3-8%, with one patient developing cardiogenic shock.
CONCLUSION: Severe tricuspid regurgitation, RV dysfunction, and elevated right atrial pressure may identify patients at risk for clinically relevant R-L shunting after M-TEER. Comprehensive RV assessment, including FAC and strain, combined with invasive hemodynamic evaluation, may improve risk stratification and facilitate timely iASD closure.
journal: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
journal_abbrev: Eur Heart J Imaging Methods Pract
title: Acute deoxygenation during M-TEER: a note of caution.

abstract: Missouri's rural health needs are inseparable from cardiovascular health. Nearly one-quarter of Missourians live in nonmetro areas, where rural hospitals, clinics, community health centers, emergency medical services agencies, public health departments, and community organizations anchor care. Yet heart disease is the leading cause of death in Missouri; the 20 counties with the highest heart disease death rates are rural; and recent data show higher rural heart disease and stroke mortality than urban Missouri. Cardiovascular risk is shaped by clinical care, primary care access, transportation, insurance, broadband, food security, medication affordability, and specialty referral networks. Missouri has building blocks: critical access hospitals, rural clinics, federally qualified health centers, the Misouri Time Critical Diagnosis System for STelevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and stroke, heart disease and stroke prevention program, workforce recruitment programs, and rural health transformation initiatives. This article proposes a rural cardiovascular agenda centered on prevention, urgent treatment, recovery, and community-level coordination.
title: Rural Cardiovascular Health in Missouri: Needs, Care Gaps, and Resources for a More Connected System.

abstract: This systematic review synthesizes the randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence for tocilizumab, an interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor antagonist, as an adjunctive therapy in acute coronary syndrome (ACS). IL-6 is a central mediator of the inflammatory response that follows myocardial infarction and contributes to ischemia-reperfusion injury, positioning its blockade as a plausible cardioprotective strategy. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidance, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Scopus for RCTs of tocilizumab administered during the acute phase of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) versus placebo or standard of care; risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. Given the substantial heterogeneity in population, dosing, and primary endpoints, findings were synthesized narratively rather than pooled. Four trials comprising 439 analyzed patients met the eligibility criteria, spanning NSTEMI and STEMI populations and both intravenous and subcutaneous dosing regimens, one of which was stopped early for futility. In the three intravenously dosed trials, tocilizumab more than halved the C-reactive protein area under the curve relative to placebo (all p < 0.001), with two trials also showing lower troponin release. One trial additionally demonstrated a significant improvement in myocardial salvage index and reduced microvascular obstruction on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI), without significant benefit on the final infarct size or six-month clinical outcomes; a separate, higher-risk trial found no significant benefit on infarct size, troponin, or neurohormonal activation despite comparable suppression of inflammation. Major adverse cardiac events did not differ significantly between arms in either trial assessing this endpoint, and the smallest, subcutaneously dosed trial raised an unreplicated cardiac tamponade signal. Two of the four trials were judged overall low risk of bias. Tocilizumab consistently attenuates the acute inflammatory response and, in one trial, improves imaging surrogates of myocardial salvage, but evidence for clinical benefit is absent, and the trial base remains too small and heterogeneous to support meta-analytic pooling or practice change. Larger, adequately powered trials with harmonized endpoints and blinded safety adjudication are needed.
title: Tocilizumab in Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.

abstract: Patients with concurrent trauma-related surgical emergencies and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (MI) present a unique anesthetic challenge, as damage control surgery and rapid resuscitation must take priority over timely coronary revascularization. During these surgeries, the physiologic insult from general anesthesia can be detrimental to a failing heart, so regional anesthesia techniques and their implications in trauma should be considered. We present a 62-year-old male motorcyclist with hypertension, diabetes, and coronary artery disease and a history of percutaneous coronary intervention who was hit by a car and presented with traumatic partial amputation of the left leg. The patient was brought to the operating room for a left below-knee amputation, and ST-segment elevation in lead II was noted. A 12-lead electrocardiogram showed elevations in II, III, and aVF. We discussed the need for surgery and proceeded with regional anesthesia via left femoral and lateral popliteal sciatic nerve blocks. After surgery, angiography in the cardiac catheterization suite revealed total thrombotic occlusion of the right coronary artery. Cardiology performed thrombectomy, angioplasty, and stent placement. Throughout the hospital course, the patient required multiple incision and drainage procedures, an above-knee amputation, and a second revascularization, all under regional anesthesia. He was eventually discharged to acute rehabilitation. This case underscores the value of damage control surgery and rapid resuscitation, which are paramount for trauma patients with perioperative MIs prior to coronary revascularization. The ability to proceed with regional techniques to avoid the physiologic insult of general anesthesia is invaluable. There are unique considerations for regional anesthesia in trauma patients, such as consent and communication, positioning limitations, coagulopathies, unknown history, and risk of compartment syndrome and infection.
title: Successful Use of Peripheral Nerve Blocks for Emergent Trauma Surgery in a Patient With Perioperative Myocardial Infarction: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) remains high in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Existing risk prediction tools mostly focus on preoperative baseline indicators and ignore intraoperative interventional parameters, lacking comprehensive postprocedural risk assessment tools for STEMI patients after PCI. This study is aimed at developing and internally validating a logistic regression prediction model for post-PCI in-hospital MACE in STEMI patients based on multidimensional perioperative clinical indicators, so as to realize accurate postoperative risk stratification and guide individualized perioperative management.
METHODS: We retrospectively included 1195 STEMI patients who underwent emergency PCI at the Chest Pain Center of Lu'an People's Hospital from January 2019 to October 2024. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 837) and validation (n = 358) sets at a 7:3 ratio. The primary endpoint was in-hospital MACE (composite of cardiogenic shock, malignant arrhythmias, acute heart failure, reinfarction, or all-cause death). A prediction model was constructed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression combined with multivariate logistic regression. Model discrimination was evaluated via the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Head-to-head discriminative comparison with the widely used GRACE and TIMI risk scores was performed using AUC values and the DeLong test to quantify the incremental predictive value of the novel model. Model calibration and clinical utility were assessed via calibration plots, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and decision curve analysis (DCA), with internal validation performed in the validation set.
RESULTS: A total of 260 patients (21.8%) experienced in-hospital MACE. After LASSO regression screening and multivariate logistic regression analysis, eight independent predictors were identified: admission systolic blood pressure, Killip classification, intervention duration, contrast volume, postprocedural TIMI flow grade, culprit vessel occlusion, serum creatinine, and serum potassium. The training set AUC was 0.84 (95% CI: 0.80-0.87) with a sensitivity of 77.7% and specificity of 78.2%; the validation set AUC was 0.826 (95% CI: 0.782-0.870). Comparative discriminative analysis showed that the traditional GRACE and TIMI risk scores exhibited moderate predictive performance. The training set AUC of the GRACE score was 0.763 (95% CI: 0.724-0.800), and that of the TIMI score was 0.748 (95% CI: 0.708-0.786). In the validation set, the AUC of the GRACE score and TIMI score were 0.751 (95% CI: 0.699-0.800) and 0.736 (95% CI: 0.683-0.786), respectively. The DeLong test confirmed that our novel model achieved significantly higher discriminative ability than both GRACE and TIMI scores in both training and validation cohorts (all p < 0.05). The training set Brier score was 0.128, with a calibration intercept of 0.042 and calibration slope of 0.991; the validation set Brier score was 0.135, with a calibration intercept of 0.051 and calibration slope of 0.985. After 1000 bootstrap optimism correction, the corrected calibration slope was 0.987 and the corrected intercept was 0.045. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated good model calibration (χ2 = 5.449, p = 0.709), and DCA demonstrated clinical net benefit within the 5%-80% threshold probability range.
CONCLUSION: The logistic regression prediction model based on eight clinical indicators demonstrated good discrimination, quantitative calibration, and clinical utility for predicting post-PCI in-hospital MACE in STEMI patients. The model integrates preoperative baseline, intraoperative procedural, and laboratory indicators, achieves stable performance after internal validation, and can assist clinicians in postoperative risk stratification of patients, timely identifying high-risk populations after PCI, and optimizing postoperative perioperative management strategies.
title: A Logistic Regression Prediction Model for Post-PCI In-Hospital Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Acute ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Construction and Internal Validation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is the leading cause of pregnancy-associated myocardial infarction and is associated with severe presentations and increased recurrence risk, particularly postpartum.
CASE SUMMARY: A 38-year-old woman with previous conservatively managed left anterior descending artery SCAD presented 9 days postpartum with infero-posterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Coronary angiography demonstrated extensive multisegment right coronary artery SCAD. She remained hemodynamically stable and was managed conservatively with favorable short-term outcomes despite recurrent SCAD.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights pregnancy as a potent trigger for recurrent SCAD and the vulnerability of the early postpartum period. Recurrence occurred despite multidisciplinary management, specialist follow-up, and planned cesarean delivery, underscoring limitations of current risk-mitigation strategies. Despite expert consensus guidance of pregnancy avoidance, both unplanned and planned pregnancies may occur after SCAD; comprehensive counseling regarding recurrence risk remains essential.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Early postpartum SCAD recurrence may occur despite optimal care and can be unpredictable and life-threatening.
title: Postpartum SCAD After Prior SCAD Despite Comprehensive Multidisciplinary Management.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have reported elevated body temperature following the removal of veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). However, the clinical implications of elevated body temperature after the removal of VA-ECMO remain unknown.
OBJECTIVES: To characterize elevated body temperature after VA-ECMO removal in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS).
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 163 CS patients undergoing VA-ECMO removal. All patients did not exhibit any evidence of infection. Blood temperature was continuously monitored using a Swan-Ganz catheter. Elevated body temperature was defined as a maximum body temperature ≥38.0 °C within 24 h after VA-ECMO removal. All-cause mortality was compared between patients with and without elevated body temperature.
RESULTS: Elevated body temperature was observed in 58.9% (96/163) of study subjects. Patients with elevated body temperature had higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (11.1 ± 8.6 vs. 8.5 ± 6.1 mg/dL, p = 0.027), accompanied by reductions in systolic blood pressure and systemic vascular resistance, and increased lactate levels. CRP levels independently predicted elevated body temperature (OR=1.050, 95%CI=1.003-1.100, p = 0.037). All-cause mortality did not differ between the two groups (30.2%vs. 29.9%, log-rank p = 0.983). However, among patients with elevated body temperature, an increase in body temperature, especially ≥1.1 °C, was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR=1.968, 95%CI=1.096-3.535, p = 0.023).
CONCLUSIONS: In CS patients requiring VA-ECMO, body temperature elevated in 58.9% patients after the removal of VA-ECMO. In those with elevated body temperature, a greater rise in body temperature was associated with higher mortality, suggesting body temperature as a potential signature to stratify risks of mortality in CS patients without any infectious signs.
journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
title: Clinical significance of elevated body temperature without infection following removal of VA-ECMO.

abstract: Interventional therapy has, as a minimally invasive approach, been widely adopted for treating cardiovascular diseases, particularly structural heart disease, where occluders play a pivotal role in transcatheter closure. This paper comprehensively reviews the evolutionary trajectory and emerging frontiers of cardiovascular occluders, beginning with their interventional applications in congenital heart defects (atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, patent foramen ovale, and patent ductus arteriosus) and left atrial appendage closure. The focus then shifts to occluder materials and design principles, tracing the progression from early non-degradable metals like stainless steel to the current gold standard, nitinol, whose hyperelasticity enables self-expanding devices. To promote rapid endothelialization on nitinol implants, surface nanocoatings of bioceramics such as titanium nitride have been developed to modulate cell-material interactions. To eliminate risks from permanent metallic implants, biodegradable occluders have emerged as an alternative. The design of biodegradable occluders utilizing medical polymers such as polylactic acid and polydioxanone is illustrated, highlighting structural innovations such as locking strategies to overcome the lack of hyperelasticity. Key considerations including matching degradation rate with tissue regeneration and achieving X-ray visibility are also described. Finally, future perspectives are presented: expanding applications to infants and the elderly, incorporating tissue engineering for in situ regeneration, and leveraging nanotechnology and artificial intelligence to optimize device performance. The ongoing advancement of occluder technologies will propel interventional therapy for structural heart disease toward a safer and more effective treatment.
title: Polymeric and metallic occluders for interventional therapy of cardiovascular diseases.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index integrates systemic inflammation, nutritional status, and immune function. We investigated its association with angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AMR)-defined coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and performed an exploratory statistical mediation analysis involving estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR).
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study included 456 consecutive patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI. AMR-defined CMD was prespecified as AMR ≥250 mmHg·s/m. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), and prespecified subgroup analyses were performed. Sensitivity and exploratory mediation analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: AMR-defined CMD was present in 228 patients (50.0%). In Model 3, each doubling of CALLY was associated with lower odds of AMR-defined CMD (OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.80-0.94; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, Q3 and Q4 were associated with 44% (OR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.32-0.97; P = 0.037) and 52% (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.28-0.84; P = 0.010) lower odds, respectively (P for trend = 0.018). RCS analysis showed an overall association (P = 0.001) without evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.310). No significant subgroup interactions were observed. Exploratory mediation analysis estimated that eGDR statistically accounted for 15.47% of the observed association.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher CALLY values were inversely associated with AMR-defined CMD after primary PCI for STEMI. eGDR may account for part of this association. CALLY may serve as an auxiliary marker for AMR-defined CMD risk stratification, pending prospective multicenter validation.
title: C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index and coronary microvascular dysfunction after primary percutaneous coronary intervention: The mediating role of insulin resistance.

abstract: Citicoline (CDP-choline) is a rate-limiting precursor for phosphatidylcholine synthesis and acetylcholine production, and thus a unique metabolic hub linking membrane phospholipid homeostasis with cholinergic signaling. The biochemical rationale for the therapeutic potential of citicoline in heart disease is rooted in fundamental metabolic principles and conserved cytoprotective pathways. However, the cardiovascular evidence base for citicoline is not as extensive as its established neuroprotective profile. The cardioprotection is mainly mediated by the cholinergic system, including vagal efferent activity and the non-neuronal cardiac cholinergic system (NNCCS). This initiates a wide signaling network including PI3K/AKT, JAK/STAT, SIRT3/AMPK, IP3/calcium and MAPK cascades that inhibit inflammation, oxidative stress and apoptosis. Moreover, cholinergic signaling modulates proteasomal activity and microRNA expression, as well as post-transcriptional gene regulation to provide cardioprotection. This review summarizes experimental and clinical evidence in support of this hypothesis with particular emphasis on citicoline-activated mechanisms that are directly relevant for myocardial protection. These include phospholipid replacement of damaged sarcolemmal membranes and pleiotropic actions such as activation of survival kinase activation, suppression of inflammatory mediators, attenuation of oxidative injury and preservation of mitochondrial bioenergetics. Based on these safety data, we recommend that citicoline should be tested in further translational studies as an adjunctive treatment during reperfusion following myocardial infarction. Its antiarrhythmic effects, cholinergic engagement, downstream signaling modulation and miRNA regulation should be specifically highlighted as these may help limit infarct size, prevent adverse remodeling and improve clinical outcome in ischemic heart disease.
title: Citicoline in cardiovascular protection: mechanistic roles of choline and acetylcholine.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of continuous bilateral lower-limb near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) monitoring as an adjunct to standard hourly neurovascular assessment (NVA) in patients receiving intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, and to characterize the relationship between regional oxygen saturation (rSO₂) and in-hospital mortality.
DESIGN: Prospective observational cohort study.
SETTING: Cardiac care unit of a tertiary cardiac center (Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Singapore).
PARTICIPANTS: Fifty consecutive adult patients receiving IABP support via femoral arterial access.
INTERVENTIONS: Continuous bilateral lower-limb rSO₂ monitoring using NIRS was performed throughout IABP support, alongside standardized hourly NVA of both limbs (capillary refill time, skin color, temperature, pulse quality, and Doppler signal).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Right femoral access was used in 94% of patients (47 of 50). Minimum contralateral (left) rSO₂ was significantly lower in nonsurvivors than survivors (29.3% ± 17.6% v 43.3% ± 14.4%, p = 0.024), with a directionally similar but nonsignificant trend on the ipsilateral (right) side (p = 0.083). Regional oxygen saturation correlated moderately with capillary refill time (Spearman rank correlation [rs] ≈ 0.50) and pulse quality (rs ≈ 0.38) bilaterally but not with temperature change, which deteriorated in >92% of limbs. Low rSO₂ (<40%) in either limb was associated with a nonsignificant 3.16-fold increase in mortality odds (95% confidence interval, 0.55-18.11; p = 0.197). No patient developed acute limb ischemia. Sepsis (odds ratio [OR], 13.0) and renal replacement therapy (OR, 7.1) were the only statistically significant predictors of mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Continuous bilateral lower-limb rSO₂ monitoring is feasible throughout IABP support and produces a physiologically coherent signal that correlates moderately with objective NVA parameters and is lower in patients who do not survive to discharge. No limb ischemic events occurred; these findings are best regarded as feasibility and physiology data rather than evidence that continuous monitoring improves limb outcomes, and they warrant confirmation in a larger, multicenter study.
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
title: Continuous Bilateral Lower-Limb Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Monitoring in Patients on Intra-aortic Balloon Pump Support: A Prospective Feasibility and Physiology Study.

abstract:
AIMS: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves cardiovascular outcomes after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but access remains suboptimal. Telerehabilitation may overcome barriers, yet evidence from real-world, public health systems is limited. This randomized controlled trial study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured telerehabilitation programme compared with standard centre-based CR in patients after ACS, focussing on cardiovascular risk factor control and lifestyle adherence.
METHODS AND RESULTS: TELECOR is a pragmatic, open-label, randomized trial conducted at a tertiary public hospital. Adults with recent ACS were randomized 1:1 to an 8 week structured telerehabilitation or a centre-based CR programme. The primary outcome was achievement of a composite target (≥4 of 7 predefined cardiovascular and lifestyle goals) at 8 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in functional capacity, medication adherence, quality of life, psychological status, satisfaction, and cardiovascular events at 6 months. A total of 129 patients were randomized (65 telerehabilitation, 64 centre-based). At 8 weeks, 86% of telerehabilitation vs. 79.7% of centre-based participants met the composite target (P = 0.37). At 6 months, this was 87% vs. 80.4% (P = 0.34). Both groups showed similar improvements in functional capacity (≈+1 metabolic equivalent of tasks), adherence (>84%), and satisfaction (>91/100). No between-group differences were observed in clinical events or psychological outcomes.
CONCLUSION: In a real-world public hospital setting, telerehabilitation was non-inferior to conventional CR in achieving cardiovascular risk factor control and improving functional capacity. These results support the broader integration of digital CR models into routine secondary prevention care.
title: Telerehabilitation vs. centre-based cardiac rehabilitation after acute coronary syndrome: results of the pragmatic TELECOR randomized trial.

abstract: Left ventricular thrombus (LVT) is a significant complication of myocardial infarction, associated with increased morbidity and mortality because of the risk of systemic embolization and stroke. Early detection of LVT is therefore important for the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared the diagnostic accuracy of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) for the detection of LVT. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Cochrane, CNKI, Scopus, LILACS, Web of Science, Google Scholar, EMBASE, and CINAHL were searched. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed in R (v3.4.3), with pooled proportions or area under the curve (AUC) values reported alongside 95% confidence intervals, and heterogeneity assessed using the I² statistic. Eighteen studies involving 3478 participants met the inclusion criteria. Most studies contributed to the primary analysis of TTE performance using CMR as the reference standard, while only five studies allowed direct head-to-head comparison using an independent reference standard. In the head-to-head analysis, CMR demonstrated higher sensitivity (70.5%, 95% CI: 0.554-0.822) and specificity (99.2%, 95% CI: 0.983-0.997) for detecting LVT compared with TTE, which showed a sensitivity of 31.8% (95% CI: 0.252-0.391) and specificity of 96.3% (95% CI: 0.929-0.981). The AUC for CMR was 0.985 compared with 0.59 for TTE. Heterogeneity was significant for TTE (I² = 75.8%) but low for CMR (I² = 0.0%). Funnel-plot assessment suggested a low likelihood of publication bias. These findings suggest that CMR may provide a diagnostic advantage over TTE for LVT detection, particularly in high-risk patients or when TTE findings are negative or inconclusive. However, this apparent advantage should be interpreted cautiously because most included studies used CMR, particularly late gadolinium enhancement CMR, as the reference standard rather than an independent imaging modality or pathological confirmation, and many studies were historical and used heterogeneous or non-optimized echocardiographic protocols. Further contemporary studies using independent validation standards are needed. Systematic Review Registration: PROSPERO CRD 42024558739.

abstract: Arterial tortuosity syndrome (ATS) is a rare autosomal recessive connective-tissue arteriopathy characterized by diffuse elongation and tortuosity of large and medium-sized arteries. Although it is typically diagnosed during childhood, adult presentation may occur and can be overlooked when overt connective-tissue manifestations are absent; coronary involvement is uncommon but clinically important. A 41-year-old woman presented with a two-week history of exertional substernal chest pain and dyspnea. CT coronary angiography demonstrated marked tortuosity of the left main coronary artery with focal kinking approximately 6.8 mm from its origin and 40-45% luminal stenosis (CAD-RADS 2). Contrast-enhanced CT angiography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis demonstrated generalized arterial elongation and marked tortuosity involving the thoracic aorta, supra-aortic branches, and abdominal aortic branches, together with early branching of the main pulmonary artery, without aneurysm, dissection, or intramural hematoma. Conventional coronary angiography was technically unsuccessful because of severe arterial tortuosity, with unsuccessful catheter advancement and coronary engagement despite radial and subsequent femoral access. The overall clinical and imaging findings were highly suggestive of ATS with coronary involvement, although molecular genetic confirmation was not available. The patient was managed conservatively with vascular risk-factor optimization and structured follow-up, with symptomatic improvement at one month. This case highlights that ATS may present in adulthood with coronary artery tortuosity and focal kinking and emphasizes the importance of recognizing diffuse multi-territory arterial tortuosity on CT. Comprehensive vascular imaging can establish a strong radiological suspicion of ATS, identify coronary involvement and procedural challenges, and guide surveillance even when genetic confirmation is unavailable.
title: Arterial tortuosity syndrome with coronary artery involvement in a middle-aged female: A case report.

abstract: Dedicated venous stents became available in Japan only recently, and reports of their use and follow-up in Japanese practice remain scarce. A 77-year-old woman developed acute left iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) after prolonged recumbency and was treated with edoxaban. Eighteen days later she underwent endovascular therapy of the right lower limb for chronic limb-threatening ischaemia, and aspirin was added. Limb swelling and pain persisted despite three months of anticoagulation and graduated compression, and imaging then showed chronic occlusion of the left common and external iliac veins (EIV) with patent femoral and deep femoral inflow, corresponding to a favourable anatomical category of chronic venous obstruction (CVO). Under intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) guidance, which identified a stenotic distal landing zone in the proximal common femoral vein (CFV) that was not evident on venography, two Venovo venous stents (Becton, Dickinson and Company (BD), Tempe, AZ, USA) were deployed from the common iliac vein (CIV) to the CFV. Symptoms and clinical severity scores improved over the following months. Three months after stenting, duplex surveillance detected a localised mural thrombus along the posterior wall of the stent despite treatment with edoxaban and aspirin; the antiplatelet agent was changed to clopidogrel, yet the thrombus enlarged from 3 to 6 mm over the next six months before reaching a plateau. Nine months after stenting, an occult breast carcinoma was diagnosed incidentally. The stent remained patent at 12 months, through two bleeding events and three interruptions of antithrombotic therapy. This case illustrates one approach to managing an asymptomatic in-stent mural thrombus and raises the possibility that a thrombus forming despite adequate antithrombotic therapy may be an early manifestation of an undiagnosed malignancy.
title: Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided Iliofemoral Venous Stenting: In-Stent Mural Thrombus as a Possible Early Sign of Occult Malignancy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is the most severe manifestation of cardiovascular disease and disproportionately affects South Asians at a younger age than Western populations. Body mass index (BMI) inadequately reflects visceral adiposity, particularly in Indian populations. Obesity phenotypes, which combine BMI with metabolic status, and novel anthropometric indices may improve cardiovascular risk assessment, but data from Indian ACS patients remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between cardiometabolic risk factors, obesity phenotypes, and novel anthropometric indices with ACS, and to quantify these associations using odds ratios (ORs).
METHODS: This case-control study enrolled 50 patients with confirmed ACS (unstable angina, Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), or ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)) and 50 age-, sex-, and weight-matched healthy controls at a tertiary care hospital. Sociodemographic, clinical, anthropometric, and biochemical data were recorded. Participants were classified into four obesity phenotypes - metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW), metabolically healthy overweight/obese (MHO), and metabolically unhealthy overweight/obese (MUO) - based on BMI and presence of hypertension, diabetes, and/or dyslipidemia. Five novel indices were calculated: A body shape index (ABSI), body roundness index (BRI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), and abdominal volume index (AVI). Continuous variables were compared using t-tests and categorical variables using chi-square/Fisher's exact test; unadjusted ORs with 95% CIs were calculated. p<0.05 was significant. ST-elevation myocardial infarction Results: Cases and controls were comparable for age and sex (p>0.05). Hypertension (60% vs 36%), diabetes (52% vs 28%), dyslipidemia (56% vs 32%), and smoking (44% vs 24%) were more common among cases (all p<0.05). Per 1-SD increase, BMI was not significantly associated with ACS (Exp(B) 1.208, 95% CI 0.816-1.790, Wald 0.89, p=0.345), whereas waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and neck circumference were each significantly associated with ACS. Each of the five novel indices was significantly associated with ACS per 1-SD increase (all p<0.001; e.g., WHtR Exp(B) 2.473, 95% CI 1.638-3.732, Wald 18.59); because each index reflects a different geometric construct even when expressed per 1-SD, indices are not ranked by strength of association. Using MHNW as reference, MUO showed significantly increased odds of ACS (OR 3.33, 95% CI 1.10-10.12); MUNW showed a similar point estimate (OR 3.33, 95% CI 0.89-12.49) that did not reach significance (p=0.074), and MHO was not significantly associated with ACS (OR 1.50, 95% CI 0.48-4.65). All ORs are unadjusted.
CONCLUSION: In this unadjusted, cross-sectional comparison, metabolic health and central fat distribution were associated with ACS, whereas BMI was not. Obesity phenotyping and novel anthropometric indices warrant further evaluation in larger, multivariable-adjusted, prospective studies as potential adjuncts to cardiovascular risk stratification in South Asian populations.
title: Cardiometabolic Risk Factors, Obesity Phenotypes, and Novel Anthropometric Indices in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Hospital-Based Case-Control Study in Central India.
Lipoprotein(a), smoking, and diabetes are additive but not interactive risk factors for major adverse cardiovascular events after acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend potent P2Y12 inhibitors over clopidogrel following percutaneous coronary intervention. Whether ticagrelor- or prasugrel-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) provides superior clinical outcomes following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain, particularly across acute coronary syndromes (ACS) and high-risk coronary artery disease (CAD) populations.
METHODS: We searched databases for randomized controlled trials comparing ticagrelor- and prasugrel-based DAPT in patients with CAD undergoing PCI with 1-year follow-up. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, stent thrombosis, and major bleeding. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses were performed in ACS populations.
RESULTS: Three trials randomized a total of 7048 patients. In the primary analysis, prasugrel-based therapy was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in MACE compared with ticagrelor-based therapy (HR = 0.83; 95% CI: 0.67-1.03; p = 0.09). All-cause mortality (HR = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.68-1.08; p = 0.20), cardiovascular death (HR = 0.93; 95% CI: 0.72-1.21; p = 0.60), myocardial infarction (HR = 0.80; 95% CI: 0.56-1.14; p = 0.22), stroke (HR = 1.04; 95% CI: 0.63-1.73; p = 0.87), stent thrombosis (HR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.45-1.11; p = 0.13), and major bleeding (HR = 0.89; 95% CI: 0.68-1.17; p = 0.41) were comparable between strategies. ACS-restricted sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent findings across all outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with ACS and high-risk CAD undergoing PCI, current randomized evidence does not establish conclusive superiority between ticagrelor- and prasugrel-based DAPT for 1-year ischemic or bleeding endpoints.
journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
title: Ticagrelor versus prasugrel following PCI in acute coronary syndromes and high-risk coronary artery disease: A meta-analysis of one-year randomized trial outcomes.

abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Vessel fractional flow reserve (vFFR) allows angiography-based physiological lesion evaluation and virtual percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) simulation, estimating post-PCI vFFR (residual vFFR). While residual vFFR has been validated against invasive post-PCI fractional flow reserve (FFR), its clinical significance remains unclear. To assess the impact of residual vFFR on long-term clinical outcomes.
METHODS: FAST Residual is a post hoc analysis of the FFR SEARCH study including 279 patients with (un)stable angina or non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing angiographically successful PCI. Residual vFFR was calculated based on two pre-procedural angiographic views. The primary endpoint was target vessel failure (TVF) at 5 years, a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI) and target vessel revascularization (TVR).
RESULTS: Mean age was 64 ± 11 years, 68.5% were men, 23.7% had diabetes, and 43.7% presented with stable angina. Median residual vFFR was 0.92 [IQR 0.87-0.95] and post-PCI FFR was 0.90 [0.85-0.94] (r = 0.509, p < 0.001). The optimal cutoff value of residual vFFR to predict 5-year TVF was <0.90. TVF occurred in 24 (23.3%) patients in the residual vFFR <0.90 group, compared with 16 (9.1%) in the residual vFFR ≥0.90 group (adjusted HR 2.66, 95% CI 1.41-5.04; p = 0.003). This difference was driven by higher rates of TVR [16 (15.5%) vs. 12 (6.8%); adjusted HR 2.33, 95% CI 1.10-4.94; p = 0.027].
CONCLUSIONS: The concept of virtual stenting is a promising tool for predicting clinical outcomes. For the first time, this post hoc analysis showed that patients with residual vFFR <0.90 experienced significantly higher rates of TVF at 5 years.
journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
title: The impact of residual vessel fractional flow reserve on clinical outcomes: The FAST residual study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Young women with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) often present with distinct risk profiles compared with older women and men, but the role of reproductive factors remains poorly understood. This study examines associations of reproductive factors with AMI in young women.
METHODS: We conducted a case-control study of 1561 women aged 18-55 years with AMI from VIRGO and age-matched controls from NHANES. A wide range of reproductive factors were evaluated. Conditional logistic regression estimated odds ratios for AMI, sequentially adjusted for race/ethnicity, socioeconomic variables, and traditional risk factors. Stratified analyses were performed by menopausal status.
RESULTS: Early menarche (<11 years; OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.56-2.73), menopause (OR 1.82, 95% CI 1.50-2.22), gestational diabetes (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.23-2.19), birth control pills use for 1-5 years (OR 1.67, 95% CI 1.36-2.05), and ever use of female hormones (OR 1.99, 95% CI 1.62-2.46) were associated with higher odds of AMI, while first live birth at ≥30 years (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.36-0.69), breastfeeding ≥1 month (OR 0.46, 95% CI 0.38-0.56), and current contraceptive use (OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.32-0.76) were associated with lower odds. After adjustment for traditional risk factors, birth control pills use for 1-5 years (OR 1.71, 95% CI 1.25-2.34) and female hormone use (OR 1.75, 95% CI 1.28-2.38) remained significantly associated. Associations varied by menopausal status.
CONCLUSION: Reproductive factors are associated with early-onset AMI in young women. Recognition of reproductive history may inform prevention strategies in young women.
title: Association of reproductive factors with acute myocardial infarction in young women: A VIRGO and NHANES case-control study.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The totality of atherosclerosis from the coronary tree can be measured with quantitative coronary CT and is increasingly being recognized as important marker for future cardiovascular events. We evaluated the risk and absolute event rates of plaque volume staging systems and provided analyses according to the clinical likelihood of obstructive CAD.
METHODS: CONFIRM2 is an ongoing, global, multicenter, observational registry that included patients with clinically indicated coronary CT angiography and follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Patients without cardiac symptoms and prior CAD were excluded. Atherosclerosis was quantified across all coronary segments by AI-QCT. Total plaque volume (TPV) was categorized into non-calcified plaque (NCPV, HU <350) and calcified (HU>350). The primary end point was the incidence rate of MACE over at 4 years and included all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, congestive heart failure, late revascularizations (occurring >90 days post index CCTA), and hospitalization for unstable angina. Secondary endpoint included Death, MI, and stroke. The prognostic value of TPV and NCPV was evaluated across the pretest likelihood according to the ESC Risk Factor Weighted Likelihood (ESC RF-CL).
RESULTS: A total of 6061 patients (mean age 58.6 ± 12.1 years, 48.6% male) were included and the mean follow-up duration was: 4.4 ± 1.8 years. According to the ESC RF-CL for obstructive CAD, patients were classified as very-low, low, and moderate risk in 36.0%, 43.0%, and 22.0%, and obstructive CAD rates were 6.8%, 15.7%. and 28.2, respectively. Within the total cohort, TPV >0-250, 250-750, and >750 mm3 were associated with MACE: HR 2.5 (95% CI 1.1, 5.6), HR 10.1 (95% CI 4.4, 22.9), and HR 15.9 (95% CI 6.7, 38.0) compared with TPV=0. According to RF-CL very-low, low, and moderate, the MACE rates were: 0.7, 2.9, 0.0% for TPV=0 mm3; 2.3%, 3.6%, 4.6% for TPV >0-250 mm3; 10.3%, 12.3%, 13.5% for TPV 250-750 mm3; and 18.8%, 16.7%, and 19.8% for TPV>750 mm3. Findings were consistent for the secondary endpoint.
CONCLUSION: Among a large cohort of symptomatic patients evaluated by coronary CT angiography, the burden of atherosclerosis by AI-QCT was the main driver for cardiovascular events. Absolute event rates were consistently higher by each plaque volume stage, and consistent across the clinical likelihood subgroups for obstructive CAD. While quantitative atherosclerosis was present in the majority of patients, risk increased significantly from 250 mm3 of TPV during intermediate term follow-up.
title: Whole heart atherosclerosis volume and risk for major adverse cardiovascular events across the clinical likelihood for obstructive CAD; the CONFIRM2 study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although the relationship between smoking and cardiovascular events is well established, it remains uncertain whether the outcomes of noninvasive testing (NIT) influence this relationship and how systemic biomarkers may aid risk stratification in patients presenting with chest pain.
METHODS: This study included PROMISE participants with stable chest pain and available smoking status (current, ever, or never) and NIT results (Positive NIT: ≥70% coronary stenosis on CT angiography or inducible ischemia on stress testing). Smoking was associated with systemic biomarkers (e.g., hsCRP, IL-6, MMP-9), NIT results, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, unstable angina), using regression and mediation models adjusted for traditional cardiovascular risk factors (median follow-up 24.4 months).
RESULTS: Among 9100 individuals (mean age 61±8 years; 53% female), 51% were ever-smokers, including 18% current smokers. Smoking was independently associated with MACE, with positive NIT mediating this relationship (current: 16%; ever: 12%, p ≤ 0.006). Compared with never-smokers, smoking was associated with MACE despite negative NIT (current: aHR 2.41, 95%CI 1.49-3.89; ever: aHR 1.80, 95%CI 1.25-2.59), with the most pronounced differences seen in men vs. women and CV death/MI (sex interaction p = 0.047). Smoking was associated with high levels of inflammatory biomarkers, particularly MMP-9 (+51%; current vs. never-smokers), which partially mediated the smoking-MACE association (current: 25%; ever: 8%, ≤0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Negative NIT does not reduce smoking-associated MACE risk in patients with stable chest pain. Particularly, current smoking confers substantial residual cardiovascular risk, potentially mediated by MMP-9-related matrix remodeling not captured by standard testing, supporting aggressive smoking cessation irrespective of NIT results.
title: Absence of significant coronary artery disease does not eliminate smoking-related cardiovascular risk: insights from the PROMISE trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established independent risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and is traditionally considered stable. Its behavior following acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and clinical implications remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize the temporal trajectory of Lp(a) following ACS, evaluate whether baseline levels predict longitudinal changes, and assess the stability of clinically relevant Lp(a) risk categories.
METHODS: In this prospective study, 225 patients with ACS underwent serial Lp(a) measurements during hospitalization and at follow-up (≥6 months). Longitudinal changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. Associations between baseline Lp(a) and changes over time were evaluated using Spearman correlation. Stability of Lp(a) threshold risk categories (<50, 50-105, ≥105 nmol/L) was assessed by examining transitions across categories.
RESULTS: Lp(a) increased following ACS (p < 0.001), peaking at Days 4-7 (+30.0 %, p = 0.0001) and remaining elevated at Day 30 (+15.0 %, p = 0.0042), before returning to baseline at follow-up. Among individuals with increases in Lp(a), baseline Lp(a) was the strongest determinant of trajectory, with higher levels associated with greater increases at all timepoints (ρ 0.37-0.63, all p < 0.05). Categories for those evels in the low (<50 nmol/L) and high (≥105 nmol/L) categories remained stable with minimal reclassification. Variability was confined to levels in the intermediate range (50-105 nmol/L), where 37.5 % transitioned to ≥105 nmol/L.
CONCLUSIONS: Lp(a) rises transiently after ACS and returns to baseline over time. Levels in the high and low risk categories remain in those categories, while variability is limited to the intermediate range. A single Lp(a) measurement obtained during ACS may be sufficient for individuals with clearly low or markedly elevated Lp(a) levels, whereas repeat testing after clinical stabilization may be considered for patients with intermediate or borderline baseline levels.
title: Temporal changes in lipoprotein(a) after acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional markers of risk such as coronary artery calcium (CAC) scores are lower and less predictive in Black adults, despite a high prevalence of Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and Metabolic Syndrome We evaluated whether incorporation of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) features capture prognostic signal beyond CAC and social deprivation index, in predicting major adverse cardiovascular events.
METHODS: Adults with T2DM undergoing non-contrast CT calcium scoring from the CLARIFY registry (NCT04075162), including 1024 non-Hispanic Black participants and 3072 propensity-matched non-Hispanic White participants were included. EAT was automatically segmented and radiomic features were extracted and selected using survival-based machine learning. Cox proportional hazards models were constructed using CAC, Social Deprivation Index (SDI), and EAT features alone and in combination. The primary endpoint was 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-3P), defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke. Model discrimination, reclassification, and calibration were assessed.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of approximately 5 years, 206 (20%) Black participants and 422 (14%) matched White participants experienced MACE-3P In Black participants, the SDI+CAC+EAT model demonstrated the highest discrimination (C-index 0.62) and significantly improved reclassification compared with CAC alone (NRI) of 0.29 (95% CI 0.15-0.56; p < 0.0007). In contrast, the SDI+CAC+EAT model showed no improvement in discrimination when compared to CAC alone (C-index 0.67 v. 0.67) in the White cohort.
CONCLUSION: In adults with T2DM, EAT may serve as a complimentary imaging marker when combined with CAC scores to provide incremental prognostic information or refine risk characterization.
title: Epicardial adipose tissue radiomics complement calcium scoring in black adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

abstract:
AIM: The benefit of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is strongly time dependent, yet in established in-hospital ECPR systems, including Prague, the median collapse-to-flow time has remained around 60 min or more, dominated by intra-arrest transport. Evidence for prehospital ECPR remains limited, particularly its comparison with in-hospital ECPR. RACE Prague evaluates whether dispatching a mobile cannulation team to the scene shortens this interval within the same ECPR system.
METHODS: Single-centre, prospective, interventional, single-arm pilot feasibility study. Twenty adults aged 18-70 years with witnessed refractory OHCA (three unsuccessful defibrillations and/or ≥10 min of resuscitation in pulseless electrical activity), receive prehospital percutaneous femoro-femoral veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) from a mobile ECPR team. The primary endpoint (time from estimated collapse to ECMO flow ≥2.0 L/min) is tested hierarchically against the historical Prague OHCA in-hospital ECPR cohort (target shortening ≥15 min) and a contemporaneous in-hospital ECPR cohort at the same centre. Secondary endpoints include 30-day survival with favourable neurological outcome assessed blind, decomposition of prehospital pathway intervals, cannulation success, and pre-specified safety endpoints. Enrolment proceeds without prior consent under ethics-approved emergency-research provisions, with deferred consent thereafter.
CONCLUSION: RACE Prague is testing the effect of cannulation location on the time to extracorporeal support and will provide essential evidence on the feasibility of prehospital ECPR.Trial registration:ClinicalTrials.govNCT06789978; Ethics Committee of the General University Hospital in Prague, reference 134/23 S-IV.
title: Prehospital extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a protocol for the Rapid prehospital ACcess to ECPR in Prague (RACE Prague) single-arm pilot feasibility study.
