abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Evidence on CVD subtypes in young Pakistani adults is limited. This study characterized CVD subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
METHODS: A multicentre, cross-sectional study was conducted at four hospitals among patients aged 18-45 years. Data were extracted from three-year hospital records. Associations were assessed using chi-square/Fisher's exact tests and logistic regression.
RESULTS: 8,650 CVD cases, 2,090 (24.2%) were young adults, predominantly male (64.6%), with a median age of 40 years (IQR: 36-44). ACS was the most common subtype (61.0%), followed by cardiomyopathy (39.0%). Overweight/obesity (77.0%), hypertension (56.5%), smoking (39.7%), dyslipidaemia (21.8%), and diabetes (14.4%) were the most prevalent factors. Compared with ACS, cardiomyopathy was independently associated with high heart rate, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes, and family history. Smoking was associated with lower odds of cardiomyopathy than ACS (aOR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.41-0.61, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Young adults accounted for 24.2% of CVD cases, with ACS and cardiomyopathy the most common subtypes, highlighting the need for targeted strategies. The cross-sectional design, findings indicate subtype differences rather than causal effects, while supporting smoking cessation and early hypertension detection in young adults.
title: Patterns of cardiovascular disease subtypes and associated factors among young adults in Peshawar, Pakistan: a multicenter hospital-based cross-sectional study.

abstract: ObjectivesTo compare the clinical characteristics, risk factors, and prognosis of incidental pulmonary embolism (IPE) and symptomatic pulmonary embolism (SPE), and to inform risk-stratified management.MethodsThis retrospective study analyzed 287 patients with hospital-acquired pulmonary embolism (HA-PE). Demographic, clinical, imaging, and laboratory data were collected. Survival outcomes were assessed using Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses.ResultsAmong 287 patients, 87 had IPE and 200 had SPE. IPE was more frequently classified as low-risk PE (63.22% vs. 31.50%, p < 0.001) and more often involved pulmonary artery branches (73.56% vs. 58.00%, p = 0.01), whereas SPE was more commonly intermediate- or high-risk. The 1-month survival rate was higher in the IPE group than in the SPE group (95.4% vs. 75.5%, hazard ratio [HR]: 5.95, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.51 - 16.5, p < 0.001), but this difference was not significant after 1 month. In IPE, cancer and bleeding were associated with increased mortality, whereas anticoagulation and lower PE risk categories were associated with reduced mortality. In SPE, cancer and immobilization were associated with increased mortality, whereas anticoagulation, thrombectomy, and lower PE risk categories were associated with reduced mortality.ConclusionsIPE is generally associated with lower-risk, more peripheral PE, but anticoagulation should be individualized. SPE requires prompt risk stratification and timely anticoagulation, with reperfusion or thrombectomy considered for selected high-risk or deteriorating patients.
title: Clinical characteristics, risk factors, and prognosis of incidental and symptomatic hospital-acquired pulmonary embolism: A retrospective cohort study.

abstract: Seronegative systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) poses a diagnostic challenge, particularly when patients develop organ-threatening disease despite negative traditional serologies. We report a fulminant case in a 24-year-old woman with congenital atrioventricular (AV) block, chronic pancytopenia, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and morbid obesity, who presented with progressive anasarca, dyspnea, dizziness, and cough. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe pancytopenia, nephrotic-range proteinuria 11-13 g/day (reference range: 0-150 mg/24 hours), and acute kidney injury. Renal biopsy demonstrated Class IV proliferative and Class V membranous lupus nephritis, despite negative antinuclear antibodies (ANA), anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibodies, anti-Smith (anti-Sm) antibodies, anti-Sjögren's-syndrome-related antigen A (SSA) and antigen B (SSB) antibodies, and normal complement levels. Within 24 hours, she developed hypoxia, hemoglobin drop, and a right subcapsular renal hematoma. Echocardiography revealed dilated cardiomyopathy, severe aortic insufficiency with valvular vegetation, and suspected pacing-induced cardiomyopathy, progressing to cardiogenic shock requiring inotropes. She developed necrotizing mucocutaneous lesions, vasculitic purpura, pseudomembranous colitis secondary to Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), and microangiopathic hemolysis. Despite high-dose steroids and mycophenolate, her condition deteriorated, necessitating transfer for plasmapheresis and rituximab. Seronegative SLE represents up to 5% of cases and is often associated with severe, multisystem involvement. Seronegativity may reflect low antibody titers, immune complex sequestration, or assay variability. This case underscores that negative serologies do not exclude SLE, and early recognition through clinical suspicion and tissue biopsy is critical. Aggressive immunosuppression and multidisciplinary care are essential in managing fulminant seronegative lupus with severe nephritis, vasculopathy, and systemic complications.
journal: Journal of investigative medicine high impact case reports
journal_abbrev: J Investig Med High Impact Case Rep
title: Fulminant Seronegative Systemic Lupus Erythematosus With Class IV/V Lupus Nephritis and Multisystem Involvement.

abstract: Polycythemia vera is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm in which erythrocytosis, Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription activation, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and abnormal blood-cell activation converge to increase cardiovascular risk. This narrative review examines how electrocardiography, echocardiography, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and right-heart catheterization contribute to recognition and characterization of cardiac involvement in polycythemia vera. Reported abnormalities include QT and P-wave changes, atrial arrhythmias, acute coronary syndromes, subclinical biventricular dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, intracardiac thrombosis, and hypertrophic remodeling. Large observational datasets in myeloproliferative neoplasms also exhibit clinically important burdens of myocardial infarction, heart-failure hospitalization, bleeding, and echocardiographic pulmonary hypertension, although polycythemia vera-specific estimates remain limited. Baseline cardiovascular testing is increasingly relevant before novel therapies and trial enrollment; however, an abnormal test should prompt confirmation, reversible-cause assessment, and protocol-specific review rather than be treated as a universal contraindication. Hematocrit control and low-dose aspirin reduce thrombotic events, while evidence that cytoreductive therapy reverses electrocardiography or imaging abnormalities remains sparse. A symptom- and risk-directed diagnostic approach, integrated with hematology and cardiology assessment, is therefore more defensible than routine universal cardiac screening.
journal: The Journal of international medical research
title: Cardiac diagnostic modalities in polycythemia vera: A narrative review.

abstract:
AIMS: Hip fracture is a global health issue. Complications are common, leading to reduced quality of life or death. These occur more frequently if anaemia is present. We hypothesize that correcting anaemia in the perioperative period may decrease major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and death after hip fracture.
METHODS: This multicentre prospective randomized trial compares transfusion strategies after hip fracture in patients aged ≥ 60 years. We initially planned to randomize 1,984 participants with anaemia, defined as haemoglobin ≤ 90 g l-1, to one of two transfusion strategies: liberal transfusion (aim haemoglobin 90 g l-1 to 110 g l-1), or restrictive transfusion (aim 75 g l-1 to 90 g l-1). The intervention lasts from randomization to hospital discharge or 30 days post randomization, whichever is soonest. The primary outcome measure was a composite of death or MACE adjudicated by blinded clinical experts. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and quality of life, evaluated at 120 days. Cost-effectiveness and health economic evaluation will also be reported.
RESULTS: This trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research, HTA award (National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) 130875) and registered at ISRCTN 28818784. Ethical approval was obtained to recruit patients in the UK. As recruitment fell short of the initial target, and following consultation with the funder, we refined our primary outcome to include myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS), and reduced the required sample size to 842.
CONCLUSION: Recruitment commenced on 10 June 2022. The first participant was recruited on 16 June 2022. We will engage clinicians and healthcare planners to implement the findings. We plan to recruit until 31 October 2026. Results will be disseminated to clinicians, policymakers, patients, and the public.
title: RESULT-Hip. The impact of restrictive compared with liberal transfusion strategy on cardiac injury and death in patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture : protocol for a multicentre, randomized controlled trial of two blood transfusion strategies.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a well-established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but its prognostic role after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains unclear. This study investigated the association between Lp(a) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), in patients with AMI.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 1,235 patients with AMI from the NARA-MI registry who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention and had serum Lp(a) measured at admission. Based on receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, patients were categorized into high (≥24 mg/dL) and low (<24 mg/dL) Lp(a) groups. The primary endpoint was MACE, defined as all-cause death, recurrent AMI, HF hospitalization, or unplanned coronary revascularization. During a median follow-up of 3.6 years, 497 MACE events occurred. The incidence of MACE (48.0% vs. 38.3%; P=0.004) and HF hospitalization (9.3% vs. 5.0%; P=0.008) was significantly higher in the high Lp(a) group. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, high-Lp(a) independently predicted MACE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-1.73; P=0.001) and HF hospitalization (HR 1.87; 95% CI 1.15-3.04; P=0.016). Among patients with HF, 39.7% were classified as HFpEF.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes after AMI, particularly HF. Measurement of Lp(a) may improve risk stratification after AMI and help identify patients at high risk of developing HF, including HFpEF.
journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
keywords: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
title: High Lipoprotein(a) Is a Predictor of Adverse Events and Heart Failure in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
PURPOSE: In coronary CT angiography, we compared the profile characteristics and visual assessment of coronary stents between hybrid iterative reconstruction combined with a sharpening filter (S-HIR) and deep learning reconstruction (DLR).
METHODS: We scanned a performance evaluation phantom and a custom-made phantom incorporating a coronary artery stent with an inner diameter of 3.5 mm. Images were reconstructed using DLR, hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR), and S-HIR of three sharpening strengths. We evaluated task-based transfer function (TTF) values, the maximum CT number of the stent struts, the error rate of the stent lumen diameter, rectangularity, and visual assessment performed by nine radiological technologists using Scheffé's paired comparison method.
RESULTS: In S-HIR, TTF values and rectangularity increased, while the error rate decreased with increasing sharpening strength. Visual assessment revealed no significant difference between sharpening medium filter+HIR (SM-HIR) and DLR. In contrast, sharpening high filter+HIR (SH-HIR) resulted in an excessive increase in the maximum CT number of the stent struts, and visual assessment scores decreased.
CONCLUSION: The S-HIR method newly proposed in this study altered the profile characteristics of coronary artery stents and improved their visibility in coronary CT angiography under phantom conditions. In particular, SM-HIR showed no statistically significant difference from DLR in visual assessment and could serve as a useful technique for improving coronary stent visibility in CT systems without DLR.
title: [Impact of Hybrid Iterative Reconstruction Combined with a Sharpening Filter on Coronary Artery Stent Profile Characteristics and Visual Assessment in Coronary CT Angiography: A Phantom Study].

abstract: Ischemic heart disease is a highly prevalent and debilitating condition throughout the world. Following an ischemic injury, the immune response can become overly active and spread damage to nearby healthy tissue. Because the heart lacks regenerative capacity, preventing excessive damage is critical. Existing immunosuppressive therapeutics provide indiscriminate suppression of inflammatory and repair functions of infiltrating immune cells. Regulatory T cells (Treg) are the body's highly sophisticated system for regulating immunologic activity. These cells can provide powerful immune suppression while amplifying repair pathways through direct stimulation of local cells. Our research group has previously developed a polymeric delivery system comprised of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) degradable microparticles (MP) loaded with the Treg-attracting protein, CCL22. In our previous work, we demonstrated CCL22MP attracts Treg to the injection site and can suppress disadvantageous inflammation. Here we combine our Treg-attracting MP technology with Hydrogels to Enhance or Attract Regulatory T cells (HEART). Topically applied HEART significantly reduced infarct size and improved ejection fraction after permanent-ligation MI, and in a cardiac transplant ischemia model reduced graft fibrosis while significantly increasing intragraft Foxp3+ Treg at 30 days. Efficacy tracked with injury severity, identifying severe ischemic injury as a setting where this therapeutic strategy may be most beneficial.
title: Topically Delivered Treg-Attracting Microparticle-Hydrogel Composites Recruit Regulatory T Cells and Limit Cardiac Injury After Severe Ischemia.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA) is a rare congenital cardiac anomaly characterized by atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance, resulting in a physiologically corrected circulation. When ccTGA is combined with dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis, surgical management becomes particularly challenging because of the mirror-image anatomy and altered spatial orientation.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 61-year-old man presented with progressive dyspnea and was diagnosed with ccTGA accompanied by dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe regurgitation of the systemic atrioventricular valve (morphological tricuspid valve) with dilation and systolic dysfunction of the systemic right ventricle. Comprehensive preoperative imaging confirmed atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance, right-sided cardiac apex, and complete visceral inversion. Tricuspid valve replacement was performed via a median sternotomy with the surgeon standing on the patient's left side to accommodate the mirror-image anatomy. Cardiopulmonary bypass was established safely after meticulous identification of the great vessels. A mechanical prosthetic valve was successfully implanted. The postoperative course was uneventful, and follow-up echocardiography at six months confirmed satisfactory prosthetic valve function without complications.
CONCLUSIONS: This case illustrates that tricuspid valve replacement can be safely and effectively performed in patients with ccTGA complicated by dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis. A left-sided surgical approach, combined with thorough preoperative imaging and careful intraoperative anatomical verification, may help restore operative orientation and reduce technical complexity in patients with mirror-image cardiac anatomy.
keywords: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
mesh: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
title: Left-sided surgical approach for tricuspid valve replacement in congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries with dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis: A case report.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a voice-guided, tap-and-talk educational tool and assess its effectiveness in improving disease-related knowledge and self-management behaviors among older adults following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHODS: A voice-guided tap-and-talk educational tool was designed to address the specific needs of older adults post-PCI. A cluster randomized controlled trial was conducted in cardiovascular wards. The control group received conventional health education using printed manuals, whereas the intervention group received education via the tap-and-talk interactive tool. Outcomes included the level of knowledge regarding coronary heart disease and engagement in self-management behaviors. Chi-squared test and independent-sample t-test, chi-square test and paired t-test, and univariate repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) were conducted accordingly.
RESULTS: A total of 96 patients completed the study, including 49 in the experimental group and 47 in the control group.No statistically significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics between the groups (p > 0.05). A significant group × time interaction effect was detected for coronary heart disease (CHD)-related knowledge (F = 9.026, P < 0.001). At 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months post-intervention, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher self-management behavior scores than the control group (F = 11.607, P < 0.001). Additionally, CHD-related knowledge scores showed a mild downward trend over time in both groups (F = 124.067, P < 0.001). Consistent with the interaction effect mentioned above, the intervention group achieved significantly higher CHD-related knowledge scores than the control group at all three follow-up time points (1 month, 3 months, and 6 months post-intervention) (F = 195.188, P < 0.001). Scores in the intervention group remained consistently higher across all domains. The tool received high acceptance ratings from participants (mean score 96.04 ± 2.61).
CONCLUSION: The tap-and-talk voice-guided educational tool was effective in enhancing knowledge and promoting self-management behaviors among older adults following PCI. The tool demonstrated a high level of user acceptability within the target population.
title: Effectiveness of a voice-guided tap-and-talk educational tool in enhancing cardiovascular knowledge and self-management in aged patients following percutaneous coronary intervention.

abstract: Failure of true-lumen re-entry after subintimal wire passage is a well-recognized limitation of endovascular treatment for external iliac artery (EIA) chronic total occlusions (CTO). We report a 73-year-old woman with severe limb ischemia and a prior failed endovascular attempt who underwent hybrid left common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy with patch angioplasty, followed by trans-patch retrograde access and dedicated device-assisted re-entry (Outback Elite) after antegrade and retrograde wires repeatedly tracked subintimally without reaching the true lumen. Controlled re-entry preserved hypogastric artery flow and allowed drug-eluting stent reconstruction of the EIA. At 12-month follow-up, ABI improved from 0.36 to 0.50, and TBI improved to 0.37. Duplex ultrasound at 6-month follow-up confirmed patency of the reconstructed segment without evidence of hemodynamically significant restenosis. This technical report illustrates the use of an endarterectomized CFA as a retrograde re-entry platform and reviews contemporary strategies for managing subintimal crossing failure in iliac CTOs.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Trans-Patch Retrograde Re-Entry During Hybrid Revascularization of an External Iliac Artery Chronic Total Occlusion: A Technical Note and Review of Re-Entry Strategies.

abstract:
AIMS: Iron deficiency (ID) is common amongst patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Its impact on outcomes remains contested. Previous studies reported favourable or adverse impacts depending on outcome measures, sampling timepoints, ID definition and follow-up duration. This study systematically characterises the prognostic impact of iron status on short-term, mid-term and long-term outcomes, and evaluates the effect of sampling timepoint and ID definition on these prognostic relationships.
METHODS & RESULTS: We performed an observational cohort study in patients with acute STEMI (n = 167) and no prior heart failure (HF). Iron markers were sampled at presentation, and successive timepoints thereafter. Cardiac Magnetic Resonance was performed at 2 days and 6 months. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), consisting of new-onset HF, recurrent MI or cardiac death were recorded over 4.5 years. Mechanisms were evaluated in a preclinical model of MI.ID was common at presentation, affecting between 44.9% and 67%, depending on ID definition. Tsat <20%, serum iron<13μM, or European Society of Cardiology's definition, but not ferritin<100μg/L, independently predicted lower risk of MACE. Lower Tsat at presentation predicted attenuated infarct and non-infarct T1, and smaller left ventricular volumes at 2 days. This prognostic effect was weakened by delayed sampling. Lower Tsat and serum iron in the post-acute timepoints, but not at presentation, predicted lower myocardial salvage at 6 months. In mice, MI triggered an acute myocardial labile iron storm and early LV remodelling, progressing to HF. Baseline ID and acute iron chelation averted these effects.
CONCLUSIONS: This study gives rise to the hypothesis that ID at presentation with STEMI improves long-term outcomes by attenuating myocardial injury. It reconciles previous conflicting reports by revealing the confounding effects of delayed sampling, and non-interchangeability of different ID definitions. It suggests iron chelation in the acute stage, followed by post-acute iron repletion might improve long-term outcomes.
title: Complex relationship between iron status and outcomes of STEMI: hypothesis-generating study.

abstract: Systemic atrioventricular valve (SAVV) regurgitation contributes importantly to systemic right ventricular deterioration in adults with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA) and dextro-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) after atrial-switch repair. Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) has emerged as an option for selected patients at high or prohibitive surgical risk, and prior congenital series have established the feasibility of transseptal, transbaffle, and alternative access strategies. However, procedural execution remains highly anatomy-dependent because systemic venous pathways, atrial baffles, ventricular topology, cardiac orientation, and access-to-valve geometry can substantially alter guide-catheter support and device coaxiality. We report a single-center Interventional Rounds experience of four consecutive high-risk adults undergoing SAVV-TEER across four distinct transposition anatomies: ccTGA with dextrocardia, d-TGA after Mustard atrial-switch repair, Mustard anatomy with severe iliofemoral tortuosity, and ccTGA with interrupted inferior vena cava and azygos continuation. Transfemoral access was used in two patients, and right internal jugular access in two. Three procedures were performed with PASCAL ACE and one with MitraClip. Device implantation was successful in all four patients, with SAVV regurgitation reduced from severe (3+) to mild (1+). Final mean SAVV gradients were 1.5, 2.1, 1.9, and 1.8 mmHg, respectively, and no major acute procedural complications occurred. The principal technical message is that access selection should be guided not only by anatomic patency but by the anticipated mechanical trajectory of the delivery system. Right internal jugular access may be selected prospectively as the preferred primary route when inferior venous anatomy is absent or expected to provide unfavorable curvature, support, or device alignment. Dextrocardia and atrial-switch baffle anatomy may additionally require specific steering and traversal adaptations. These observations represent focused procedural refinements within the evolving congenital TEER experience rather than evidence of comparative efficacy or safety.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
keywords: congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
surgically corrected transposition of the great arteries
title: Anatomy-Driven Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair of the Systemic Atrioventricular Valve in Complex Transposition Anatomy.

abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) and advanced perfusion imaging have transformed acute ischemic stroke (AIS) treatment, yet tissue hypoxia may persist because of delayed presentation, incomplete reperfusion, microvascular no-reflow, and secondary injury. Oxygen is an essential substrate for cerebral metabolism and a modifiable therapeutic exposure; however, clinical studies of oxygen-based interventions have yielded inconsistent results because of heterogeneity in timing, dose, delivery, and patient selection. Here we propose precision oxygen modulation (POM) as a stage-, phenotype-, and tissue-informed framework for the reperfusion era-treating oxygen exposure as a dose-titrated therapy that must be matched to the right patient, time window, physiological target, and safety boundary. POM integrates oxygen conditioning strategies that may prime neurovascular resilience before or around ischemia, time-limited therapeutic oxygen strategies deployed around reperfusion to support tissue at risk, and recovery-stage strategies paired with rehabilitation. We synthesize clinical and preclinical evidence linking oxygen tension to excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and repair, while emphasizing the context-dependent risks of hyperoxia. We outline an operational decision framework and translational roadmap based on phenotype- and imaging-guided selection, biomarker validation, protocolized dosing, predefined safety boundaries, and phenotype-enriched randomized trials. POM is presented as a testable translational framework for organizing heterogeneous evidence and guiding the prospective validation of stage-specific oxygen modulation in modern stroke care.
title: Precision Oxygen Modulation in the Reperfusion Era: Conditioning and Therapeutic Strategies in Ischemic Stroke.

abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have significantly enhanced the diagnosis in patients suspected of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). New hs-cTn point-of-care (POC) devices (turnaround time <20 min) may significantly reduce time to diagnosis. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of four currently commercially available hs-cTn POC devices to assess their potential for clinical implementation at the emergency department (ED). We conducted a search in PubMed Central on 20 November, 2025. Studies were included if they investigated patients greater than or equal to 18 years presenting with chest pain suggestive of ACS and evaluated commercially available hs-cTn POC devices. Studies had to report diagnostic accuracy [sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value] for the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Studies were assessed for risk of bias and applicability using the QUADAS-3 tool. We identified 436 articles. The 11 included studies consisted of both derivation and validation studies, including a total of 10 115 patients. The hs-cTn POC assays demonstrated the best diagnostic accuracy when applied as a single-test rule-out upon arrival at the ED, showing the following sensitivity and NPV: Atellica VTLi sensitivity 98.8-100% for troponin less than 4 ng/L (NPV: 99.8-100%) and 100% for troponin less than 7 ng/L (NPV 100%). Pathfast sensitivity 96.3-100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV: 98.1-100%). i-STAT sensitivity of 99.8% for troponin less than 5 ng/L (NPV: 100%). TriageTrue sensitivity of 100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV 100%). VTLi, Pathfast, and TriageTrue were also tested using the 99th percentile with a 0 + 1/2/3 h troponin protocol. Reported sensitivities: VTLi 64.8-100%, Pathfast 87% for plasma and 83% for whole blood, and TriageTrue 79.8%. Hs-cTn POC assays are reliable for integration into the diagnostic pathways for patients presenting with chest pain at the ED, mainly when used for rapid rule-out of AMI in patients with very low troponin values upon arrival.
journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
title: Diagnostic accuracy of high-sensitivity point-of-care troponin assays in emergency department for patients presenting with chest pain: a systematic review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a cornerstone of post-acute care for patients experiencing cardiovascular events or interventions. It aims to improve cardiorespiratory capacity, enhance quality of life, and maximize physical function, facilitating a return to daily activities. However, the optimal timing for initiating CR following acute coronary events or procedures remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this randomized clinical trial, 40 patients diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction and treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were randomly assigned to two groups. Group A commenced cardiac rehabilitation one month after PCI, while Group B initiated rehabilitation two months post-PCI. Both groups completed a supervised 12-session rehabilitation program under the guidance of a physical medicine specialist. Functional outcomes were assessed before and after rehabilitation using the SF-36 quality of life questionnaire and echocardiographic parameters. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25. Within-group changes were evaluated with paired t-tests, and between-group comparisons of change scores were conducted using independent samples t-tests. A P-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Post-rehabilitation, the mean SF-36 score was 65.85±6.67 in Group A and 67.05±5.96 in Group B (P=0.192). The mean change in Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) was 2.25% in Group A and 0.15% in Group B (P=0.305). After rehabilitation, grade 1-2 diastolic dysfunction remained present in 85% of patients in both groups, while 15% of patients in each group showed no evidence of diastolic dysfunction (P=0.506).No significant differences were found between groups in heart rate (HR) Max (107.45±15.04 vs. 115.20±13.12; P=0.091), HR Recovery (22.50±7.05 vs. 23.10±7.78; P=0.800), or MET change (6.60±1.83 vs. 6.20±2.39; P=0.556).
CONCLUSION: Initiating cardiac rehabilitation one month as opposed to two months after primary PCI did not yield significant differences in quality of life or cardiac functional parameters. These findings indicate that there may be flexibility in the timing of CR initiation without compromising short-term functional outcomes.
journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
title: Timing of Cardiac Rehabilitation After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Layered plaque, representing organized thrombus overlying a previously disrupted plaque, is a marker of coronary destabilization and plaque vulnerability. Despite its clinical relevance, identifying layered plaque remains expert dependent with interobserver variability, limiting large-scale assessment. We developed and validated an artificial intelligence (AI) model for layered plaque segmentation, and assessed occurrence and associations with plaque vulnerability in non-culprit lesions.
METHODS: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) pullbacks from the PECTUS-obs and ORANGE datasets were used to develop an enhanced version of our validated multiclass segmentation model (OCT-AID), by adding layered plaque as an additional pixel-level class. Pullbacks were divided into a training set (n = 4121 frames, 493 with layered plaque) and an independent held-out test set (n = 433 frames, 71 with layered plaque). Using this model, prevalence of layered plaque and associations with plaque vulnerability features were studied in patients with non-culprit lesions (PECTUS-obs data; 414 patients, 488 lesions).
RESULTS: The model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.68 ± 0.27 for layered plaque segmentation, with pullback-level sensitivity of 96.2% and specificity of 75.0%. At least one layered plaque was present in 366/414 patients (88.4%). Presence of layered plaque was higher in STEMI patients (p = 0.018). Lesions containing layered plaques showed higher prevalence of lipid-rich plaque (76.4% vs. 60.9%, p = 0.008), thin-cap fibroatheroma (29.2% vs. 15.6%, p = 0.016), macrophage accumulation (25.0% vs 9.4%, p = 0.010), and cholesterol clefts (0.0% vs. 8.3%; p = 0.009).
CONCLUSIONS: Automated OCT-based identification of layered plaque using AI is feasible. In non-culprit coronary lesions, layered plaque was highly prevalent and associated with established markers of plaque vulnerability.
journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
title: Automated segmentation and clinical characterization of layered plaque in intracoronary optical coherence tomography.

abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of preoperative and early postoperative echocardiographic parameters for left ventricular function recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and to evaluate the relationship between functional recovery and 1-year clinical prognosis.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 214 patients undergoing first-time elective CABG at The First Affiliated Hospital of Yangtze University between January 2022 and October 2024. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively, 3-7 days postoperatively, and at 6 months to evaluate left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial volume index (LAVI), and ratio of early mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/e'). Based on 6‑month LVEF change, patients were divided into recovery (ΔLVEF ≥5%) and non‑recovery (ΔLVEF <5%) groups. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors, and the corresponding models were established and validated. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were recorded at 1‑year follow‑up.
RESULTS: Of the 214 patients enrolled in the study, functional recovery of the left ventricle was observed in 128 individuals, corresponding to 59.8% of the cohort. Multivariate analysis identified several preoperative and procedural variables as independent predictors of functional recovery, including left atrial volume index (LAVI), left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD), left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD), left atrial diameter (LAD), Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery (SYNTAX) score, and the number of graft vessels. Age, preoperative LVEF, and e' velocity were independently associated with lower odds of functional recovery. Global longitudinal strain (GLS) and diabetes history showed no independent predictive value. The clinical-echocardiographic combined model demonstrated excellent discrimination and showed higher discriminative performance than the basic clinical model and conventional echocardiographic model. Subgroup analysis revealed that GLS showed no independent predictive value across all LVEF subgroups (p > 0.05), whereas LAVI and LAD were significant predictors in patients with LVEF ≥40% (including the 40%-49% subgroup), but showed no predictive relevance in those with LVEF <40%. Early postoperative ΔLVEF predicted 6-month functional recovery with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.846. After one year of follow‑up, the recovery group exhibited a markedly lower rate of MACE than the non‑recovery group, with left ventricular functional recovery serving as an independent protective factor against MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative structural parameters, including LAVI, LVEDD, LVESD, and LAD, are independent imaging biomarkers for predicting left ventricular functional recovery after CABG. GLS and E/e' ratio show no independent predictive value in this study. The integrated model combining clinical factors with multi-dimensional echocardiographic parameters demonstrates excellent discriminative ability. Early postoperative LVEF improvement strongly predicts 6-month functional recovery, while postoperative recovery of left ventricular function is associated with a significantly lower 1-year MACE risk.
title: Multidimensional Echocardiographic Parameters Predict Left Ventricular Functional Recovery After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.

abstract:
AIM: To compare the 1-year patency rates of drug-coated balloon (DCB) and drug-eluting stent (DES) in the treatment of lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans (LEASO), and to systematically analyze the factors influencing post-treatment patency.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 302 patients with LEASO who received treatment at Fuyang People's Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Based on the treatment modality, patients were divided into a DCB group (n = 152) and a DES group (n = 150). Comprehensive baseline demographic, clinical, and procedural data were collected. The 1-year primary patency rates of the two groups were compared using imaging assessment, primarily based on ultrasonography. Independent risk factors affecting patency were identified using a multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression model.
RESULTS: The 1-year primary patency rate was 87.5% (133/152) in the DCB group and 89.3% (134/150) in the DES group. No statistically significant difference in the 1-year primary patency rates was observed between the two groups (p > 0.05). Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that diabetes mellitus, lesion length, and severe calcification were independent risk factors affecting patency after endovascular treatment (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The 1-year patency rates did not differ significantly between the DCB and DES groups. Diabetes mellitus, long lesion length, and severe calcification were identified as key factors associated with reduced patency rates. Clinical management should emphasize individualized intervention strategies and postoperative management for these high-risk patients.
title: Comparison of Primary Patency Rates and Influencing Factors Between Drug-Coated Balloons and Drug-Eluting Stents in the Endovascular Treatment of Lower Extremity Arteriosclerosis Obliterans.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED.
METHODS: We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days.
RESULTS: Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33-61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P=0.54).
CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pragmatic stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial, six sites, 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals).
appraisal.main_limitation: The primary outcome is a process measure (length of stay) and the safety outcome has very few events.
appraisal.one_line: Stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial of point-of-care hs-cTnI in an accelerated ED pathway shortened ED length of stay without a difference in 30-day MI or cardiac death.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33-61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P=0.54).
