abstract: There is a lack of clinical data regarding sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors' effects on myocardial injury, a common clinical condition that deteriorates patient prognosis. Hence, this systematic review aims to investigate the effects of SGLT2 inhibitors on myocardial injury, using the cardiac injury biomarkers, particularly high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn). We performed a literature review on Embase, MEDLINE (PubMed), and the Cochrane Library, up to May 27, 2025. All potentially relevant randomized clinical trials (RCTs) assessing the effects of SGLT2 inhibitors on myocardial injury in individuals with diabetes or cardiovascular diseases were identified. The outcome measures were the most relevant cardiac injury biomarkers, including hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI, creatine kinase (CK)-MB, heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), myoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), ischemia-modified albumin, and glycogen phosphorylase BB. In total, 1770 articles were identified through the literature search. After eliminating duplicates and screening articles, 10 studies involving 10440 participants were included. Of them, 6 studies evaluated hs-cTnT and 4 studies evaluated hs-cTnI. Among individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), four of six trials showed significant attenuation in hs-cTn rise with SGLT2 inhibitors. In contrast, studies on HFrEF populations reported no significant change in hs-cTn levels. One study, including patients with acute myocardial infarction, also did not demonstrate a significant effect on hs-cTnI. The outcomes of this systematic review may suggest the potential effects of SGLT2 inhibitors in reducing myocardial injury by lowering hs-cTn levels in T2DM individuals. However, more studies are recommended to provide robust evidence.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular and thoracic research
title: SGLT2 Inhibitors' Effects on Biomarkers of Myocardial Injury: A Systematic Review.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Given the proven cardiovascular benefits of Empagliflozin (EM), we aimed to investigate the effect of Empagliflozin on Cardiotrophin-1 (CTF-1) and growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) expressions in circulating monocytes in type 2 diabetic patients after MI.
METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study included 33 patients referred to Ayatollah Mousavi Hospital in Zanjan between 5 of September to 25 of December, 2024. Eligible patients with type 2 diabetes and MI who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were randomly assigned (17:16) to receive either 10 mg of EMPA daily or placebo for 12 weeks. Target genes expression levels were quantified by real time PCR, and data were analyzed by SPSS version 26.
RESULTS: Thirty-three patients were included in this study (mean age: 61.27±9.07, 66% male), mean diabetes duration was longer in intervention group (7.82±5.13) compared to placebo group (3.75±2.74), hypertension was the most common comorbidity (57%). CTF-1 expression in the intervention group was 0.3±0.28 and in placebo group was 5.66±6.52. GDF-15 expression in the intervention group was 0.198±0.22 and in placebo group was 1.66±1.04. EMPA significantly reduced expression of CTF-1 (13-fold) (P=0.003) and GDF-15 (7-fold) (P ˂ 0.0001). The CTF-1 and GDF-15 expression reduction were not associated with any other clinical variables. Significant reduction observed in LDL (P=0.045) and triglycerides (P=0.013) after intervention.
CONCLUSION: EMPA significantly reduced the expression of CTF-1 and GDF-15 in type 2 diabetic, post MI patients, which are associated with atherosclerosis, and suggest that potential anti-atherosclerotic effect of EMPA mediated through modulation of GDF-15 and CTF-1 gene expression.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular and thoracic research
title: Impact of Empagliflozin on mRNA Levels of Cardiotrophin-1 and GDF-15 in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing PCI: A Double-Blind Pilot Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have substantially improved long-term oncologic outcomes in patients with advanced malignancies; however, ICI-related cardiovascular adverse events have emerged as a growing clinical challenge. Accumulating clinical evidence confirms that ICI treatment markedly increases the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Although cardiovascular toxicities secondary to ICIs are relatively infrequent, these complications carry severe and potentially fatal clinical consequences. Herein, we describe a rare case of acute non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) complicated by accelerated atherosclerosis potentially associated with ICI therapy in a middle-aged woman with advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma harboring proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) status. Following successful coronary revascularization, the patient safely reinitiated immunotherapy and achieved long-term sustained tumor-free survival.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 39-year-old woman was diagnosed with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage IVB cervical squamous cell carcinoma, with comorbid type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. She received first-line quadruple combination therapy comprising nab-paclitaxel, cisplatin, bevacizumab, and tislelizumab. Complete tumor response was achieved following six cycles of systemic treatment. Subsequent maintenance therapy combined with pelvic radiotherapy enabled sustained disease remission for more than 5 years. Approximately 2 years after transitioning to single-agent tislelizumab maintenance, the patient experienced an acute NSTEMI. Coronary angiography demonstrated severe multivessel coronary stenosis, and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed successfully. After thorough multidisciplinary cardio-oncology evaluation, tislelizumab was safely reinitiated and continued until August 2024. At the most recent follow-up in June 2026, the patient maintained a persistent complete response with stable cardiac function.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights that patients with advanced pMMR cervical cancer complicated by diabetes and hypertension can achieve durable complete remission exceeding 5 years with tislelizumab-based combination regimens. Furthermore, this case report also suggests that ICIs may be associated with cardiovascular events secondary to accelerated atherosclerosis, and demonstrates the clinical feasibility of safely resuming immune-checkpoint-inhibitor therapy following myocardial infarction.
title: Durable complete response to tislelizumab in advanced pMMR cervical cancer and successful rechallenge after immune-related NSTEMI: a case report.

abstract: High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) can lead to acute right ventricular failure, obstructive shock, and cardiac arrest. Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provides bridging life support, buying time for imaging confirmation and reperfusion. However, reperfusion injury, pulmonary hemorrhage, and airway thrombotic obstruction may follow pulmonary artery reperfusion. Severe airway obstruction caused by bronchial cast thrombi is rare and challenging. We report a woman in her 60s awaiting surgery for a left femoral neck fracture who developed preoperative cardiac arrest due to high-risk PE. After VA-ECMO bridging and staged catheter-based pulmonary reperfusion, the patient developed reperfusion injury and bilateral bronchial cast thrombosis, managed by repeated bronchoscopy with cryoextraction. Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) monitored ventilation and perfusion. The patient was weaned from VA-ECMO and invasive ventilation but remained in a persistent vegetative state due to hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. This case suggests that in cardiac arrest caused by high-risk PE, VA-ECMO can buy time for diagnosis and reperfusion; however, reperfusion injury after recanalization can cause severe hemorrhage, with blood coagulating within the airways into bronchial cast thrombi and life-threatening obstruction. Bronchoscopy with cryoextraction effectively clears tenacious airway cast thrombi. EIT assists ventilation/perfusion monitoring during complex VA-ECMO support. Even when cardiopulmonary function recovers, hypoxic-ischemic brain injury may determine long-term prognosis.
title: Case Report: Pulmonary reperfusion injury with bilateral bronchial cast thrombosis after VA-ECMO-bridged catheter-based reperfusion for cardiac arrest caused by high-risk pulmonary embolism.

abstract: Traumatic popliteal artery occlusion is a limb-threatening condition traditionally managed with open surgical revascularization. Here, we describe a 66-year-old man with delayed occlusion after high-energy lower-extremity trauma. Initial computed tomography angiography indicated preserved flow despite severe arterial deformation. Progressive heel necrosis developed after fracture fixation and debridement; repeat imaging on day 24 showed complete occlusion of the popliteal artery. Intravascular ultrasound-guided endovascular repair with an interwoven nitinol stent restored antegrade flow. Wound healing was achieved after flap and skin graft procedures, and stent patency was maintained for >2.5 years.
journal: Journal of vascular surgery cases and innovative techniques
journal_abbrev: J Vasc Surg Cases Innov Tech
title: Intravascular ultrasound-guided repair of delayed traumatic popliteal artery occlusion using an interwoven nitinol stent.

abstract: Catheter-based renal denervation (RDN) is endorsed by major international guidelines as an adjunct to antihypertensive therapy, yet most regulatory and reimbursement frameworks still restrict its use to true resistant hypertension, usually defined as uncontrolled blood pressure (BP) despite three or more maximally tolerated antihypertensive drugs including a diuretic. This restriction leaves a clinically important population without an effective escalation pathway: patients with uncontrolled, high-risk hypertension who cannot tolerate the multi-class drug regimens required to qualify as resistant. We argue that this exclusion is increasingly difficult to justify. Contemporary sham-controlled trials enrolling patients on no or limited antihypertensive therapy demonstrate modest but reproducible ambulatory BP reductions in precisely the pharmacological context in which drug-intolerant patients are managed and guidelines published since 2023 acknowledge uncontrolled hypertension on fewer drugs or drug intolerance as clinically relevant scenarios for RDN. The device-attributable ambulatory systolic effect converges on 4-6 mmHg, 25-40% of treated patients derive no meaningful BP reduction, no pre-procedural variable reliably identifies responders, and no trial has been powered for cardiovascular outcomes. Drug intolerance also lacks an objective definition and frequently reflects undisclosed non-adherence. We propose a pragmatic referral pathway in which biochemical adherence testing and a documented trial of a low dose single-pill combination are mandatory steps, followed by out-of-office BP confirmation, secondary hypertension screening, anatomical eligibility and multidisciplinary shared decision-making.
journal: International journal of cardiology. Cardiovascular risk and prevention
journal_abbrev: Int J Cardiol Cardiovasc Risk Prev
title: Renal denervation beyond resistant hypertension: should drug intolerance redefine eligibility?

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) with the EVOQUE system has expanded therapeutic options for severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR), but a prohibitively dilated tricuspid annulus may exceed the device-sizing matrix and preclude implantation. No transcatheter strategy has been described to mechanically pre-condition such an annulus.
CASE SUMMARY: A 71-year-old woman with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (left ventricular ejection fraction 38%, suspected premature-ventricular-complex-induced cardiomyopathy), permanent atrial fibrillation, and class III obesity presented with torrential atrial functional TR refractory to fully optimized guideline-directed medical therapy. Screening cardiac computed tomography (CT) classified the native annulus as 'outside parameters' for the 56 mm EVOQUE (Edwards Lifesciences); the Heart Team also deemed standalone tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) inadequate owing to the massively dilated annulus. We performed the TriArtic procedure-a single TriClip XTW (Abbott) deployed in the septo-anterior position as a transcatheter annuloplasty step. Repeat CT after 27 days demonstrated an ∼11% reduction in tricuspid annular area and conversion of projected-derived-diameter oversizing from -2.9% to +3.3% (within parameters). Transfemoral EVOQUE 56 mm was implanted 48 days after the TriClip; postprocedural imaging confirmed no residual regurgitation and a mean transtricuspid gradient of 1 mm Hg, with rapid recovery of cardiorenal function.
DISCUSSION: Transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty by a strategically placed commissural TEER device may convert a prohibitively dilated annulus into one within EVOQUE-implantable parameters. In carefully selected patients ineligible for either standalone strategy, sequential transcatheter annuloplasty followed by valve replacement-the TriArtic procedure-may offer a feasible pathway, conceptually analogous to the mitral ARCTIC technique. This single case demonstrates feasibility only and does not establish general applicability.
title: The TriArtic procedure: TRIcuspid annular reduction by TEER in the commissure-a transcatheter annuloplasty enabling EVOQUE tricuspid valve replacement: a case report.

abstract: Left ventricular (LV) thrombus is a serious complication of cardiomyopathy with severely reduced ejection fraction, carrying significant risk of systemic embolization. While direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have emerged as a reasonable alternative to warfarin for LV thrombus treatment in the general population, no guideline-directed evidence exists for their use in patients with concomitant acute kidney injury (AKI) or significant renal impairment in this specific clinical context. We present the case of a 47-year-old male with newly diagnosed nonischemic cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 25%), LV apical thrombus, and Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO)-defined AKI attributed to type 1 cardiorenal syndrome, who was managed with heparin bridging to warfarin due to the absence of evidence supporting DOAC use for LV thrombus in the setting of renal dysfunction. The requirement for heparin-to-warfarin bridging prolonged the patient's hospitalization by five days, illustrating the tangible clinical and resource burden imposed by the current guideline gap. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is present in approximately 45% of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; roughly two-thirds of heart failure hospitalizations are associated with a discharge estimated glomerular filtration rate below 60 mL/min/1.73 m², and AKI complicates approximately one-third of heart failure admissions, so this clinical scenario is far from rare. We additionally provide a literature review of the current evidence comparing DOACs and vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) for LV thrombus, DOAC pharmacokinetics in renal impairment, and the guideline landscape at this clinical intersection. Notably, every randomized trial comparing DOACs with warfarin for LV thrombus to date has explicitly excluded patients with moderate-to-severe renal impairment. This case and review underscore the need for prospective studies evaluating DOAC safety and efficacy for LV thrombus in patients with impaired renal function, which could reduce unnecessary hospital days and healthcare costs while maintaining safe anticoagulation.
title: Warfarin for Left Ventricular Thrombus in Nonischemic Cardiomyopathy With Acute Kidney Injury: A Case Report and Literature Review of Anticoagulation Strategies in Renal Impairment.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: End-tidal carbon dioxide tension (P ETCO2 ) may be reduced when lung units are ventilated but under-perfused, as occurs in pulmonary embolism (PE). We sought to determine whether early P ETCO2 measurement reflects PE severity according to European Society of Cardiology (ESC) risk categories and identifies shock-level haemodynamics among patients undergoing catheter-directed therapy (CDT).
METHODS: Patients admitted with acute PE confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography were enrolled in this prospective observational study. P ETCO2 was measured using nasal capnography within 24 h of presentation or immediately prior to urgent CDT. P ETCO2 was compared between lower and higher severity PE groups and between patients referred for CDT or not. In patients undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (CDT) with invasive haemodynamic assessment, pulmonary arterial pressures and cardiac indices were recorded. A subgroup analysis evaluated patients with cardiogenic shock defined as cardiac index ≤1.8 L·min-1·m-2.
RESULTS: 62 patients were analysed. P ETCO2 was significantly lower in the combined higher risk group compared to the combined lower risk group (mean 21.7 (95% CI 20.2-23.3) versus 30.2 (95% CI 27.8-32.6) mmHg; p<0.001). P ETCO2 was also lower in patients referred for CDT compared to those not referred (mean 20.4 (95% CI 18.7-22.0) versus 28.2 (95% CI 26.2-30.1) mmHg; p<0.001). Among patients who underwent CDT and met haemodynamic criteria for cardiogenic shock (n=16), P ETCO2 was the lowest (mean 18.6 (95% CI 16.1-21.1) mmHg).
CONCLUSIONS: P ETCO2 can be rapidly obtained early in PE evaluation and reflects ESC-defined severity. A P ETCO2 level <20 mmHg was associated with shock-level haemodynamics among normotensive intermediate-high-risk patients undergoing CDT. P ETCO2 may serve as a non-invasive marker of physiological severity.
title: Low end-tidal carbon dioxide identifies high-severity pulmonary embolism and shock-level haemodynamics.

abstract: We report the case of a 95-year-old man with a previous history of myocardial infarction, pulmonary oedema, and hypertension who developed recurrent collapse while undergoing ambulatory urological follow-up for a six-week history of macroscopic haematuria. Following a recent outpatient review, he had received oral antibiotics for a presumed urinary tract infection (UTI). Throughout this six-week ambulatory period, no full blood count or other blood tests were performed, leaving the extent of blood loss and its haematological consequences clinically occult. The patient subsequently experienced three episodes of sudden collapse within one week at home. The episodes were preceded by a prodrome of marked weakness. On assessment by ambulance clinicians, a profound postural blood-pressure drop was identified. Given the postural component and presumed recent urinary infection, dehydration was considered the initial explanation, and intravenous fluid resuscitation was commenced. However, hospital point-of-care investigations substantially changed the diagnostic picture. Venous blood gas analysis demonstrated a haemoglobin concentration consistent with profound anaemia. ECG demonstrated a right bundle branch block, left axis deviation, and a prolonged PR interval, indicating significant conduction-system disease in the context of previous ischaemic myocardial injury. Serum biochemistry demonstrated elevated creatinine and urea, alongside a severely reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate, consistent with severe renal dysfunction. Venous blood gas analysis further showed a low pH and elevated lactate, indicating significant metabolic acidosis. The clinical picture suggested an interaction between severe blood-loss anaemia, impaired cardiovascular compensatory reserve, postural haemodynamic stress, and renal hypoperfusion. Severe anaemia substantially reduces arterial oxygen content, necessitating compensatory increases in cardiac output and oxygen extraction. When cardiovascular reserve is already compromised, this compensation may be inadequate. Emergency packed red blood cell transfusion and careful fluid-volume optimisation were undertaken. Given the recurrent collapse and significant conduction abnormalities, an urgent cardiology transfer was arranged for permanent pacemaker insertion. Severe renal dysfunction prompted urgent nephrology involvement and transfer.
title: Active Exsanguination Behind a Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) Diagnostic Label: A Quadruple-Hit Cardiorenal Collapse Following Ambulatory Urological Care.

abstract: In-stent restenosis (ISR) remains a major complication following vascular interventions, with neointimal hyperplasia representing a central pathological process that can adversely affect postoperative outcomes. Accumulating evidence indicates that neointimal hyperplasia is driven by vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic transition, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and multiple forms of programmed cell death. Despite substantial advances, the underlying pathogenic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This review comprehensively examines neointimal hyperplasia from the perspectives of epidemiology, pathophysiology, preclinical animal models, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic strategies. Particular attention is given to the emerging associations between recently characterized forms of programmed cell death, including ferroptosis and cuproptosis, and neointimal hyperplasia. In addition, commonly used preclinical animal models are reviewed, together with potential therapeutic approaches such as colchicine and vasostatin-2 and their underlying mechanisms. The diagnostic roles of invasive imaging and noninvasive modalities in evaluating neointimal hyperplasia are discussed, with emphasis on their respective advantages and limitations. Furthermore, current stent-based strategies, pharmacological therapies, and alternative interventions for ISR are summarized, along with critical consideration of their limitations and potential avenues for improvement. By integrating mechanistic evidence with available therapeutic options, this review aims to provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for the clinical management of ISR.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Influenza-induced rhabdomyolysis is an uncommon but serious complication that can cause life-threatening hyperkalemia. The use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) for hyperkalemic cardiac arrest has rarely been described.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 48-year-old woman with influenza A developed severe rhabdomyolysis (creatine kinase: 255,240 U/L) and progressive hyperkalemia despite improved renal function and continuous renal replacement therapy. On hospital day 3, the patient experienced a hyperkalemic cardiac arrest and VA-ECMO was initiated after 29 min of low-flow time. Treatment for hyperkalemia was continued, and cardiac function gradually recovered, allowing the removal of ECMO on day 8. However, she later developed hemorrhagic complications related to mechanical circulatory support and died on hospital day 89.
CONCLUSION: Influenza-induced rhabdomyolysis can cause rapid, life-threatening hyperkalemia, even in patients with improving renal function. Temporary mechanical circulatory support may serve as a bridge through the acute reversible phase, and device-related complications should be considered.

title: Influenza-Induced Rhabdomyolysis Leading to Hyperkalemic Cardiac Arrest Managed With Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT scans to quantify volumes (L/m2) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure).
RESULTS: Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77-90]; 58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile range, 14-36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.
title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP) is rapidly released following myocardial injury, but its prognostic significance in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between elevated H-FABP and adverse clinical outcomes in confirmed or suspected ACS.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science and Scopus were searched from inception to 30 August 2026 without date restriction. Studies assessing diagnostic and/or prognostic relevance of circulating H-FABP in adults with confirmed or suspected ACS were eligible. Prognostic outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), heart failure (HF)-related hospitalisation and recurrent myocardial infarction (MI). Risk of bias was assessed using QUIPS. Crude odds ratios (ORs) from extractable 2 × 2 event data were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation.
RESULTS: Twelve studies were included, with five contributing to meta-analysis. Elevated H-FABP was associated with higher odds of all-cause mortality (OR 5.68; 95% CI 3.98-8.09; I2 = 30%), MACE (OR 4.56; 95% CI 1.97-10.55; I2 = 47%), HF-related hospitalisation (OR 4.29; 95% CI 2.94-6.26; I2 = 0%) and recurrent MI (OR 1.65; 95% CI 1.15-2.37; I2 = 0%). Pooled estimates were unadjusted; seven studies were synthesised narratively.
CONCLUSION: Elevated H-FABP is associated with adverse outcomes in ACS, but current evidence does not establish independent prognostic value. Further prospective studies should determine whether H-FABP adds predictive value beyond established clinical and biochemical risk markers.
title: Prognostic Value of Heart-Type Fatty Acid-Binding Protein in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract: Left ventricular dysfunction and thrombosis in unrepaired tetralogy of Fallot are rarely reported. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy with unrepaired tetralogy of Fallot, severe biventricular dysfunction, large left ventricular thrombus, and diffuse subendocardial fibroelastosis. After surgical repair, recovery of ventricular function and thrombus resolution were observed. This case highlights the interplay between cyanosis, myocardial remodelling, and hypercoagulability and emphasises the role of multimodality imaging.
title: Left ventricular dysfunction and massive intracavitary thrombus in unrepaired tetralogy of Fallot with endomyocardial fibroelastosis: a case report.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Ozaki procedure reconstructs the aortic valve with autologous pericardium, but long-term leaflet durability remains uncertain. Coronary artery disease (CAD) may reflect a systemic atheroinflammatory milieu associated with impaired leaflet integrity.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 733 patients undergoing Ozaki reconstruction from 2015 to 2020 and assessed the association between CAD and aortic regurgitation (AR) ≥ 2 at last echocardiographic follow-up. Baseline heterogeneity was addressed using propensity-score overlap weighting based on age, sex, body mass index, body surface area, weight, diabetes, European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II, aortic stenosis, bicuspid valve, and peripheral artery disease. Effects were estimated as weighted risk ratios (RRs) using Poisson models with robust variance. Sensitivity analyses used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and an extended model including prior myocardial infarction/percutaneous coronary intervention.
RESULTS: Of 733 patients, 365 (49.8%) had CAD. Unadjusted AR > 2 rates were 10.1% in CAD vs. 5.7% in no-CAD patients (P = 0.037). After overlap weighting, weighted risks were 12.7% vs. 6.2%, yielding RR 2.05 (95% CI, 1.01 - 4.18; P = 0.048), with excellent covariate balance. IPTW showed consistent results: RR 2.22 (95% CI, 1.38 - 3.56; P = 0.001). Regurgitation-free survival was lower in CAD patients (log-rank P = 0.0087).
CONCLUSION: CAD was associated with an approximately two-fold higher risk of AR ≥ 2 after Ozaki reconstruction. This association likely reflects systemic atheroinflammatory processes rather than a direct mechanical effect, supporting closer postoperative surveillance in CAD patients.
title: Impact of Coronary Artery Disease on Long-Term Valve Function After the Ozaki Procedure: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study (2015 - 2020).

abstract: Background Poor outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) may reflect microvascular dysfunction, or no-reflow phenomenon, but operational definitions are lacking. Purpose To identify the most informative candidate no-reflow definition at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging for outcome assessment. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis used data from two prospective multicenter imaging registries of patients with acute stroke who were recruited between June 2016 and July 2022, achieved modified thrombolysis in cerebral infarction grade 2c or 3 recanalization after EVT, and underwent pre-EVT and 24-hour post-EVT CT or MR perfusion imaging. Candidate no-reflow definitions were evaluated across eight perfusion maps and their corresponding stepwise thresholds. Delay time (DT) quantifies the delay in contrast material arrival between arterial input and brain tissue. For primary screening, no-reflow status was defined as any residual hypoperfusion lesion for each map-threshold combination. The best-performing combination was evaluated using residual volume and reperfusion index cutoffs. The primary outcome was poor 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score >2); infarct growth was secondary. Associations with the outcome were evaluated using multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression. Results The primary cohort included 67 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 56-77 years]; 41 male), and the independent cohort comprised 54 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 62-78 years]; 28 female). In the primary cohort, lesions with DT longer than 4 seconds showed the strongest discrimination for poor 90-day functional outcome (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.72 [95% CI: 0.57, 0.86]; P < .001). According to this definition, 14 of 67 patients (21%) had no reflow. Poor functional outcome occurred in 11 of 14 patients (79%) with no reflow and 11 of 53 (21%) with reflow (odds ratio, 12.14 [95% CI: 3.38, 54.63]; P < .001). Infarct growth was greater with no-reflow status than with reflow (median, 24.1 mL [IQR, 3.7-40.7 mL] vs 0 mL [IQR, -10.1 to 6.1 mL]; P < .001). Findings were consistent in the independent cohort. Conclusion The presence of a lesion with DT longer than 4 seconds at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging appeared to be the most informative candidate no-reflow definition. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Gemmete in this issue.
title: No Reflow at Perfusion Imaging: Thresholds That Distinguish Functional and Tissue Outcome Groups in Acute Stroke.
Beyond Recanalization: Defining Cerebral No-Reflow Status after Thrombectomy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous debulking of left-sided endocarditis and thrombus has previously relied on cerebral-only embolic protection devices. The Emboliner is an investigational nitinol-mesh filter that provides whole-body embolic protection and has been studied in transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
SUMMARY: We describe its first reported use as an adjunct to AngioVac-based debulking in 2 patients: 1 with aortic valve endocarditis and 1 with combined tricuspid and mitral endocarditis.
DISCUSSION: The Emboliner was successfully deployed in both cases, with over 90% of vegetation removed and no periprocedural or in-hospital embolic events. Deployment technique differed by vegetation location: in the aortic valve case, the AngioVac cannula was advanced through the filter's access port; in the tricuspid/mitral case, no further interaction with the filter was required once deployed.
NOVELTY: This represents, to our knowledge, the first reported use of whole-body embolic protection during aortic and combined tricuspid/mitral percutaneous endocarditis debulking.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Whole-body embolic protection may offer an important adjunct to percutaneous debulking in patients at high surgical risk.
title: Percutaneous Multivalvular Endocarditis Debulking With a Whole-Body Embolic Protection Device.

abstract: Glossopharyngeal nerve block (GPNB) can provide effective anesthesia for procedures involving the oropharynx and upper airway. Ultrasound-guided GPNB (UGPNB) may be particularly useful when conventional sedation or topical anesthesia is undesirable because of the risk of respiratory or cardiovascular complications. In this article, we report the use of UGPNB as an alternative anesthetic technique for gastroduodenal endoscopy in a 57-year-old male patient with AMI and gastrointestinal bleeding. In this patient requiring emergency endoscopy, UGPNB was performed via the peristyloid approach to provide oropharyngeal anesthesia while minimizing the need for sedation. The block effectively suppressed the gag reflex and provided adequate procedural conditions while maintaining hemodynamic stability. No procedure-related complications or adverse effects were observed, and the patient reported no discomfort following the procedure. In conclusion, UGPNB may be a useful alternative to sedation for endoscopy in high-risk cardiac patients.

title: Ultrasound-guided glossopharyngeal nerve block for safe and effective anesthesia in a critically ill patient with acute myocardial infarction undergoing urgent endoscopy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary bifurcation lesions remain one of the most challenging lesions. In particular, satisfactory clinical outcomes have not yet been achieved for side branches. The use of drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has demonstrated acceptable clinical outcomes in native coronary arteries. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of additional DCB inflation in the side branches of bifurcation lesions.
METHODS: The OCVC-BIF study (Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branch of Bifurcation Lesions) was conducted as a multicenter, randomized, open-label trial. Patients with bifurcation lesions scheduled for drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation in the main vessel followed by kissing balloon inflation were enrolled in the study. The patients were randomized to receive either additional dilatation of the side branch using a DCB after DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation (DCB group) or only DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation using conventional balloons (non-DCB group). The primary end point was restenosis of the side branch, assessed using scheduled coronary angiography at 9 months or symptom-driven coronary angiography during the 1-year follow-up. Restenosis was defined as ≥50% stenosis of the side branch, determined using 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography. The key secondary end points included major adverse cardiac events at 12 months, which were defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, clinically driven target lesion revascularization, and stent thrombosis.
RESULTS: In total, 299 patients were randomized into the DCB (151 patients) and non-DCB (148 patients) groups between October 2019 and September 2024. Serial 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography evaluation was performed in 262 (87.6%) patients. The restenosis rate was lower in the DCB group than that in the non-DCB group (8.1% versus 18.3%, P=0.012). However, the incidence of major adverse cardiac events at 12 months was similar between them (10.1% versus 12.4%, P=0.58).
CONCLUSIONS: Additional DCB inflation in the side branch after main-vessel DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation decreases restenosis in the side branch in the treatment of bifurcation lesions.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/en-latest-detail/jRCTs052200077; Unique identifier: jRCTs052200077.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre, randomised, open-label trial; 299 patients (151 DCB, 148 non-DCB).
appraisal.main_limitation: The primary endpoint is angiographic, and the trial was not powered for clinical events; open-label design.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre open-label randomised trial in Japan found that adding a drug-coated balloon to the side branch after main-vessel DES and kissing inflation lowered angiographic side-branch restenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Restenosis rate was lower in the DCB group than in the non-DCB group (8.1% versus 18.3%, P=0.012); MACE at 12 months was similar (10.1% versus 12.4%, P=0.58).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bifurcation side-branch treatment is common and DCB use there lacks randomised evidence, so this informs a technique decision, though clinical benefit remains unshown.

title: Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branches of Bifurcation Lesions: OCVC-BIF Study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Age-based comparisons in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) often use a binary young-older framework, which may obscure premature non-young disease. We evaluated age-group patterns in measured modifiable risk factors, angiographic complexity, inflammatory-metabolic indices, and in-hospital outcomes in patients presenting with first STEMI.
METHOD: This single-center retrospective study screened 421 STEMI records between January 2019 and May 2026. After exclusions, 150 patients were selected from an eligible pool of 229 using sex-stratified, equal-size quota sampling. The groups were defined as young STEMI (≤45 years), premature non-young STEMI (men 46-55 years, women 46-65 years), and older STEMI (men >55 years, women >65 years). Measured four-component standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factor (SMuRF) burden, angiographic findings, SYNTAX score, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet score (HALP), C-reactive protein/albumin ratio (CAR), mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were analyzed. Two multivariable models were used to assess age group and SYNTAX score.
RESULTS: Smoking prevalence decreased across groups, whereas diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and measured four-component SMuRF burden increased with age. Thrombus was most frequently observed in young STEMI. SYNTAX score, multivessel disease, SYNTAX ≥23, SII, and CAR increased with age, whereas HALP decreased. Non-smoking SMuRF burden distinguished premature non-young STEMI and older STEMI from young STEMI; older STEMI was independently associated with a higher SYNTAX score. No significant differences in mortality or MACE were detected.
CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort, young STEMI was characterized by smoking predominance, a higher prevalence of angiographic thrombus, and lower coronary complexity, whereas older STEMI showed greater measured four-component SMuRF burden, increased coronary complexity, and less favorable inflammatory-metabolic indices. No differences were detected in in-hospital mortality or MACE.
journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
title: Age Phenotypes, Angiographic Complexity, and Inflammatory-Metabolic Profiles in First-Presentation STEMI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: As total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) is increasing in volume, limited data exist regarding how recent myocardial infarction (MI) influences postoperative outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of MI timing, type, treatment, and anatomical location on rates of postoperative cardiac, medical, and surgical complications following TSA.
METHODS: A national insurance database, PearlDiver, was queried to identify patients with a history of MI within two years prior to TSA. These patients were propensity-matched 1:4 to controls without prior MI based on demographics and comorbidities. The MI cohort was stratified by timing (0-6 months, 6-12 months, 12-18 months, 18-24 months), and subgroup analyses were performed by MI type (Type 1 vs. Type 2), ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) vs Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI) classification, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), and infarct location.
RESULTS: A history of MI within 2 years preceding TSA had a strong association with higher odds of postoperative MI (OR 5.67; 95% CI, 3.86-8.32). The strongest association was observed when MI occurred within 6 months of TSA (OR 9.95; 95% CI, 6.50-15.24). Type 1 MI was strongly associated with postoperative MI, particularly within 6 months (OR 10.86; 95% CI, 6.96-16.95). Type 2 MI within 6 months was strongly associated with postoperative MI (OR 10.69; 95% CI, 2.50-45.63), DVT (OR 9.81; 95% CI, 2.30-41.79), and PJI (OR 5.24; 95% CI, 1.60-17.18). Both STEMI (OR = 6.17) and NSTEMI (OR = 5.77) were strongly associated with postoperative MI. Anterior MI was strongly associated with postoperative MI (OR 7.22; 95% CI, 3.36-15.49), whereas inferior MI was strongly associated with 90-day mortality (OR 6.46; 95% CI, 1.85-22.60).
CONCLUSION: MI within 2 years and specifically 6 months of TSA was associated with higher odds of postoperative complications. MI timing, subtype, treatment, and location should be carefully weighed when considering TSA in this high-risk population.
journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
title: Myocardial Infarction Within 6 Months before Total Shoulder Arthroplasty is Strongly Associated with Postoperative Complications.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early risk stratification in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is essential but established scores such as TIMI and GRACE require multivariable computation. The Shock Index-Creatinine (SIC) is a simpler bedside alternative, yet Indian data are sparse.
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether admission SIC predicts in-hospital adverse events in anterior wall STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHODS: Two hundred consecutive patients with anterior wall STEMI undergoing primary PCI at a tertiary care centre in northern India were prospectively enrolled over 12 months. SIC was computed at admission as (Shock Index × 100) - Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance. The primary outcome was in-hospital death; secondary outcomes were heart failure, cardiogenic shock, contrast-induced acute kidney injury (CI-AKI), and life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia. Discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: The cohort was 73.0% male with a mean age of 54.5 years; in-hospital mortality was 10.0% (n = 20). Admission SIC was markedly higher in non-survivors than survivors (82.0 ± 42.4 versus -20.1 ± 19.4; p < 0.001). AUCs were 0.992 for mortality and cardiogenic shock, 0.971 for CI-AKI, 0.909 for ventricular arrhythmia, and 0.907 for heart failure (all p < 0.001). A SIC ≥ 20 predicted death with 95.0% sensitivity and 98.9% specificity.
CONCLUSIONS: In this Indian cohort, admission SIC was a powerful bedside predictor of adverse in-hospital events after primary PCI for anterior wall STEMI. The unusually high discriminative performance requires external validation in larger multicentre populations before routine clinical adoption.
title: Shock Index-Creatinine as a Predictor of In-Hospital Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Anterior Wall ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract: Propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS) has been described in patients requiring prolonged sedation with this drug, as may occur in some cases after cardiac surgery. Its treatment is based on discontinuation of the drug and supportive management of organ dysfunction until resolution. In the postoperative period of cardiac surgery, diagnosing PRIS poses a challenge, since it must be differentiated from other, more common complications such as postcardiotomy shock. In these patients, PRIS may fatally worsen the prognosis. Veno-arterial ECMO therapy may help maintain cardiac output. Both the diagnosis of PRIS after cardiac surgery and its treatment with ECMO have been scarcely reported. We present a case of PRIS after cardiac surgery successfully managed with ECMO.
journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion
title: Veno-arterial ECMO for the management of propofol infusion syndrome following cardiac surgery.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic regurgitation (AR) causes left ventricular (LV) volume overload, while transvalvular Impella support may permit regurgitant recirculation. We constructed schematic pressure-volume (PV) loops to illustrate the interaction between ventricular unloading and systemic perfusion in severe AR.
METHODS: Conceptual LV PV loops were constructed from established principles of ventricular mechanics to depict progressive AR, cardiogenic shock (CS), and alternative hypothetical responses to Impella support. No patient-specific measurements or numerical simulation were used.
RESULTS: Increasing AR was depicted by rightward PV-loop displacement and greater LV volume excursion without quantifying effective forward stroke volume. The hypothetical transition to CS showed lower LV pressure and greater end-systolic volume. During Impella support, a leftward loop shift and smaller enclosed area were compatible with unloading; regurgitant recirculation could offset its benefit and permit recurrent LV distension. Pump flow, regurgitant flow, and effective systemic output could not be derived from the loops.
CONCLUSIONS: This qualitative framework illustrates a plausible hemodynamic paradox: LV unloading during Impella support may coexist with limited improvement in net systemic perfusion in severe AR. It does not establish the magnitude or temporal sequence of these responses.
title: Pressure-volume loop reconstruction of Impella support in severe aortic regurgitation: explaining a hemodynamic paradox.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) frequently present with advanced right heart failure (RHF), commonly attributed to delayed referral for intervention. Whether this reflects delayed referral or the stage at which severe TR is first documented remains uncertain.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 625 consecutive patients with a first echocardiographic diagnosis of severe TR. RHF severity was classified using a validated hierarchical staging system (Stages 1-4). In a subgroup of 310 patients with a previous echocardiogram documenting non-severe TR, RHF stage was retrospectively assessed before severe TR was first documented. Two-year all-cause mortality was evaluated.
RESULTS: At first documentation of severe TR, 66.4% of patients were classified as Stage 3 and 17.3% as Stage 4, whereas only 16.3% were in Stages 1-2. Functional TR accounted for 85% of cases. RHF stage was associated with progressively higher TRI-SCORE and two-year mortality. Among patients with prior non-severe TR, 78% were already in Stage 3-4 before severe TR was first documented, whereas only 7% had reached Stage 4.
CONCLUSIONS: Severe TR was predominantly diagnosed in patients with stage 3-4 RHF. Higher RHF stages were already present in most patients before severe TR was first documented. These findings suggest that delayed referral alone may not fully explain the advanced clinical profile of severe TR and that eligibility for guideline-directed intervention frequently coincides with an already advanced stage of disease.
title: Advanced right heart failure stage at first documentation of severe tricuspid regurgitation: beyond the late-referral paradigm.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In this study we investigated temporal trends, indications, practice variation, and outcomes associated with intravascular imaging (IVI) use in a large, multicenter chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) registry.
METHODS: We analyzed CTO PCIs performed at 76 US and international centers in 2012-2026 in the PROGRESS-CTO registry. Patients were categorized according to IVI use. P value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Among 18,024 CTO PCIs, IVI was used in 10,569 procedures (58.6%). IVI use increased over time. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was the predominant modality, accounting for 98.1% of IVI-guided procedures. Following 1:1 propensity score matching, technical (85.8% vs 78.8%; p < 0.001) and procedural success (83.6% vs 78.1%, p = 0.003) remained higher in the IVUS-to-cross group. Difference was also pronounced when IVUS was used to cross ambiguous proximal cap: technical success was 85.1% versus 75.9% (OR, 1.81; 95% CI, 1.49-2.21), and procedural success was 83.0% versus 75.1% (OR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.34-1.99). Centers contributing <100 cases had lower IVI use than centers contributing ≥100 cases (47.7% vs 58.7%; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: IVI use during CTO PCI continues to increase. Procedures in which IVUS was used to facilitate lesion crossing were associated with higher technical and procedural success rates and similar in-hospital MACE rates. The association with success was also pronounced when IVUS was used to resolve proximal cap ambiguity. IVI use varied significantly among participating centers, highlighting differences in practice patterns and adoption of IVI during CTO PCI.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis (PROGRESS-CTO); 18,024 CTO PCIs at 76 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with operator-selected imaging and residual confounding; outcomes are procedural success rather than long-term events.
appraisal.one_line: Large multicentre CTO PCI registry analysis of intravascular imaging use, with higher technical and procedural success when IVUS was used to cross.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After 1:1 propensity score matching, technical success (85.8% vs 78.8%; p < 0.001) and procedural success (83.6% vs 78.1%, p = 0.003) remained higher in the IVUS-to-cross group.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Describes uptake and practice variation of imaging in CTO PCI and supports a possible randomised evaluation of IVUS-guided crossing.

title: Temporal trends and outcomes of intravascular imaging in chronic total occlusion interventions: insights from the PROGRESS-CTO registry.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Despite advances in coronary intervention and secondary prevention, patients without diabetes who experience acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remain at elevated cardiovascular risk. Metformin has pleiotropic cardiovascular effects beyond glucose lowering, but its role after ACS in people without diabetes is uncertain.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: MetCool ACS is a multicentre, prospective, quasi-randomised, open-label trial enrolling 1000 adults without diabetes hospitalised for ACS and treated with successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stent implantation. Allocation is determined by the second digit of the Polish national identification number: even digits allocate to metformin and odd digits to standard care (allocation 1:1). Participants allocated to metformin will receive dose-escalated therapy to 850 mg three times a day (2550 mg/day) for 24 months, followed by 6 months of post-treatment follow-up (total 30 months). The primary endpoint is unplanned coronary revascularisation (PCI or coronary artery bypass grafting) within 30 months after the index ACS-related revascularisation. Secondary endpoints include cardiac death, all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke and safety outcomes. Time-to-event outcomes will be analysed using appropriate survival analysis methods, including Kaplan-Meier estimates, log-rank testing and Cox proportional hazards models, with competing-risk methods applied where appropriate. Detailed statistical methods will be prespecified in the statistical analysis plan. Protocol version: 3.1/2023 (10 January 2023).
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study was approved by the Bioethics Committee at the Military Institute of Medicine (Resolution 55/WIM/2020; 18 November 2020) and the Bioethics Committee at the Military Chamber of Physicians (Resolution 31/23; 27 October 2023). All participants provide written informed consent. Results will be disseminated primarily through peer-reviewed publication and scientific meetings. The trial is covered by clinical trial insurance, including coverage for potential claims arising from harm related to participation in the trial. Any compensation for trial-related harm will be provided in accordance with applicable regulations and the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBERS: EudraCT 2020-004962-21; EU CT 2024-516589-13-00; NCT05305898.
title: MetCool ACS: study protocol for a multicentre quasi-randomised trial of metformin in patients without diabetes after acute coronary syndrome in Poland.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) accounts for around one in ten hospitalisations with acute myocardial infarction. Despite guideline recommendations, diagnostic and management approaches vary. We aimed to characterise current UK practice for the investigation and treatment of patients with MINOCA.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of UK clinicians involved in MINOCA care between March and December 2025. To provide clinical context, two clinical vignettes with probable non-ischaemic (Case A) and ischaemic (Case B) aetiologies were used to assess investigation preferences, with agreement documented using a Likert scale from 0 to 5 and reported as the proportion agreeing or strongly agreeing (score 4 or 5). General management questions and free-text responses underwent thematic analysis by two independent reviewers.
RESULTS: Of 146 respondents, 140 provided demographic data. Most were cardiology consultants (76/140, 54.3%) from tertiary centres (74/140, 52.9%). Echocardiography received high endorsement across both vignettes (Case A: 93/99 (93.9%) vs Case B: 86/88 (97.7%) agreeing or strongly agreeing). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging preferences differed between vignettes: 83/101 (82.2%) agreed or strongly agreed with CMR for the younger patient with viral prodrome versus 38/86 (44.2%) for the older patient with atheroma (p<0.001). Hyperaemic (adenosine) coronary microvascular function testing was endorsed by 14/100 (14.0%) and 18/88 (20.5%), respectively, and no respondent endorsed acetylcholine provocation testing in either vignette. Thematic analysis identified four themes: context-dependence of decisions, uncertainty regarding diagnostic utility, psychological burden on patients and concerns about MINOCA terminology.
CONCLUSIONS: UK clinicians demonstrate considerable variation in the investigation of patients with MINOCA, with clinical presentation strongly influencing recommendations for CMR imaging. Although the vignettes differed in several clinical features, the extent of variation in investigation preferences highlights the absence of a standardised diagnostic approach. These findings support the need for evidence-based care pathways incorporating refined case definitions and more precise terminology.
title: Heterogeneity in the diagnostic management of MINOCA: a UK clinician survey.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Discharge N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a recognised prognostic marker after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), but its value after surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) remains uncertain, possibly reflecting differences in perioperative physiology.
AIMS: To compare the prognostic utility of discharge NT-proBNP after TAVR versus SAVR in patients with severe aortic stenosis and preserved ejection fraction, and to examine the association between NT-proBNP reduction and Left Ventricular Mass Index (LVMI) regression.
METHODS: This propensity-matched cohort study included 556 patients (TAVR, n=278; SAVR, n=278) with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% treated at a single centre (2019–2023). The primary endpoint was a 2-year composite of all-cause death or heart failure rehospitalisation.
RESULTS: After matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced. Discharge NT-proBNP >1000 pg/mL predicted lower event-free survival after TAVR (77.3% vs 91.4%; adjusted HR 3.21, 95% CI 1.96 to 5.26, p<0.001) but not after SAVR (83.8% vs 86.7%; adjusted HR 1.18, p=0.50; p for interaction=0.008). Longer aortic cross-clamp time progressively abolished NT-proBNP prognostic value in SAVR. NT-proBNP reduction correlated with LVMI regression regardless of procedure (β=2.2 per 10% ΔNT-proBNP%, p<0.001). A 6-month NT-proBNP ≤1000 pg/mL identified favourable outcomes irrespective of procedure (adjusted HR 0.51, p=0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Discharge NT-proBNP predicts outcomes after TAVR but not SAVR, likely due to cardiopulmonary bypass-induced inflammation. NT-proBNP reduction correlates with LVMI regression irrespective of procedure. Risk stratification may be optimised by discharge measurement after TAVR and 6-month reassessment after SAVR.
title: Discharge NT-proBNP predicts 2-year outcomes after TAVR but not after SAVR in preserved ejection fraction: a propensity-matched cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prehospital point-of-care high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) may support earlier triage of adults with suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS). We assessed its short-term economic consequences compared with standard emergency department (ED)-based care in France.
METHODS: We developed a decision-analytic, continuous-time semi-Markov model over a 24-hour horizon using individual patient data from the prospective, multicentre, double-blinded cohort study (VALIDATE) conducted across four French hospitals (July 2021-May 2024; n = 737). The reference analysis adopted a restricted prehospital-and-ED perspective covering measured medical and paramedical resources from first emergency medical service contact through ED disposition (states 1-3). A complementary database audit searched for patients recorded with less than 24 h of follow-up in an extended "prehospital, emergency department and hospital" setting. None were identified; inpatient, intensive care unit (ICU), coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) costs were therefore excluded from the reference-case totals. The initial hs-cTnI H0 sample was obtained before hospital arrival, whereas subsequent H1 or H3 samples, when required, were intended to be collected after arrival. Costs were reported in 2025 euros. Sampling uncertainty was assessed using 1,000 non-parametric bootstrap replications and scenario analyses examined clinically relevant subgroups (> 3 h since symptom onset; availability of a prehospital HEART score).
RESULTS: Among 737 participants (mean age 65.4 years; 58.8% men), 77 (10.4%) had non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. ED attendance was lower with hs-cTnI than with standard care (90.9% [95% CI 88.6-92.8] vs. 96.7% [95% CI 95.2-97.8]; absolute difference - 5.8% points [95% CI - 9.2 to - 2.4]; P < 0.001). Among ED attendees, mean ED length of stay was 1.63 h versus 2.76 h (P < 0.001). Mean prehospital-and-ED cost per patient was €185.24 with hs-cTnI and €268.55 with standard care, a saving of €83.31 ([95% CI 70.81-96.60]; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Within the restricted 24-hour prehospital-and-ED perspective supported by the available patient-level data, a strategy beginning with prehospital hs-cTnI testing was associated with fewer ED attendances, shorter ED stays and lower costs. Longer-term evaluations are planned because these findings do not establish system-wide for inpatient, wider organisational, patient and societal costs.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The VALIDATE study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04950244).
title: Cost-effectiveness of prehospital high-sensitivity troponin i testing versus standard emergency department care in patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome in France.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a devastating complication following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Coronary microcirculatory dysfunction (CMD) is implicated in adverse post-STEMI outcomes, but its relationship with subsequent stroke is unknown. We aimed to investigate the association of the coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (caIMR), a novel non-invasive tool for assessing CMD, for new-onset ischemic stroke in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI).
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study enrolled 602 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent successful pPCI between July 2020 and February 2025. The caIMR was calculated post-procedure using specialized software. The primary endpoint was new-onset ischemic stroke. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess the association between caIMR and stroke risk.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 29.3 months, 38 patients (6.3%) developed a new-onset ischemic stroke. In the multivariable Cox model, caIMR was independently associated with the risk of ischemic stroke (HR: 1.044, 95% CI: 1.022-1.065, P < 0.001), along with new-onset atrial fibrillation (HR: 9.113, 95% CI: 4.587-18.107, P < 0.001). A linear dose-response relationship was observed between caIMR levels and the risk of stroke (P for non-linearity = 0.975). Reclassification analysis showed that adding caIMR improved risk classification, with an IDI of 0.0307 (95% CI: 0.0031-0.0636; P = 0.030) and an NRI of 0.3887 (95% CI: 0.3156-0.4618; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Elevated caIMR is independently associated with an increased risk of long-term ischemic stroke in STEMI patients after pPCI. This easily accessible metric may serve as a valuable tool for future risk stratification in this patient population.
keywords: Coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance
title: Association between coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance and ischemic stroke in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-eluting stents (DES) have significantly reduced the incidence of in-stent restenosis (ISR). However, a subset of patients still develop refractory, rapidly progressive, and diffuse ISR, which poses substantial therapeutic challenges and reflects its complex underlying mechanisms.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 46-year-old male who underwent five percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) over five years, with repeated diffuse ISR in the left anterior descending artery (LAD). Initial PCI was followed by DCB therapy after first ISR, achieving temporary symptom relief. Four years later, ISR progressed to chronic total occlusion, requiring further stenting and DCB therapy. Within five months, he developed 99% LM stenosis and recurrent LAD ISR. Despite a SYNTAX score of 36 favoring CABG, the patient refused surgery. Under intra-aortic balloon pump support, a balloon-only PCI (stent-less) strategy was performed. IVUS revealed diffuse fibrous proliferation and neoatherosclerosis. During follow-up, the patient remained clinically stable overall.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights a potential systemic hyperproliferative phenotype, in which repeated vascular injury triggers accelerated neoatherosclerosis and intimal hyperplasia. It challenges the conventional view of ISR as a local mechanical problem and underscores the importance of mechanism-driven risk stratification and individualized management, particularly when standard surgical therapy is declined.
title: Refractory rapidly progressive diffuse in-stent restenosis with left main involvement: a case report.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether preload with colloids could reduce hypotension during induction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared to crystalloids.
METHODS: This study is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled trial conducted at Xijing Hospital. A total of 116 patients scheduled for elective TAVR under general anesthesia will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the colloid group or the crystalloid group, receiving either 5 ml/kg of colloid or crystalloid solution before anesthesia induction infused over 15 min. The primary outcome is the area under curve (AUC) of the change in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from baseline during the induction period (until 15 min after induction). Secondary outcomes include the incidence of intraoperative hemodynamic instability, the use of intraoperative vasoactive drugs, the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on the first postoperative day, postoperative hospital length of stay, the rate of intensive care unit (ICU) admission postoperatively, all-cause mortality during hospitalization and by 30 days after surgery, and the incidence of renal replacement therapy by 30 days after surgery.
DISCUSSION: The results of this study will provide evidence on optimizing fluid preload to prevent hypotension during induction, reduce postoperative complications, and enhance recovery for patients undergoing TAVR. The findings are expected to promote anesthesia protocols in this patient population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol and statistical analysis plan were approved by the institutional Ethics Committee of Xijing Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University (XJLL-KY-20252560). The study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07329660) on December 29, 2025.
title: Crystalloid vs colloid for Hemodynamics during Anesthesia INduction in TAVR patients (CHAIN-T): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery anomalies are anatomical abnormalities involving abnormal origin, course, or termination of any of the three main epicardial arteries. These abnormalities may go unnoticed during a person's lifetime; however, they can occasionally present acutely or chronically as angina, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmias, or even sudden cardiac death.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 65-year-old woman with angina and stress-induced ST-segment depression in a treadmill test. Coronary angiography showed the absence of the left main coronary artery with separate origins of the left anterior descending artery and circumflex artery. During a planned cardiac computed tomography angiography scan, the patient presented with cardiac arrest secondary to ventricular fibrillation and was hospitalized. A high-risk interarterial course of the left anterior descending artery was identified, and coronary artery bypass grafting with surgical mobilization of the left anterior descending artery along its interarterial course, where it was ligated with a hemoclip prior to the first septal branch to prevent competitive flow. The postoperative course was uneventful.
CONCLUSIONS: When this rare anomaly is detected in the population, clinicians must identify the risk of fatal events and determine appropriate management based on age, symptoms, vascular anatomy, and the presence of arrhythmia.
title: Sudden cardiac arrest during diagnostic workup: a rare case of high-risk interarterial left anterior descending artery anomaly.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perivalvular leak (PVL), valve embolization, and migration of valve in mitral position are critical complications of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). To date, rescue strategies, and outcomes following unsuccessful initial TMVR deployment remain poorly documented.
METHODS: Between March 2016 and December 2024, 86 patients with high risk of open-heart surgery underwent TMVR with a balloon expandable valve at a single institution. 19.8% (17/86) of patients experienced unsuccessful first TMVR (unsuccessful group) due to valve embolization, migration, significant PVL, or pericardial effusion, whereas 80.2% (69/86) had successful first TMVR (successful group). We evaluated postoperative outcomes comparing unsuccessful to successful groups.
RESULTS: Among 17 patients with unsuccessful first TMVR, 70.6% (12/17) underwent additional valve deployment, with successful valve-in-valve implantation in 75.0% (9/12). 17.6% (3/17) developed valve embolization in left atrium after transcatheter rescue procedures or additional valve deployment failed, subsequently 66.7% (2/3) required emergent surgical explantation of embolized valves, 33.3% (1/3) was managed medically due to prohibitive surgical risk. Surgical patients were discharged home without complications. Early mortality in unsuccessful group was 29.4% (5/17) and 13.0% (9/69) in successful group. There was no significant difference in early mortality between the 2 groups (p = 0.10). Median follow-up term was 10 months. Cumulative survival rate in 12 months was 50.5% in unsuccessful group, and 60.0% in successful group. Mid-term outcomes were similar between the 2 groups (p = 0.34).
CONCLUSIONS: The study was underpowered to detect differences in all-cause mortality, but unsuccessful deployment was associated with substantially higher numerical early mortality and significantly higher cardiac mortality.
title: Outcomes of rescue procedures in patients undergoing unsuccessful deployment of transcatheter mitral valve replacement.

abstract: BACKGROUND High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) carries significant mortality, and management becomes complex when it coexists with severe anemia and active bleeding, as thrombolysis is then contraindicated. We report the case of a patient with high-risk PE complicated by severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L) and active uterine bleeding from adenomyosis. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old woman presented with haemodynamic instability (blood pressure 74/47 mm Hg), critical anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), and a 3-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding from adenomyosis. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed bilateral PE with right pulmonary artery main-trunk occlusion; echocardiography showed severe pulmonary hypertension, and duplex ultrasound showed extensive left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis. Thrombolysis was contraindicated. Emergency percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy was performed using large-bore catheters (22F, 20F, 16F) with concurrent inferior vena cava filter placement, reducing pulmonary artery pressure from 51/23 to 34/12 mm Hg; the estimated blood loss, quantified from filtered aspirate, was approximately 100 mL. Adjuncts included transfusion of 13 units of packed red cells, dilatation and curettage, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy, and titrated anticoagulation. At discharge after a 24-day hospitalization she was hemodynamically stable, and free of dyspnea, with resolved edema and hemoglobin 72 g/L, on oral rivaroxaban. CONCLUSIONS In this thrombolysis-contraindicated patient, aspiration thrombectomy with inferior vena cava filter placement was a feasible rescue strategy that achieved rapid hemodynamic and angiographic improvement without thrombolysis, with palliative rather than curative intent. As a single case, it cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy, and broader conclusions regarding efficacy cannot be drawn. It illustrates a potentially useful approach in similarly complex scenarios where coordinated multidisciplinary care is essential.
journal: The American journal of case reports
title: Aspiration Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Life-Threatening Anemia and Active Uterine Bleeding: A Case Report.
