abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is associated with adverse clinical outcomes, yet the underlying right atrial (RA) molecular remodeling remains poorly understood. We aimed to define TR-associated RA remodeling using metabolomic and lipidomic profiling of human RA tissue.
METHODS: RA appendage tissue was obtained intraoperatively from 24 adults undergoing cardiac surgery (11 with ≥severe TR; 13 controls). Gas chromatography mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used for targeted small-molecule metabolomics, and liquid chromatography quadrupole time of flight mass spectrometry (LC-qTOF-MS) for untargeted lipidomics. Mann Whitney U testing, principal component analysis (PCA), partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), and variable importance in projection (VIP) scoring were used to identify discriminatory multi-omics patterns between groups.
RESULTS: Patients with TR demonstrated a distinct metabolic phenotype characterized by reduced glycolysis-related intermediates (glucose-6-phosphate, β-alanine, α-glucosamine-1-phosphate; all p < 0.05) and metabolites consistent with oxidative stress and amino acid catabolism markers (6-hydroxycaproic acid, porphine, phosphoric acid; all p < 0.05). Lipidomic analysis revealed broad phospholipid remodeling and signals consistent with mitochondrial-associated alterations, including a decreased phosphatidylcholine/phosphatidylethanolamine (PC/PE) ratio and reductions in selected diacylglycerol and ceramide species. PCA and PLS-DA demonstrated clear group separation with consistent VIP signals, indicating consistent multi-omics discrimination.
CONCLUSIONS: TR is associated with coordinated metabolic and lipidomic reprogramming in the RA, a pattern compatible with, though not direct evidence of, mitochondrial stress, impaired bioenergetics, and membrane destabilization. These findings support a model in which RA remodeling is tightly linked to TR pathophysiology, highlighting candidate molecular features for future validation. Multi-omics biomarkers may enhance risk stratification, inform the timing of intervention, and guide the development of future point-of-care molecular diagnostics.
title: Multi-omics analysis of human right atrial tissue ıdentifies molecular signatures of remodeling in tricuspid regurgitation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-obstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD) represents an increasing proportion of patients presenting with angina, yet these patients face significant cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to explore distinct classes in NOCAD patients based on demographic characteristics, clinical comorbidities, and inflammatory biomarkers, and to investigate their associations with prognosis.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients diagnosed with NOCAD by coronary angiography for angina between January 1, 2023, and December 1, 2024, with follow-up until August 1, 2025. Latent Class Analysis (LCA) was employed to identify distinct classes based on demographic features, inflammatory markers, including 8 composite inflammatory indices. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations between different classes and individual inflammatory markers with clinical outcomes after multivariate adjustment. Prognostic discrimination compared with traditional risk factors was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.
RESULTS: Among 342 NOCAD patients, LCA identified three distinct classes: low-inflammation with few comorbidities (n = 156, 45.6%), elderly with multiple comorbidities (n = 126, 36.8%), and high-inflammation subgroup (n = 60, 17.5%). Over a median follow-up of 363 days (interquartile range, 193-613 days), 89 patients (26.0%) experienced MACEs. In fully adjusted models, the high-inflammation class was the strongest predictor of MACEs (HR 3.090, 95% CI: 1.614-5.919), followed by the elderly with multiple comorbidities class (HR 2.181, 95% CI: 1.224-3.886). Among 8 composite inflammatory indices evaluated, three demonstrated significant associations with MACEs: the C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index (per unit increase in Z-score, HR 0.402, 95% CI: 0.230-0.703), neutrophil-to-albumin ratio (NAR) index (per unit increase in Z-score, HR 1.234, 95% CI: 1.002-1.522), and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI) index (Z-score > 0, HR 1.635, 95% CI: 1.007-2.655). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated significant differences in MACE-free survival across the three classes (log-rank p = 0.001), with CALLY, NAR, and AISI also showing significant prognostic discrimination. Component analysis revealed the high-inflammation phenotype was independently associated with a 2.44-fold increased risk of hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure (HR = 2.44, 95% CI 1.230-4.846), accounting for 60.67% of total MACEs. These findings were consistently reproduced in a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients without a history of myocardial infarction.
CONCLUSION: Inflammatory and clinical phenotyping identifies distinct risk subgroups in NOCAD. While the high-inflammation phenotype is associated with the highest overall MACEs risk, this prognostic signal is predominantly driven by hospitalizations for unstable angina or heart failure. These findings suggest that inflammation-based phenotyping could serve as an exploratory complementary tool for risk stratification, requiring further external validation before any routine clinical application.
title: Inflammation-based phenotyping and prognostic implications in patients with non-obstructive coronary artery disease.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: After mitral valve replacement with preservation of the subvalvular apparatus, prosthetic dysfunction resulting from retained native structures is extremely rare. When it occurs, it may directly threaten the patient's life. We report an unusual case of severe regurgitation resulting from preserved chordal rupture. The key distinction of this case is the presentation of late, severe continuous prosthetic regurgitation and reversibility.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man had undergone double mechanical valve replacement for severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with mild regurgitation and concomitant aortic regurgitation three years earlier. During surgery, the posterior mitral leaflet and its entire subvalvular apparatus were preserved. Current transesophageal echocardiography revealed a mobile, cord-like structure between the lateral occluder and the prosthetic sewing ring, interfering with leaflet excursion and preventing full closure. This was accompanied by severe prosthetic mitral continuous regurgitation. Surgical findings revealed a ruptured chordae tendineae at the papillary muscle attachment, with the remnant preventing leaflet coaptation. Surgical excision of the ruptured chordal remnant successfully restored normal leaflet function, with complete resolution of the regurgitation confirmed on intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography.
CONCLUSIONS: When obstruction or regurgitation develops after valve replacement with subvalvular preservation, uncommon causes-such as residual subvalvular tissue or ruptured chordal entrapment-should be considered after excluding more common etiologies. This case illustrates the critical role of transesophageal echocardiography in the diagnosis of chordal entrapment after mitral valve replacement and potentially in preventing complications. The potential benefit of preserving the subvalvular apparatus warrants thoughtful deliberation. Surgical removal of the offending tissue or valve replacement remains the definitive treatment.
keywords: Mitral valve replacement with preserved subvalvular apparatus
title: Severe continuous prosthetic mitral regurgitation from chordal rupture after valve-sparing replacement: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to elucidate research trends, collaborative networks, and the thematic evolution of predictors for coronary slow flow (CSF).
METHODS: Relevant literature published between 1977 and 2026 was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection database. Bibliometric analysis was conducted utilizing VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R 4.3.3.
RESULTS: A total of 366 articles were included, indicating an upward trend in research output. China (118 articles), Turkey (65), and the USA (35) emerged as the leading countries. Prominent institutions included China Medical University (29 articles), Capital Medical University (20), and Tabriz University of Medical Sciences (14). Influential journals were Circulation (impact factor 41.3, JCR Q1), Circulation Journal (5.8, Q1), and American Journal of Physiology-Heart and Circulatory Physiology (3.9, Q1). The most prolific author was Wang Yong, with 12 publications and an H-index of 10. Keyword clustering identified three research themes: pathogenesis of CSF, prediction for CSF following percutaneous coronary intervention, and its prognostic implications. Emerging keywords highlighted increasing attention to "endothelial function", "prevalence", "CSF phenomenon", "myocardial infarction" and "reserve".
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a bibliometric overview of key trends and future directions in the field of CSF predictors, emphasizing the growing focus on this area. Future research is anticipated to concentrate on risk stratification and mechanism-targeted intervention strategies.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.
title: Uncovering research themes in coronary slow flow predictors: a bibliometric and cluster analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: This review aims to provide a concise summary of hemodynamic considerations and the pharmacology and current evidence of vasoactive support, including inotropes and vasopressors, during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support.
MAIN TEXT: Patients requiring ECMO for cardiogenic shock or cardiac arrest have a high mortality rate. Despite advancements in medical and mechanical therapies, optimal use of vasoactive in patients receiving venoarterial ECMO is not well defined. Venoarterial ECMO introduces unique hemodynamic disturbances and considerations for the provision of vasoactive medications. Many different pharmacotherapies with varying inotropic, vasoconstrictive, and vasodilating effects are available and include catecholamine and non-catecholamine agents. Mechanisms and level of evidence vary based on agent, yet distinct characteristics may make certain agents more attractive than others depending on the clinical situation faced during ECMO.
CONCLUSIONS: A nuanced understanding of receptor pharmacology and ECMO specific considerations is essential to tailor the vasoactive strategy in this unique population.
journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
title: Pharmacology of vasopressors and inotropes during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare serum levels of Transforming Growth Factor-Beta (TGF-β) and Platelet-Derived Growth Factor-BB (PDGF-BB) among patients with normal coronary arteries (NCA) and those with coronary artery disease (CAD) subclasses [stable CAD and acute coronary syndrome (ACS)], and to evaluate their potential diagnostic value and discriminatory power, particularly in identifying stable CAD.
METHODS: This single-center, cross-sectional study included 176 patients who underwent coronary angiography. Participants were classified into normal coronary artery (NCA; symptomatic control), stable CAD, and ACS groups. Demographic, clinical, and biochemical data were recorded. Blood samples were collected for the analysis of TGF-β1 and PDGF-BB levels using ELISA kits.
RESULTS: Hypertension and diabetes mellitus were significantly more prevalent in the stable CAD group compared to others (p < 0.001). Both TGF-β and PDGF-BB levels were significantly elevated in patients with stable CAD compared to individuals with normal coronary arteries and those with ACS (p < 0.001). Multivariate regression analysis identified hypertension, diabetes, TGF-β, and PDGF-BB as independent predictors of stable CAD (p < 0.01 for all). ROC curve analysis demonstrated good diagnostic performance for TGF-β and PDGF-BB individually (AUC = 0.847, 0.798, respectively), with combined assessment further improving accuracy (AUC = 0.924).
CONCLUSION: Serum TGF-β and PDGF-BB levels are significantly increased in stable CAD patients relative to those with ACS and normal coronary anatomy. The combined evaluation of these biomarkers provides high diagnostic accuracy in distinguishing stable CAD, underscoring their potential role in the non-invasive assessment of chronic atherosclerotic disease. These findings support the use of TGF-β and PDGF-BB as complementary biomarkers for early identification and risk stratification in stable CAD.
title: Comparative evaluation of serum TGF-β1 and PDGF-BB levels across patients with normal coronary arteries, stable coronary artery disease, and acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the standard for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF), but bleeding, non-persistence and thromboembolism despite treatment create important unmet needs. Catheter ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) address distinct mechanisms and do not reproduce systemic anticoagulation.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review covers randomized anticoagulation-withdrawal studies after ablation, trials and pooled evidence on LAAO, patients unable to sustain anticoagulation, procedural imaging and healing, post-implant antithrombotic therapy, and future trial design. Targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov were supplemented by citation screening and review of contemporary congress reports, for evidence spanning 2005-10 October 2026.
EXPERT OPINION: The completed randomized LAAO programme mainly tests substitution where OAC remains feasible. Precision source control should be investigated as rescue when OAC cannot be sustained and as a potential dose-sparing complement in selected patients, while addressing residual ischemic risk and verifying durable closure.
title: Left atrial appendage occlusion for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation: recent evidence, catheter ablation, and future trials.

abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has revolutionized the management of aortic stenosis (AS), particularly for high-risk and inoperable populations. Nevertheless, patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who require TAVR present a unique clinical challenge. These patients tend to have a high burden of comorbidities, as well as chronic uremia, that purportedly predispose them to a higher risk of more frequent and rapid structural valve deterioration (SVD). This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the mechanisms, incidence, and clinical outcomes of TAVR SVD in the ESRD population. In doing so, we summarize the pathophysiology for SVD in this patient population, contextualize the reported rates of TAVR SVD, and summarize the limited literature describing the clinical outcomes for these patients. We posit that clinical management for ESRD patients must focus on proactive, multidisciplinary surveillance and the integration of predictive modeling to optimize the timing of rescue interventions. Finally, we underscore the importance of better understanding the underlying mechanisms that accelerate TAVR SVD in uremic conditions.
title: Structural Valve Deterioration in End-Stage Renal Disease Patients With Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract: Importance It remains unclear if intraoperative hemodynamic therapy should be guided by cardiac index. Objective To evaluate whether individualized cardiac index–guided hemodynamic therapy vs routine hemodynamic therapy improves outcomes in high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery. Design, Setting, and Participants This multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial enrolled high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. The date of last follow-up was January 15, 2026. Interventions Patients were randomized to individualized cardiac index–guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient’s preoperative resting cardiac index vs routine hemodynamic therapy (with blinded cardiac index monitoring). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. Results Of the 1128 patients enrolled, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis (median age, 67 years [IQR, 59-74 years]; 49.4% were female). The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized cardiac index–guided hemodynamic therapy group vs 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine hemodynamic therapy group (relative risk, 0.94 [95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08]; P = .38). There were no between-group differences for the incidence of the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. Conclusions and Relevance Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index–guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient’s preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05648279
title: Individualized Cardiac Index–Guided Hemodynamic Therapy in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Elective Major Abdominal Surgery

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Frailty is highly prevalent among elderly patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes and impaired health‐related quality of life. However, different frailty assessment tools vary in their conceptual frameworks, assessment domains, and predictive performance, and their applicability in elderly PCI populations remains unclear. Aims To compare four commonly used frailty assessment tools, including the Frailty Phenotype (FP), FRAIL scale, Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI), and Frailty Index (FI), and to investigate their associations with quality of life in elderly patients with CHD undergoing PCI. Methods This cross‐sectional study included 244 elderly patients with CHD undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital in Shanghai from August to December 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Frailty Phenotype (FP), FRAIL scale, Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI), and Frailty Index (FI), and quality of life using the 12‐Item Short Form Health Survey (SF‐12). Agreement was evaluated using the Kappa statistic. Associations with physical component summary (PCS) and mental component summary (MCS) scores were assessed using correlation and multivariable linear regression, while discriminatory performance was examined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and Bayesian discriminant analyses. Results Mean PCS and MCS scores were 40.08 ± 11.23 and 52.30 ± 7.82, respectively. Frailty prevalence was 40.6% by FP, 8.6% by FRAIL, 28.3% by TFI, and 22.1% by FI. Agreement was fair to moderate (Kappa = 0.242–0.496). Higher frailty scores were independently associated with lower PCS and MCS after adjustment for age, sex, education, smoking, and comorbidity burden. FP and FI showed comparable discrimination for PCS, whereas TFI had the highest AUC for MCS. Classification accuracy was highest for FP in PCS and TFI in MCS (both 79.51%). Conclusion Frailty was consistently associated with poorer quality of life. FP and FI performed similarly for physical health, whereas TFI showed the most favorable performance for mental health.
title: Application of Four Frailty Assessment Tools in Elderly Patients With Coronary Heart Disease PCI and Its Relationship With Quality of Life

abstract: ABSTRACT Failure of true‐lumen re‐entry after subintimal wire passage is a well‐recognized limitation of endovascular treatment for external iliac artery (EIA) chronic total occlusions (CTO). We report a 73‐year‐old woman with severe limb ischemia and a prior failed endovascular attempt who underwent hybrid left common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy with patch angioplasty, followed by trans‐patch retrograde access and dedicated device‐assisted re‐entry (Outback Elite) after antegrade and retrograde wires repeatedly tracked subintimally without reaching the true lumen. Controlled re‐entry preserved hypogastric artery flow and allowed drug‐eluting stent reconstruction of the EIA. At 12‐month follow‐up, ABI improved from 0.36 to 0.50, and TBI improved to 0.37. Duplex ultrasound at 6‐month follow‐up confirmed patency of the reconstructed segment without evidence of hemodynamically significant restenosis. This technical report illustrates the use of an endarterectomized CFA as a retrograde re‐entry platform and reviews contemporary strategies for managing subintimal crossing failure in iliac CTOs.
title: Trans‐Patch Retrograde Re‐Entry During Hybrid Revascularization of an External Iliac Artery Chronic Total Occlusion: A Technical Note and Review of Re‐Entry Strategies

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Real‐world data after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using drug‐coated balloons (DCBs) in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are limited. Aims We compared 1‐year clinical outcomes after PCI with paclitaxel DCBs between the ACS and non‐ACS patients. Methods The ALLIANCE is a prospective, multicenter registry of PCI using paclitaxel DCBs. Primary endpoint was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all‐cause mortality at 1 year. Adverse events were adjudicated by an independent committee. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences between the ACS and non‐ACS patients. Results From July 2023 to February 2024, 1794 patients with de novo lesions (ACS 513 [28.6%] and non‐ACS 1281 [71.4%]) were enrolled at 57 medical institutions in Japan. Mean age was 71 years, and 76% were male. Among ACS patients, 34.7% had ST‐segment elevation MI, 33.9% non–ST‐segment elevation MI, and 31.4% unstable angina. Intracoronary imaging was used in 88.5% of lesions. Bailout stenting after DCB angioplasty was required in only 1.1% of 1984 lesions. Technical success, defined as post‐procedural residual stenosis < 40% and absence of flow‐limiting coronary dissection, was significantly lower in patients with ACS than those with non‐ACS. At 1 year, TLF occurred in 7.0% of ACS and 3.8% of non‐ACS patients (adjusted HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.06–3.17, p = 0.03). All‐cause mortality was 6.4% and 3.3%, respectively (adjusted HR 2.06; 95% CI 1.13–3.75, p = 0.02). Conclusions One‐year TLF and all‐cause mortality were significantly higher in ACS than non‐ACS patients treated with paclitaxel DCBs in real‐world clinical settings. Registration: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials ( https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp ); unique identifier: jRCT1032230218.
title: One‐Year Clinical Outcomes of Paclitaxel‐Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Patients With and Without Acute Coronary Syndrome: The ALLIANCE Registry

abstract: ABSTRACT Systemic atrioventricular valve (SAVV) regurgitation contributes importantly to systemic right ventricular deterioration in adults with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA) and dextro‐transposition of the great arteries ( d ‐TGA) after atrial‐switch repair. Transcatheter edge‐to‐edge repair (TEER) has emerged as an option for selected patients at high or prohibitive surgical risk, and prior congenital series have established the feasibility of transseptal, transbaffle, and alternative access strategies. However, procedural execution remains highly anatomy‐dependent because systemic venous pathways, atrial baffles, ventricular topology, cardiac orientation, and access‐to‐valve geometry can substantially alter guide‐catheter support and device coaxiality. We report a single‐center Interventional Rounds experience of four consecutive high‐risk adults undergoing SAVV‐TEER across four distinct transposition anatomies: ccTGA with dextrocardia, d ‐TGA after Mustard atrial‐switch repair, Mustard anatomy with severe iliofemoral tortuosity, and ccTGA with interrupted inferior vena cava and azygos continuation. Transfemoral access was used in two patients, and right internal jugular access in two. Three procedures were performed with PASCAL ACE and one with MitraClip. Device implantation was successful in all four patients, with SAVV regurgitation reduced from severe (3+) to mild (1+). Final mean SAVV gradients were 1.5, 2.1, 1.9, and 1.8 mmHg, respectively, and no major acute procedural complications occurred. The principal technical message is that access selection should be guided not only by anatomic patency but by the anticipated mechanical trajectory of the delivery system. Right internal jugular access may be selected prospectively as the preferred primary route when inferior venous anatomy is absent or expected to provide unfavorable curvature, support, or device alignment. Dextrocardia and atrial‐switch baffle anatomy may additionally require specific steering and traversal adaptations. These observations represent focused procedural refinements within the evolving congenital TEER experience rather than evidence of comparative efficacy or safety.

abstract: Abstract Aims Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany). Methods and Results The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65–66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p&lt;0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p&lt;0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p&lt;0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant. Conclusion This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.
title: Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact – The MISSION reBEAT trial

abstract: Abstract Acute heart failure (AHF) represents a major cause of emergency medical care worldwide and continues to carry a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality despite advances in chronic heart failure management. Most patients with AHF present to emergency departments (EDs), where the first hours of care are critical to determine prognosis. Of these, some have been previously evaluated and treated by prehospital emergency medical services before ED arrival. This consensus document summarizes the current evidence and provides practical advice to emergency physicians for the diagnosis, treatment, and disposition of patients with AHF in these emergency settings (emergency medical services and ED). It emphasizes the importance of a rapid phenotypic classification into acute decompensated heart failure, acute pulmonary oedema, isolated right ventricular failure, or cardiogenic shock, as a key tool to guide early management and triage decisions. It reviews evidence on prehospital and ED management, including the use of biomarkers, imaging, ventilatory support, diuretic and vasodilator strategies, and early initiation or continuation of guideline-directed medical therapy. It also discusses risk stratification and disposition decisions supported by validated tools. Finally, it identifies major knowledge gaps and future research priorities, including pragmatic trials to assess prehospital interventions, biomarker-guided therapy, and early initiation of disease-modifying treatments. Ultimately, this consensus document is aimed to contribute to the improvement of outcomes in AHF.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus with practical advice rather than new comparative evidence; cardiogenic shock is one of four phenotypes covered.
appraisal.one_line: Consensus document on diagnosis, treatment and disposition of acute heart failure in prehospital and emergency department settings, including cardiogenic shock phenotyping.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets out early phenotypic triage and research priorities that bear on shock recognition and escalation in the emergency pathway.

title: Acute heart failure in emergency settings

abstract: Background: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a growing public health concern in Yemen, yet detailed data from local healthcare facilities remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, risk factors, and outcomes of CVDs in a military cardiac center.. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Military Cardiac Center in Sanaa, including all patients admitted to the Coronary Care Unit (CCU) in 2019. Clinical data were extracted from both electronic and archived paper records, including prior medical histories dating back to 2008 or 2010 when available. Variables included demographics, clinical presentations, diagnoses, prior cardiac history, and outcomes. Statistical analyses were performed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, ANOVA, and univariate logistic regression to identify predictors of in-hospital and 5-year mortality. Results: A total of 446 patients were included (mean age: 53.0 (+/- 13.6) years), 84% male. The most common diagnoses were acute coronary syndrome (ACS, 60.9%), acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF, 13%), valvular heart disease (VHD, 9%), and cardiogenic shock (5%). Risk factors included khat use (76%), smoking (61%), hypertension (41%), diabetes (31%), and dyslipidemia (4.9%). Younger patients had higher rates of smoking, khat use, and prior myocardial infarction or PCI, while older patients had more diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. Significant predictors of in-hospital mortality included diabetes (OR=2.6), rheumatic heart disease (RHD, OR=2.4), cardiogenic shock (OR=11.3), heart failure (OR=9.2), sepsis (OR=31.1), and cardiac arrest (OR=74.0). For 5-year mortality, key predictors were unstable angina (OR=8.7), ACS (OR=4.0), elective PCI (OR=2.9), and khat use (OR=2.0). Conclusion: CVDs in Yemen affect relatively young patients and are driven by modifiable, region-specific risk factors. Limited access to emergency interventions and late hospital presentation contribute to poor outcomes. Public awareness, preventive measures, and improved cardiac care infrastructure are urgently needed. Keywords: cardiovascular diseases; Acute coronary syndrome; STEMI; NSTEMI; Risk factors; Mortality predictors; Non-communicable disease; Communicable disease; Yemen; Coronary Care Unit
title: Clinical Presentation, Risk Factors, and Outcomes of Cardiovascular Disease in a Military Cardiac Center in Yemen

abstract: BACKGROUND: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. METHODS: In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. RESULTS: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85–1.44]; P =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96–1.30]; P =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93–1.13]; P =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03–1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27–2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique Identifier: NCT05686070.

title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial

abstract: Background: The association between smoking and clopidogrel response has been stated in numerous studies, so the nature of this relationship remains undefined and may be confounded by methodological, hematological, and clinical factors. This study was designed to examine the relationship between smoking status and clopidogrel response between patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) who undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods In this observational analytical study, smoking status was assessed as the primary exposure variable, and responsiveness of clopidogrel was defined according to a predefined area-under-the-curve (AUC) threshold found using the Multiplate platelet function test. Patients were first classified according to smoking status (smokers vs non-smokers). Inside these groups, patients were further categorized as clopidogrel responder’s or non-responders. Baseline laboratory and clinical and features were compared between smokers and non-smokers, and a multivariable logistic regression model was tested to measure whether smoking status was independently related with responsiveness of clopidogrel after modification for main cardiovascular risk factors and hemoglobin level. Results Smokers confirmed a higher percentage of clopidogrel responders compared with non-smokers. Related to multivariable analysis, smoking status remained independently related with an increased likelihood of clopidogrel responsiveness, and level of hemoglobin similarly exhibited a significant positive relation with treatment responsiveness, whereas hypertension, age, BMI, and diabetes were not significant predicters. Conclusions Between patients undergoing PCI; smoking status was independently related with clopidogrel responsiveness; though, this result represents an observational association rather than sign of clinical benefit. The findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and justified further mechanistic and longitudinal study to explain the underlying elucidations for this design.
title: The impact of smoking status on clopidogrel responsiveness in patients with coronary artery disease who undergo percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Background: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a severe manifestation of acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Although several studies have investigated factors associated with OHCA, the findings have been inconsistent. This study evaluates the clinical and angiographic factors associated with OHCA in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: This retrospective study included consecutive STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI at Rambam Health Care Campus between 2010 and 2024. Patients were categorized by the presence of pre-hospital OHCA. Clinical and angiographic characteristics were compared, and logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of OHCA. Results: Among 2,176 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, 135 (6.2%) experienced pre-hospital OHCA. OHCA patients were younger and had higher serum creatinine levels. The distribution of the IRA differed significantly (p=0.005): LMCA and LAD were more frequently the infarct-related arteries, whereas RCA involvement was less common. Independent predictors of OHCA were LMCA (OR 6.03), LAD (OR 1.81), and higher creatinine (OR 1.44). Age and smoking were inversely associated with OHCA (OR 0.97 per additional year, and OR 0.62, respectively). Lesion location, initial TIMI flow, and extent of coronary artery disease were not associated with OHCA. Conclusions: Patients with OHCA in the setting of STEMI are younger, have higher creatinine levels, and more often have culprit lesions in the LMCA or LAD. These findings suggest that specific anatomic and metabolic factors, rather than overall coronary disease burden, are associated with pre-hospital cardiac arrest.
title: Clinical and Anatomical Correlates of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in Patients With ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction

abstract: Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) remains an established imaging modality for guiding percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), providing real-time visualization during transseptal puncture, device deployment and procedural assessment. However, esophageal instrumentation and prolonged probe manipulation may result in gastrointestinal injury, particularly in patients with pre-existing esophageal abnormalities or increased bleeding risk. This narrative review summarizes the available evidence regarding the mechanisms, risk factors, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, management and prevention of TEE-associated esophageal injury during LAAO while examining alternative imaging strategies. A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by targeted searches of broader structural heart intervention literature. Although clinically recognized TEE-associated gastrointestinal complications are uncommon, studies employing systematic endoscopic surveillance have identified substantially higher rates of subclinical mucosal injury. Reported manifestations range from transient dysphagia and superficial mucosal lesions to gastrointestinal bleeding, intramural esophageal hematoma, perforation and fistula formation. Nevertheless, limited LAAO-specific evidence, heterogeneous outcome definitions and differences in surveillance strategies preclude reliable estimation of procedure-specific esophageal injury incidence. Intracardiac echocardiography eliminates esophageal instrumentation but carries a distinct procedural risk profile, whereas cardiac computed tomography (CCT) provides complementary opportunities for preprocedural planning and postprocedural surveillance. Careful preprocedural assessment, judicious probe manipulation, early recognition of complications and individualized imaging selection are important considerations. Prospective studies incorporating standardized esophageal injury endpoints are needed to establish the true clinical burden and guide preventive strategies.
title: Esophageal Injury During Transesophageal Echocardiography-Guided Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: A Narrative Review

abstract: Background: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) causes increased sleep systemic systolic blood pressure (SBP) and cardiovascular (CV) risk. Methods: This secondary analysis encompassed data of 2,065 Spanish polysomnography-confirmed OSA hypertensives (61±11.9 years, 79.5% male) and 32,471 Spanish non-OSA hypertensives (60.2±14.0 years, 51% male) from the Hygia Project. Annually throughout the 5.1-year median follow-up, they underwent comprehensive clinical evaluation and 48-h ambulatory blood pressure (BP) monitoring, with bed and wake-up times diary-recorded to calculate individualized awake and sleep BP means and sleep-time relative declines. Results: OSA subjects experienced higher CV event rates (p<0.001), including a 1.79-fold higher rate of the primary composite study outcome: myocardial infarction, surgical coronary revascularization, heart failure, stroke, and CV death. Cox survival analyses revealed the baseline asleep SBP mean most strongly predicted the primary composite study outcome [HRadjusted =1.37 (1.23, 1.52); p<0.001], while baseline enhanced sleep-time relative SBP decline most strongly predicted protection against it (HRadjusted=0.75 (0.67, 0.83); p<0.001]. Furthermore, when the Cox statistical model included adjustment for the sleep SBP mean, office BP was not predictive of risk. Conclusion: The sleep SBP mean and decline were the BP parameters most predictive of CV events in OSA subjects, constituting major targets of clinical management.
title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea Is Associated with Adverse Cardiovascular Events Related to Sleep Blood Pressure

abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular revascularization is an established treatment for symptomatic femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease. Drug-coated balloon angioplasty allows antiproliferative drug delivery without permanent metallic implantation, while atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation in calcified and occlusive disease. This study evaluated the procedural safety and one-year clinical and hemodynamic outcomes of filter-free retrograde popliteal JETSTREAM atherectomy followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty, with additional assessment of dual antiplatelet therapy adherence and continued smoking. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study included 107 patients with Rutherford category 4–5 femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease who underwent JETSTREAM atherectomy exclusively through retrograde popliteal access followed by Ranger paclitaxel-coated balloon angioplasty. No distal embolic protection device was used. Aspirin 100 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg daily were prescribed for 12 months. The primary procedural safety endpoint was clinically evident distal embolization within 24 hours. Longitudinal outcomes included tibialis posterior artery and dorsalis pedis artery Doppler waveform scores, Rutherford category, and ankle-brachial index. Outcomes were compared according to dual antiplatelet therapy adherence and smoking status. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression was performed for factors associated with treatment non-adherence. RESULTS: Mean age was 67.0±6.9 years, and 69.2% of patients were male. Total occlusions were present in 45.8%, PACSS grade 4 calcification in 83.2%, and adjunctive stenting was required in 21.5%. No clinically evident distal embolization occurred within 24 hours (0/107; upper two-sided 95% exact confidence limit, approximately 3.4%). At one year, mean tibialis posterior artery and dorsalis pedis artery waveform scores improved from 1.05±0.42 to 2.42±0.71 and from 1.07±0.60 to 2.28±0.74, respectively; mean Rutherford category decreased from 4.16±0.37 to 1.64±1.17, and median ankle-brachial index increased from 0.59 to 1.20 (all P< .001). Seventy-seven patients (72.0%) were adherent to dual antiplatelet therapy. At one year, adherent patients had better tibialis posterior artery (2.69 vs 1.73), dorsalis pedis artery (2.56 vs 1.57), Rutherford category (1.13 vs 2.93), and ankle-brachial index (1.218 vs 0.873; all P< .001). Forty-six patients continued smoking. Compared with patients not smoking during follow-up, continued smokers had poorer one-year tibialis posterior artery (2.24 vs 2.56; P=.036), dorsalis pedis artery (2.04 vs 2.46; P=.004), Rutherford category (2.02 vs 1.34; P=.002), and ankle-brachial index (1.044 vs 1.179; P=.004). Continued smoking was independently associated with dual antiplatelet therapy non-adherence (adjusted odds ratio, 3.43; 95% confidence interval, 1.27–9.29; P=.015). CONCLUSIONS: Filter-free retrograde popliteal JETSTREAM atherectomy followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty was associated with substantial one-year clinical and hemodynamic improvement and no clinically evident distal embolization in this cohort. Dual antiplatelet therapy adherence was associated with better one-year outcomes, whereas continued smoking was associated with poorer outcomes and greater non-adherence.
title: Filter-Free Retrograde Popliteal JETSTREAM Atherectomy Followed by Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty: Procedural Safety and One-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes

abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), often called “broken heart syndrome,” is an acute and usually reversible form of left ventricular dysfunction that mimics acute coronary syndrome but is not explained by an obstructive coronary lesion [1,2]. It is preceded by an emotional or physical trigger in many, but not all, patients and predominantly affects postmenopausal women [2]. This narrative review synthesizes current understanding of the epidemiology, proposed cellular and systemic mechanisms, brain–heart interactions, diagnosis, clinical course, and management of TTS. Particular emphasis is placed on the catecholamine surge and sympathetic activation thought to link stress to myocardial dysfunction, and on the contributions of receptor-level signaling, microvascular dysfunction, inflammation, and altered limbic and autonomic brain networks. Seven tables and four figures summarize registry data, proposed mechanisms, neuroimaging findings, diagnostic tools, management, and practical nursing considerations. Many mechanistic details remain hypotheses rather than established facts, no treatment has been proven to improve outcomes in randomized trials, and the evidence for psychological interventions is limited. The review is non-systematic and is intended as an accessible synthesis for students and early-career clinicians.
title: The Neuro-Cardiac Axis: Cellular and Systemic Consequences of Acute Stress in Takotsubo Syndrome

abstract: Background: Severe COVID-19 is driven by a complex interplay between systemic hyperinﬂammation, cellular immune dysregulation, and activation of coagulation cascades. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 52-year-old man with a history of rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis managed with chronic etanercept therapy, who was hospitalized with rapidly progressive COVID-19. Longitudinal monitoring of C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), D-dimer, and ﬁbrinogen demonstrated a transient suppression of select acute-phase reactants followed by profound cellular immune dysregulation and escalating thrombo-inﬂammatory activity. Despite multimodal management—including remdesivir, convalescent plasma, invasive mechanical ventilation, and veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)—the patient suﬀered fatal cardiac arrest. Conclusions: This case highlights the clinical utility of longitudinal, multiparametric biomarker proﬁling in severe COVID-19 and underscores the critical importance of timely immunomodulatory interventions prior to irreversible immunothrombotic damage.
title: Longitudinal Trajectories of Inflammatory, Immune, and Coagulation Biomarkers in Critical COVID-19 Under Chronic Etanercept Therapy: A Case Report

abstract: Background: Mechanical circulatory support significantly improved survival in end-stage heart failure patients. However, this treatment associated with a wide range of complications, including infections, stroke and bleeding. Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB) is often underreported gynecological disorder in female patients following left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. Case Presentation: A 15-year-old female patient with dilated cardiomyopathy and chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction underwent implantation of “Heart Mate 3” as a “bridge” to transplant. After LVAD implantation she had recurrent nosebleeds and AUB complicated with moderate anemia. She frequently admitted to the hospital and then managed with antifibrinolytic medication (Tranexamic acid: 500 mg was administered once a day for 3 days) and blood transfusions. By heart team it was decided to reduce antithrombotic therapy: antiplatelets were discontinued and her INR level was maintained 1.4-1.8. For 2 years prior to HTx LVAD function kept fine on minimized antithrombotic therapy without thromboembolic complications. It was made a multidisciplinary team decision to avoid combined oral contraceptives due to the high risk of thromboembolic complications outweighing the benefits. Twice she underwent urgent laparoscopic surgeries but after all her fertile function remained preserved. Conclusions: LVAD patients should be managed with a multidisciplinary heart team. In case of recurrent bleeding and low-risk of thromboembolic complications reduction of antithrombotic therapy should be considered. A personalized approach is essential to determine whether conservative or surgical management is superior, as it balances evidence-based medicine with individual patient needs, reducing the risks of futile or overly aggressive care. Taking into account the reproductive function, an organ-preserving operation was performed for the subsequent preservation of fertile function. Surgical interventions for gynecological disorders can be safely performed in patients “bridged” with LVAD.
title: Management of Abnormal Uterine Bleeding in a Patient “Bridged” with LVAD

abstract: Abstract Background Implantation of expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) artificial chordae is an established approach for mitral valve repair, but current transapical systems are typically limited to single-thread implantation per delivery and remain procedurally complex. This study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and mid-term efficacy of the HaloChord® system, which delivers up to two sets (four threads) of ePTFE chordae per sequence, in a porcine model of acute mitral regurgitation (MR). Methods Five adult Large White pigs (60–80 kg) underwent transapical induction of acute moderate to moderately severe MR via surgical blunt disconnection of the primary chordae tendineae attached to the P2 segment. Under beating-heart transesophageal echocardiographic (TEE) guidance, one or two suturing devices per animal were deployed with the HaloChord® system and anchored at the left ventricular apex. Animals followed a staged terminal-endpoint design (n = 1 at 30 days, n = 1 at 90 days, n = 3 at 180 days). Evaluations included serial echocardiography, clinical pathology, gross examination, and histopathological scoring per GB/T 16886.6–2022 Annex E. Results Implantation succeeded in all 5 animals; two received one suturing device (4 equivalent chordae) and three received two suturing devices (8 equivalent chordae). Suturing-device operation time was 10.5 ± 5.10 min per device; fixation-device operation time was 5.2 ± 6.14 min per cycle, with the wide fixation-time variability reflecting iterative echocardiographic length titration. MR grade was reduced from 2 + to 3 + post-modeling to ≤ 1 + immediately post-procedure and remained stable through each terminal endpoint. Vena contracta width decreased substantially and remained stable at follow-up. Gross examination confirmed stable anchoring with no detachment, rupture, or thrombus. Histopathological scoring showed a more pronounced tissue response at 30 days that moderated to predominantly moderate scores at 90 and 180 days, driven primarily by fibrosis and neovascularization rather than active inflammation. Conclusions In this porcine acute MR model, the HaloChord® system demonstrated procedural feasibility on the beating heart, effective acute MR reduction, and acceptable mid-term device stability and biocompatibility. The dual-set delivery design simplifies transapical chordal implantation, providing a foundation for clinical evaluation.
title: Preclinical Animal Study of a Dual-Set Artificial Chordae Mitral Valve Repair System in a Porcine Model

title: WITHDRAWN: Antithrombotic Management Strategies and Outcomes After Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Atrial Fibrillation Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention

abstract: Abstract Background: Repolarization heterogeneity underlies malignant arrhythmia in acute coronary syndrome (ACS). We examined whether the admission Tpeak–Tend (Tp-e) interval and Tp-e/QTc ratio track angiographic complexity, clinical risk and six-month outcome. Methods: We prospectively enrolled 250 consecutive patients with ACS at a single tertiary centre. Hodges-corrected QT, Tp-e and Tp-e/QTc were measured in leads V4–V6 on the admission electrocardiogram, with echocardiography, angiography and SYNTAX/GRACE scoring. The composite outcome comprised ventricular arrhythmia, heart failure, cardiogenic shock and death. Results: Interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC 0.99–1.00). All three indices rose incrementally across SYNTAX and GRACE categories (P Conclusions: In ACS, Tp-e and Tp-e/QTc increase with anatomical and clinical severity, and Tp-e/QTc independently predicts six-month events. By refining GRACE-derived prognostic information, these indices merit consideration in early risk stratification.
title: Ventricular repolarization heterogeneity on the admission electrocardiogram in acute coronary syndrome: relationship of the Tpeak–Tend interval and Tp-e/QTc ratio to angiographic complexity, clinical risk and six-month outcome

abstract: Abstract Backgrounds: Short-term outcome of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) through transcarotid access (TC) and transthoracic access (TT) such as transapical or transaortic has been reported as alternative access options in patients who were not feasible with transfemoral access. However, mid to long-term outcomes have been poorly documented. The purpose of this study was to evaluate postoperative outcomes comparing TC with TT groups. Methods Between January 2016 and January 2024, 93 patients underwent TAVR through TC access while 62 through TT access. To adjust baseline differences, 1:1 propensity score matching was performed using the nearest neighbor method between the TC and TT groups. Results 38 pairs were matched in propensity score matching. A significant higher incidence of postoperative new atrial fibrillation was detected in the TT compared with TC groups (10.5% vs 0%, p = 0.04). 30-day mortality rate, postoperative stroke, permanent pacemaker placement, and surgical reintervention for access site did not differ between the two groups. Length of hospital stay was shorter in the TC group (4.9 ± 5.5days vs 7.7 ± 4.8days, p = 0.02). Mean follow-up term was 2.3 ± 2.1years. Cumulative survival rate in 5 years was 70.1% in the TC group and 54.3% in the TT group. There was no significant difference in mid-term outcome between the 2 groups (p = 0.47). Conclusions Transcatheter aortic valve replacement through transcarotid access was associated with lower rate of new postoperative atrial fibrillation and shorter hospital stay compared with transthoracic access. However, short and mid-term survival rates were comparable in this patient cohort.
title: Outcome of transcarotid versus transthoracic access for transcatheter aortic valve replacement

abstract: Abstract Objective: The long-term prognosis of patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is influenced by multiple factors. This study aimed to identify independent predictors of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at one year, with a specific focus on anatomical complexity assessed by the SYNTAX score and platelet activity indices. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 310 patients who underwent PCI for at least one CTO between January 2019 and June 2021. Patients were followed for one year for the occurrence of MACE (a composite of cardiac death, target vessel revascularization, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and hospitalization for heart failure). Baseline clinical, angiographic (including SYNTAX score), and laboratory data (including mean platelet volume [MPV], platelet count, and MPV/platelet ratio) were collected. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed to identify predictors. Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank test was used for survival comparisons. Predictive performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results: During follow-up, 64 patients (20.6%) experienced MACE. In univariate analysis, high MPV group (HR 2.13, 95% CI 1.27–3.60, p=0.004), lower HDL-cholesterol (HR 0.21, 95% CI 0.06–0.71, p=0.012), lower platelet count, higher serum creatinine, and higher MPV/platelet ratio were significant predictors. A risk score incorporating these factors effectively stratified patients (Log-rank p=0.044). In multivariable models, lower HDL-cholesterol remained an independent protective factor (HR 0.17, 95% CI 0.05–0.58, p=0.005). SYNTAX score was a significant predictor in optimized models (HR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01–1.07, p=0.020). Patients with both high SYNTAX score and high MPV had the worst MACE-free survival (Log-rank p=0.046). The full predictive model (including age, SYNTAX score, MPV, platelet count, HDL-C, creatinine) showed the best discriminative ability (AUC=0.659). Subgroup analysis indicated the predictive value of SYNTAX score and high MPV was most pronounced in patients aged Conclusion: Lower HDL-cholesterol, higher SYNTAX score, and a profile suggestive of higher platelet activity (high MPV group, lower platelet count) are important predictors of one-year MACE in CTO patients after PCI. A model combining clinical, anatomical, and platelet indices offers improved risk stratification, particularly for identifying high-risk younger patients.
title: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Independent Predictors for Long-Term Prognosis in Patients with Chronic Total Occlusion: Focus on SYNTAX Score and Platelet-Related Indices

abstract: Abstract Background Mycoplasma hominis(M. hominis) is a common commensal of the urogenital tract frequently associated with localized infections; however, hematogenous dissemination is uncommon, and cases secondary to indwelling central venous catheters are exceedingly rare. Here, we report a case of M. hominis bloodstream infection following transfemoral cannulation for extracorporeal life support, including an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Case Presentation: A 68-year-old male patient underwent coronary stent implantation for acute myocardial infarction at Haining People's Hospital on July 25, 2025. Postoperatively, he developed heart failure and cardiogenic shock, necessitating IABP support. Although, his cardiac function and hemodynamics improved, and the patient’s IABP was weaned on Day 8. However, the patient subsequently developed recurrent dyspnea, along with increasing body temperature and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. CRRT was therefore initiated to maintain fluid balance and metabolic homeostasis and to remove inflammatory mediators. Despite this, the patient continued to experience fever with persistently elevated inflammatory markers. On Day 13, blood cultures, urine cultures, and catheter tip cultures were obtained. Hemodynamic deterioration occurred on Day 15, prompting veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support. Dynamic monitoring revealed a rising trend in troponin I levels, and repeated coronary angiography demonstrated occlusion of the coronary stent, which was managed with balloon dilatation. The patient was then transferred to the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University for further management. On Day 16, the microbiology laboratory at Haining People's Hospital reported that the blood cultures yielded M. hominis ; this finding was communicated to the receiving hospital. Subsequent anti-infective therapy with omadacycline was administered. After undergoing left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, the patient ultimately improved and was discharged in stable condition. Conclusions In terms of femoral catheter-related infections adjacent to the urogenital tract, uncommon atypical pathogens such as M. hominis warrant consideration in addition to routine bacterial etiologies.
title: Mycoplasma hominis bloodstream infection following transfemoral cannulation for extracorporeal life support: a case report

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains the most lethal complication of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), particularly in elderly patients who lack dedicated prediction tools. This study developed and internally validated a nomogram for admission-time CS risk stratification in elderly (≥ 60 years) STEMI patients, and evaluated the incremental value of combining Killip classification with laboratory parameters. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study consecutively enrolled 527 patients aged ≥ 60 years with STEMI between January 2019 and December 2022; after excluding 4 patients with missing CS status, 523 were analyzed (CS, n = 39; non-CS, n = 484). Admission demographics, Killip classification, comorbidities, vital signs, laboratory tests, echocardiography, and coronary angiography data were collected.
