title: Development and Validation of a Nomogram for Predicting Cardiogenic Shock in Elderly Patients with ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Retrospective Cohort Study

abstract: Abstract Background Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is an inherited arrhythmia syndrome that can cause sudden cardiac arrest. Its recognition after resuscitation may be obscured by troponin elevation and transient ventricular dysfunction, resembling fulminant myocarditis. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) can provide temporary circulatory support during refractory cardiac arrest; however, cervical cannulation carries a risk of vascular thrombosis and bleeding. We report a case of a child with ryanodine receptor 2 ( RYR2 )-associated CPVT, complicated by a compressive cervical haematoma after decannulation. Case presentation A 9-year-old boy with two previous syncopal episodes sustained a startle-triggered out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and developed recurrent polymorphic ventricular tachycardia after admission to the paediatric intensive care unit. Right cervical veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was established after continuous cardiopulmonary resuscitation without sustained return of spontaneous circulation, with an estimated resuscitation-to-flow interval of approximately 60 minutes. Serum troponin I was measured at 5.11 µg/L and left ventricular ejection fraction was 42–44%, prompting treatment for suspected diagnosis of fulminant myocarditis; the ejection fraction subsequently fell to 33%. Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous RYR2 variant, c.11836G > A (p.Gly3946Ser), classified as pathogenic by the reporting laboratory according to ACMG/AMP criteria. The variant is absent from ClinVar, relevant population reference databases, and the published literature, and its identification, together with the patient’s characteristic clinical phenotype, supported the diagnosis of RYR2 -associated CPVT. During anticoagulation for cervical vascular thrombosis after decannulation, an enlarging haematoma with active extravasation and tracheal compression required surgical evacuation, carotid repair, jugular thrombectomy, and venorrhaphy. The child was discharged after 41 days with a signficant improvement ejection fraction of 67%, persistent internal jugular occlusion, and propranolol and aspirin therapy. Conclusions CPVT should be reconsidered after an adrenergic cardiac arrest, even when post-arrest findings suggest myocarditis. ECPR can provide temporary rescue support. A rare RYR2 variant detection may support the clinical diagnosis and intervention.
title: A novel RYR2 variant associated with catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia requiring extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation and complicated by cervical vascular injury: a case report

abstract: Abstract Background Intramural dissecting hematoma (IDH) is a rare but life-threatening subacute cardiac rupture type that occurs after acute myocardial infarction or during its remodeling process. IDH may resolve spontaneously, or it may extend and destroy adjacent structures, leading to serious mechanical complications. Owing to its low incidence and limited literature, there is currently no standardized diagnostic, therapeutic, or management consensus. Case presentation: A 67‑year‑old male with acute extensive anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction underwent emergency coronary angiography and percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty. After the procedure, the patient still had precordial discomfort and was transferred to our hospital. One week later, repeat angiography with intra‑aortic balloon pump (IABP) support revealed suspected left anterior descending branch (LAD) dissection, prompting two-stent implantation. The next day, echocardiography showed an apical septal myocardial dissecting hematoma with complex perforation. Surgical ventricular septal repair was planned electively. On day 25 after infarction, cardiogenic shock and multiple organ failure developed; after IABP and biventricular assist device support, acute cerebral infarction occurred, and the family ultimately withdrew treatment. Conclusion Ventricular septal IDH with perforation after acute myocardial infarction is a rare and catastrophic mechanical complication. Early recognition, appropriate timing of intervention, and adequate use of mechanical circulatory support are key to improving prognosis.
title: Acute Extensive Anterior Myocardial Infarction Complicated by Intramyocardial Dissecting Hematoma of the Interventricular Septum with Perforation: A Case Report

abstract: Abstract Background Cardiac injury is closely linked to defective mitochondrial energy production, yet the factors that preserve mitochondrial function in cardiomyocytes remain incompletely understood. Semaphorin 3B (SEMA3B) participates in metabolic and stress responses, but its contribution to cardiac mitochondrial homeostasis is unclear. We examined whether SEMA3B is linked to AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling and myocardial injury. Methods Lentiviral short-hairpin RNA was used to reduce SEMA3B expression in human AC16 cardiomyocytes and high-fat-diet-fed mice. Selected groups received the AMPK activator AICAR. We assessed AMPK signaling, mitochondrial-dynamics proteins, membrane potential, ATP, reactive oxygen species, cellular metabolic activity, inflammatory mediators, serum lipids, and cardiac histopathology. Results SEMA3B knockdown in AC16 cells reduced phosphorylated AMPK and ACC, together with Mfn1, Mfn2, and Drp1. Mitochondrial membrane potential, ATP content, and MTT reduction declined, whereas oxidant generation increased and mitophagy-related markers changed. AICAR attenuated most of these effects. In mice, SEMA3B knockdown was associated with myocardial necrosis, collagen accumulation, apoptosis, and an adverse serum-lipid profile. AICAR restored AMPK-associated signaling, improved mitochondrial measures, and reduced structural injury. Conclusion SEMA3B appears to support mitochondrial and metabolic homeostasis in cardiomyocytes through an AMPK-associated pathway. Loss of SEMA3B worsened biochemical and structural indices of cardiac injury, whereas AICAR produced substantial rescue. Further work is required to identify the receptors involved and establish AMPK-specific causality.
title: SEMA3B Loss Disrupts AMPK-Associated Mitochondrial Homeostasis and Aggravates Cardiac Injury

abstract: Abstract Objective(s): Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major contributor to cardiac damage after coronary revascularization. Intralipid, a soybean oil-based lipid emulsion, exerts cardioprotective effects via activation of prosurvival signaling pathways and preservation of mitochondrial function, but its optimal timing and its effects on remote pulmonary injury remain unclear. This study evaluated the cardioprotective and pulmonary effects of Intralipid administered at different time points during myocardial I/R injury in rats. Materials and Methods Fifty male Wistar rats (300–350 g) were randomly assigned to five groups (n = 10/group). Myocardial I/R injury was induced by 30 min occlusion of the left anterior descending artery followed by 120 min of reperfusion. Intralipid was administered before or during reperfusion according to different protocols. Heart and lung tissues were evaluated histopathologically, and myocardial necrosis and inflammatory cell infiltration were quantified by histomorphometry. Results The control group showed extensive myocardial necrosis and inflammatory cell infiltration. All Intralipid-treated groups showed significantly less myocardial injury than controls (P
title: Cardioprotective and Pulmonary Effects of Intra-lipid on Myocardial Ischemia- Reperfusion Injury in Rat Heart and Lung Tissue

abstract: Abstract Background The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) have been associated with adverse outcomes in various cardiovascular populations. However, their comparative prognostic value in oldest-old (≥ 80 years) patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), coronary heart disease (CHD), and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains unexplored. We aimed to compare the predictive performance of NLR, PLR, and SII for in-hospital all-cause mortality in this population. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 372 male patients aged ≥ 80 years with documented CHD, T2DM, and ACS. NLR, PLR, and SII were calculated from admission blood tests. The primary outcome was in-hospital all-cause mortality. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the associations, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated to compare discriminative ability. Results The overall in-hospital mortality rate was 80.9% (301/372). None of the three indices was significantly associated with mortality in univariate analysis (NLR: OR = 0.99, 95% CI 0.95–1.03, P = 0.589; PLR: OR = 1.00, 95% CI 1.00–1.00, P = 0.641; SII: OR = 1.00, 95% CI 1.00–1.00, P = 0.994). After multivariable adjustment for age, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, serum creatinine, and HbA1c, all three indices remained non-significant (NLR: OR = 0.98, P = 0.461; PLR: OR = 1.00, P = 0.281; SII: OR = 1.00, P = 0.890). ROC analysis showed AUC values of 0.555, 0.526, and 0.540 for NLR, PLR, and SII, respectively, indicating negligible discriminative ability. Conclusion NLR, PLR, and SII do not provide independent prognostic information for in-hospital mortality in oldest-old male patients with CHD, T2DM, and ACS. Routine use of these indices for risk stratification in this population is not supported by our data.
title: NLR, PLR, and SII Do Not Predict In-Hospital Mortality in Oldest-Old Male Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome and Type 2 Diabetes: A Head-to-Head Comparative Study

abstract: Abstract Background : Despite its growing use as a rescue therapy for refractory cardiac arrest (CA), extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) is plagued by persistently high early in-hospital mortality. While existing prediction tools focus on mid-term survival, few are designed for the critical initial 10-day period—a time window when clinical interventions are most impactful. This study sought to address this gap by developing and externally validating a nomogram for 10-day mortality prediction using routinely available laboratory parameters. Methods : A training cohort of 162 ECPR-treated CA patients (Huai'an Hospital Affiliated to Xuzhou Medical University, 2018–2025) and an external validation cohort of 49 patients (Huai'an First Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing Medical University, same period) were retrospectively analyzed. Cox regression was used to identify independent predictors and build the nomogram, which was then assessed for calibration and discrimination in both cohorts. Results : Among the 211 patients analyzed, five routine laboratory parameters were confirmed as independent predictors: D-dimer, international normalized ratio, serum potassium, serum sodium, and lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR). The nomogram demonstrated good discriminative performance in the external validation set, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.793 (95% CI: 0.660–0.926). Conclusions : We developed and externally validated a concise, routine blood test-based nomogram for early mortality risk stratification in the first 10 days post-ECPR. This readily applicable tool may facilitate timely risk assessment and individualized decision-making in critically ill CA patients receiving ECPR.
title: A Nomogram for Predicting Early Mortality in Cardiac Arrest Patients Undergoing ECPR: A Multicenter Development and External Validation Study

abstract: Abstract Background: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) combined with left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an emerging one-step strategy for atrial fibrillation. Current clinical studies mainly focus on procedural safety and recurrent arrhythmia, while subtle anatomical changes after PFA, especially alterations of the left atrial ridge, are rarely recognized. This cohort represents a preliminary real-world experience of one-stage PFA+LAAO using the VARIPULSE system in Chinese patients, where related anatomical morphological data remain scarce in domestic literature. Methods: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 40 consecutive patients underwent combined PFA and LAAO. LAA ridge thickness and LAA orifice diameter were measured via transesophageal echocardiography before and after ablation.The primary follow-up endpoint at 90 days was the presence of residual shunt of the LAA occluder. Periprocedural adverse events were analyzed descriptively as secondary outcomes. Results: Implant success was achieved in all 40 patients (100%), with no deaths, strokes, major bleeding events, or intervention-requiring pericardial effusions observed. No complications such as hemolysis, air-bubble stroke, phrenic nerve palsy, or coronary artery spasm occurred intraoperatively. All patients underwent pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) with VARIPULSE, followed by LAAO with Watchman FLX (21/40) or LACbes (19/40) guided by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Post-PFA, LAA ridge thickness increased significantly by 1.21±0.50 mm ( P Conclusion: Combined PFA and LAAO was feasible with high implant success, low periprocedural complication rates, and favorable outcomes through 90 days. This integrated approach offers a promising “one-stop” strategy for patients with AF requiring rhythm control and stroke prevention. we observed a mean 30.45% increase in LAA ridge thickness immediately following PFA. This study provides preliminary anatomical evidence for postoperative structural changes after VARIPULSE PFA.
title: Left Atrial Ridge Edema After VARIPULSE pulsed field ablation: Correlation With Early Peri-device leak

abstract: Abstract Background Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) frequently coexist and jointly increase cardiovascular risk. Whether worsening renal impairment is associated with graded increases in coronary plaque burden on intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) in patients with T2DM—and whether metabolic, inflammatory, and nutritional markers attenuate this association—remain unclear. Methods This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included 129 adults with T2DM who underwent coronary IVUS between January 2022 and May 2026. Using KDIGO principles and dialysis status, we defined a three-level renal gradient: T2DM alone (n = 64), non-dialysis CKD (n = 31), and dialysis-dependent CKD (n = 34). We used linear trend tests and stepwise multivariable regression for plaque burden (primary outcome) and minimum lumen area (key secondary outcome), Firth penalized logistic regression for binary outcomes, restricted cubic splines for continuous eGFR, and multiple imputation for missing covariates. Results Plaque burden increased across the renal gradient (unadjusted β 1.63% per category, 95% CI 0.47 to 2.79; P = 0.006) and remained associated after adjustment for conventional cardiometabolic risk factors (β 1.49%, 95% CI 0.05 to 2.93; P = 0.042). Additional adjustment for phosphorus, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, hemoglobin, albumin, calcium, and target vessel location attenuated the association toward the null (β − 0.20%, 95% CI − 2.08 to 1.68; P = 0.833). Minimum lumen area did not differ across groups ( P = 0.708). Each one-category increase in renal impairment was associated with higher odds of high plaque burden (≥ 80%) (adjusted OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.28 to 4.03; P = 0.005). Phosphorus and hs-CRP increased and hemoglobin and albumin decreased across the gradient (all P
title: Association of renal impairment gradient with coronary plaque burden assessed by intravascular ultrasound in patients with type 2 diabetes: a single-center retrospective study

abstract: Abstract Objective The predictive performance of EuroSCORE II may have evolved over the last decade owing to major changes in cardiac surgery practice, including an ageing population, increasing comorbidity burden, and advances in perioperative management. We aimed to evaluate the contemporary performance of EuroSCORE II in a large nationwide French cohort. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of consecutive adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery between 2020 and 2024 in centers participating in the French EPICARD registry (French Society of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery, Federation des Specialites Medicales, France). Patients undergoing heart transplantation, durable mechanical circulatory support implantation, cardiac tumor surgery, or with missing EuroSCORE II data were excluded. The primary endpoint was operative mortality, defined as in-hospital or 30-day mortality, identified through linkage with the French national mortality database (INSEE). Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), while calibration was evaluated using the Hosmer–Lemeshow test and calibration plots. Results A total of 108,412 patients were included. Median EuroSCORE II was 1.7% [IQR 1.0–3.4], and overall operative mortality was 3.3% (n = 3,572). EuroSCORE II demonstrated acceptable discriminative performance (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.82–0.84). Calibration varied across surgical subgroups, with slight overestimation in low-risk patients and isolated CABG, and underestimation in high-risk settings, particularly acute aortic dissection and combined CABG-aortic procedures. Conclusions EuroSCORE II remains a valuable risk stratification tool in contemporary cardiac surgery but shows calibration limitations in specific high-risk populations, supporting the need for periodic recalibration and updated risk models.
title: Predictive Value of EuroSCORE II in Contemporary Cardiac Surgery : Insights from the EPICARD Registry

abstract: Abstract Background. Electrocardiographic prediction in critical illness has relied on single parameters measured once — most often the corrected QT interval — with modest and inconsistent results. Whether quantitative parameters spanning the whole cardiac cycle (depolarization through repolarization), measured from every ECG of an ICU stay, carry independent prognostic and mechanistic information is unknown. Methods. We linked MIMIC-IV v3.1 to the MIMIC-IV-ECG waveform subset and built a cohort of 14,319 adult ICU stays without known coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, or pacing (25,112 analyzable ECGs from a 72,166-ECG linked pool). We assembled a whole-cycle parameter panel per ECG: machine-derived intervals and axes (heart rate, PR, QRS duration, QT/QTc, frontal QRS-T angle) and waveform-measured amplitudes from a validated median-beat engine (ST amplitude, J-to-Tpeak amplitude, QRS voltage, ST-T area, Tp-Te). Analyses: (1) 48-hour landmark Cox models for 28-day mortality; (2) linear mixed models of day-by-day trajectories by survival; (3) new-onset repolarization abnormalities as exposures for ECG-specific outcomes (new atrial tachyarrhythmia, new myocardial injury) with cause-specific and Fine–Gray models; (4) within-patient difference-in-differences ECG responses to ICU interventions, with amiodarone as a positive control. Results. The spatial QRS-T angle was the strongest whole-cycle predictor of 28-day mortality: per-SD HR 1.125 (95% CI 1.068–1.185; P
title: Whole-Cardiac-Cycle ECG Dynamics in Critical Illness: The Spatial QRS- T Angle as a Prognostic Marker, an Early-Warning Signal for Arrhythmia and Myocardial Injury, and an In-Vivo Pharmacodynamic Readout

abstract: Abstract Background Chronic critical illness (CCI) is characterized by persistent organ dysfunction and poor outcomes, yet reliable early biomarkers remain limited. We investigated whether early expression of programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) on peripheral T cells was associated with subsequent CCI and 28-day mortality. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included critically ill adults consecutively admitted to the intensive care unit of the First Affiliated Hospital of Shihezi University between July 2025 and July 2026. Within 24 h of ICU admission, clinical and laboratory variables, echocardiographic parameters, circulating cytokines, and PD-1/CTLA-4 expression on T-cell subsets were assessed. Spearman correlation with false discovery rate (FDR) correction was used to examine associations between immune checkpoint expression and cardiac parameters. Receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated discrimination for subsequent CCI, and Cox proportional hazards models examined associations with 28-day mortality. Results Of 81 patients analyzed, 39 developed CCI, 41 did not, and one died before CCI status could be determined. Patients who developed CCI had higher APACHE II scores, lactate, myocardial injury markers, inflammatory cytokines, and proportions of CD4 + PD-1 + , CD4 + CTLA-4 + , and CD8 + PD-1 + T cells, but lower albumin and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (all P + PD-1 + T-cell proportion showed the strongest individual discrimination for CCI (area under the curve [AUC], 0.934; 95% CI, 0.885–0.983). An exploratory model combining CD4 + PD-1 + , CD4 + CTLA-4 + , and APACHE II score yielded an AUC of 0.977 (95% CI, 0.953-1.000), with 94.87% sensitivity and 87.80% specificity. In the CCI group, CD4 + PD-1 + proportion correlated with left ventricular end-diastolic volume before, but not after, FDR correction (ρ = 0.441, P + PD-1 + T-cell proportion and lower LVEF as independently associated with increased 28-day mortality. Conclusions Early increases in PD-1 and CTLA-4 expression on selected T-cell subsets were associated with subsequent CCI. CD4 + PD-1 + expression, particularly when combined with CD4 + CTLA-4 + and APACHE II score, may aid early risk stratification, while its association with mortality warrants further validation. Trial Registration: The study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the First Affiliated Hospital of Shihezi University (KJ2025-633-01). Clinical trial number: not applicable.
title: Early PD-1 and CTLA-4 Expression on Peripheral Blood T Cells and Subsequent Chronic Critical Illness and 28-Day Mortality: A Prospective Cohort Study

abstract: Abstract Background: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) accounts for approximately 5% of myocardial infarction (MI) cases and predominantly affects young women without traditional cardiovascular risk factors; it is markedly less common in men. Recognized triggers include severe physical exertion, emotional stress, and conditions that acutely raise intrathoracic pressure, such as severe coughing. Case Presentation: A 21-year-old male was hospitalized with a preliminary diagnosis of pneumonia after severe coughing episodes. He had recently started tirzepatide for obesity. During hospitalization he developed chest pain and tachycardia; an electrocardiogram (ECG) captured monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT), and a repeat ECG after rate control showed inferior ST-segment elevation. Echocardiography revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35%. Coronary angiography demonstrated spontaneous dissection of the circumflex artery (CX) without atherosclerotic disease elsewhere. The patient was managed conservatively with dual antiplatelet therapy and enoxaparin, remained free of recurrent symptoms, and was discharged with an improved LVEF of 40%. Conclusion: SCAD should be considered in young men presenting with chest pain or arrhythmia after severe coughing, even without classic cardiovascular risk factors. The co-occurrence of CX-related SCAD, inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and monomorphic VT is rarely reported and raises the possibility of Purkinje-related arrhythmogenesis in this territory, a mechanism warranting further study.
title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection Presenting with Monomorphic Ventricular Tachycardia in a Young Man Hospitalized for Pneumonia and Severe Coughing Episodes: A Case Report

abstract: Abstract Background Older adults receiving long-term antihypertensive therapy represent a rapidly growing surgical population in whom intraoperative blood pressure management remains contentious. Observational evidence consistently links intraoperative hypotension with adverse postoperative outcomes, but whether specific blood pressure targets or hemodynamic management strategies improve clinical outcomes remains uncertain Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov from 1 January 2013 to 15 January 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and prospective or retrospective cohort studies of haemodynamic monitoring-guided management in patients with a mean or median age of at least 65 years receiving chronic antihypertensive therapy or with documented chronic hypertension undergoing non-cardiac surgery. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data using a piloted form capturing design, setting, population, hypertension status, intervention, comparator, and raw outcome events, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2 for RCTs; ROBINS-I for cohort studies). Quantitative pooling was prespecified only for comparisons with three or more studies sharing design, intervention class, and outcome definition; otherwise, a structured narrative synthesis with fully tabulated study-level effect data was performed. Certainty was rated with GRADE. Reporting follows PRISMA 2020. Results Nineteen studies (7 randomized controlled trials reported in 9 publications; 12 cohort studies) comprising 1,074,313 patients were included. In RCTs, higher or individualized intraoperative blood pressure targets did not reduce major vascular or organ-injury composites compared with routine targets (POISE-3: risk ratio [RR] 0.99, 95% CI 0.89–1.11; IMPROVE-multi: RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.93–1.30), although one small trial favoured individualized systolic targets (INPRESS: RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57–0.95); certainty was low because of inconsistency and indirectness. Observational cohorts consistently reported duration-dependent associations between intraoperative hypotension and acute kidney injury or myocardial injury (moderate certainty for the association, not for a causal effect of any specific target). Goal-directed haemodynamic therapy was neutral in the largest contemporary trial (OPTIMISE II: postoperative infection RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.88–1.18) but beneficial in smaller earlier trials (low certainty). Continuing renin–angiotensin-system inhibitors increased intraoperative hypotension (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.19–1.44) without increasing major complications (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.87–1.19; moderate certainty). A hypotension-avoidance strategy did not reduce postoperative delirium in randomized data (cogPOISE-3: RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.79–1.38), and observational findings were inconsistent (low certainty). Conclusions Intraoperative hypotension is consistently and duration-dependently associated with organ injury in observational surgical cohorts, although much of this evidence is derived from broader non-cardiac surgical populations rather than exclusively elderly hypertensive patients. Randomized evidence specific to elderly hypertensive populations remains limited and does not demonstrate consistent benefit from higher blood pressure targets, goal-directed haemodynamic therapy, or specific antihypertensive withholding strategies.Recommendations for this population should rest on guidelines and individualized judgment rather than on claims of moderate-certainty trial evidence that the current literature does not provide. Renal denervation and other device-based therapies are outside the scope of this review and are identified as future research priorities only.
title: Perioperative Hemodynamic Management in Elderly Hypertensive Patients: A Systematic Review of Monitoring-Guided Strategies and Postoperative Outcomes

abstract: Abstract Background Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) induces complex hemostatic disturbances, and the pharmacodynamic response to oral P2Y12 inhibitors during extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) is poorly characterized. We compared platelet reactivity and ticagrelor response between ECPR and conventionally resuscitated cardiac arrest patients. Methods In this single-center analysis of two prospectively collected, non-contemporaneous cohorts, 16 adults undergoing ECPR and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were compared with 20 conventionally resuscitated cardiac arrest patients undergoing PCI without ECMO. All received crushed ticagrelor via gastric tube. Platelet reactivity was measured before and 2–48 h after loading by Multiplate adenosine diphosphate (ADP) aggregometry and the VerifyNow P2Y12 assay (P2Y12 reaction units, PRU) and analyzed with linear mixed-effects models. Results Baseline PRU was lower in ECPR patients (median 220 vs. 246; p = 0.020), independently of platelet count. After loading, PRU declined more slowly with ECPR (group × time interaction p
title: Platelet reactivity and pharmacodynamic response to ticagrelor in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation compared with conventionally resuscitated cardiac arrest patients

abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence models may improve emergency department (ED) screening for acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but such models often rely on International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes as training labels, whose accuracy in contemporary ED populations is uncertain. In this 10-year retrospective study of 619,599 adult ED encounters, we compared ICD-coded ACS against a chart-reviewed reference standard defined as the treating team’s documented diagnosis. Sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value were 94.4%, 99.7%, and 72.4%, respectively. Disagreement occurred in 0.31% of encounters. Among false positives (n=1,647), the leading reason was ACS suspected but later ruled out (80.3%); among false negatives (n=257), coder omission of documented ACS (86.0%). ACS ICD codes are suitable training labels for screening models where missing ACS is more consequential than over-identification, and the observed error patterns are systematic and interpretable rather than random.
title: Validating Acute Coronary Syndrome ICD Codes as Training Labels for Clinical AI

abstract: Abstract Alveolar capillary dysplasia with malpositioned pulmonary veins (ACD/MPV) is a lethal congenital lung disorder with a mortality rate of almost 100%. Infants deteriorate within the first 24 hours of life. Here, we present a 2-day old female child born of full term normal vaginal delivery and cried immediately after birth. The baby presented with Respiratory distress within 6 hours of life and was put on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. 2-D echo revealed no congenital heart disease. The child continued to have pulmonary hypertension non-responsive to pharmacotherapy and eventually passed away. A post mortem histopathology examination revealed immature lung parenchyma with arrest in the saccular phase, thickened alveolar septae with abnormally positioned pulmonary capillaries. Focally, there were thin-walled vessels invested in the same adventitial sheath as the pulmonary arteries. The pulmonary arterioles exhibited features of pulmonary artery hypertension. Based on this constellation of features, the baby was diagnosed with ACD/MPV. The rarity and the focal nature of this condition make it a diagnostic challenge in terms of awareness of this entity and subsequent interpretation. Conclusion : This case reiterates the importance of knowing and understanding normal histology. A high degree of clinical suspicion as well as expertise in the field of thoracic pathology is required for appropriate diagnosis.
title: When tiny lungs Struggle to breathe; a rare cause of Refractory Primary Pulmonary Hypertension

abstract: Abstract Background Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) usually presents with pauci-immune necrotizing and crescentic glomerulonephritis, hematuria, and rapidly progressive kidney dysfunction. However, AAV may rarely manifest as tubulointerstitial-dominant renal injury without hematuria, creating diagnostic uncertainty. Cardiac involvement in AAV can also mimic acute coronary syndrome, particularly when dynamic electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers are present. Case presentation: A 64-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with severe oliguric acute kidney injury and acute left heart failure. Urinalysis showed predominantly tubular proteinuria without hematuria. After continuous renal replacement therapy, his heart failure improved substantially, but dynamic electrocardiographic changes and marked Troponin I elevation to 1.6 ng/mL developed on hospital day 3. Coronary angiography revealed moderate left anterior descending artery stenosis of 60–70%, which was insufficient to explain the extent of myocardial injury. MPO-ANCA was strongly positive at 215.6 AU/mL. Kidney biopsy demonstrated predominant acute tubulointerstitial nephritis with relative glomerular sparing and pauci-immune immunofluorescence, supporting a diagnosis of microscopic polyangiitis with atypical renal involvement. Although heart failure had improved, cardiac biomarkers continued to rise before subsequently normalizing in parallel with ANCA decline, suggesting vasculitis-driven myocardial injury. The patient received double filtration plasmapheresis combined with immunosuppressive therapy. ANCA titers rapidly normalized, cardiac biomarkers improved, and the patient was gradually weaned off renal replacement therapy. Conclusion This case illustrates an unusual presentation of MPO-ANCA-associated microscopic polyangiitis with tubulointerstitial-dominant nephritis without hematuria and concurrent cardiac involvement mimicking acute coronary syndrome. Improvement in volume overload or heart failure does not exclude ongoing vasculitis-related myocardial injury. In patients with unexplained acute kidney injury and concurrent myocardial injury, AAV should be considered even when hematuria is absent, and early ANCA testing, kidney biopsy, and timely immunosuppressive therapy may be crucial for organ recovery.
title: Atypical MPO-ANCA–Associated Vasculitis Presenting as Acute Tubulointerstitial Nephritis and Cardiac Involvement: A Case Report

abstract: Abstract Background and Aims: In-stent restenosis (ISR) remains a major limitation of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Inflammatory biomarkers such as interleukin-6 (IL-6) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) may contribute to ISR pathogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of IL-6, hsCRP, and the Gensini score (GS) for ISR in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) undergoing drug-eluting stent implantation. Methods and Results : A total of 262 CAD patients treated with PCI were enrolled. Patients were classified into ISR (n=107) and non-ISR (n=155) groups. ISR was assessed by protocol-driven coronary angiography performed between 6 and 12 months in all patients. Clinical, angiographic, and biochemical parameters were assessed. IL-6 and hsCRP levels were measured pre-procedurally, and CAD severity was evaluated by the Gensini score. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to determine predictive values. Serum IL-6, hsCRP levels, and GS values were significantly higher in the ISR group when compared with No ISR group (p=0.012, p=0.017, and p=0.032, respectively). ROC analysis showed moderate predictive value for IL-6 (AUC=0.717, p=0.012) and GS (AUC=0.674, p=0.040), whereas hsCRP did not reach statistical significance (AUC=0.602, p=0.171). Conclusions: Elevated IL-6 and increased GS were significantly associated with ISR, highlighting the importance of both systemic inflammation and angiographic CAD severity in restenosis risk. ClinicalTrials.gov Number: NCT03075566 (09/03/2017).
title: Interleukin 6 and high sensitive C reactive protein in predicting in-stent restenosis in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention

abstract: Abstract Background Clinical definitions can be operationalised from routine data only when the required evidence is represented, linked, and available at the intended decision time. We assessed the fitness of linked electronic health record (EHR) data for retrospective evaluation of Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction (UDMI) components. Methods This retrospective data-field audit included 6189 adults in MIMIC-IV with a pragmatic dynamic troponin T pattern above an available local upper reference limit during an estimated 2008–2019 care period. The primary analysis mapped required definition components to linked sources and quantified component-specific operational observability. Symptom and machine-electrocardiogram (ECG) evidence were anchored to 1 hour before to
title: Observability of Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction components in linked electronic health records: a retrospective MIMIC-IV study

abstract: Abstract Background Ramus intermedius (RI) changes the left main (LM) coronary division from bifurcation to trifurcation, but its associations with LM geometry, CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR), and adjacent-vessel atherosclerotic features remain incompletely characterized. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, consecutive adults who underwent clinically indicated coronary computed tomography angiography between December 2024 and April 2025 were screened. The final age-matched cohort included 300 patients (150 with RI and 150 without RI). LAD-LCX angle, vessel diameter and cross-sectional area (CSA), plaque features, stenosis severity, and CT-FFR were evaluated. RI-specific analyses by ostial location, diameter, and functional status were exploratory. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was applied within prespecified outcome families. Because sex distribution differed between groups, the primary LAD-LCX angle comparison was supplemented by an aggregate tipping-point sensitivity analysis. Results Patients with RI had a wider LAD-LCX angle than patients without RI (99.35° ± 25.61° vs. 69.22° ± 17.83°; P
title: Ramus Intermedius Anatomy and Left Main Coronary Geometry on Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography: A Retrospective Single-Center Study

abstract: Aim: To develop an integrated framework that strengthens reproducibility and interpretability in FAERS analysis through scalable drug standardization, event harmonization, and exposure normalization. Methods: FAERS reports from 2015–2024 were deduplicated. Drug ingredients were normalized to RxNorm concepts using the OHDSI Standardized Vocabularies and mapped to Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classifications. Adverse event terms were harmonized across MedDRA versions. U.S. exposure estimates from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS) were mapped to RxNorm concepts and aligned with event year to derive annual reporting rates and assess temporal trends. The framework was demonstrated using two case studies. Results: The analytic dataset included 13.8 million cases. Exact RxNorm mapping was achieved for 95.8% of 30.5 million suspect or interacting drug records. A total of 769 legacy PTs (3.6% of event terms; affecting 4.4% of cases) were mapped to MedDRA v28.0. MEPS exposure estimates were linked to 513 RxNorm concepts representing 46.1% of U.S. FAERS drug records, with 80.8% of drug-year estimates meeting AHRQ precision standards. For bleeding, the cumulative rivaroxaban–apixaban reporting odds ratio remained elevated, while reporting rates reversed after 2020. For myocardial infarction, SGLT2 inhibitors showed higher disproportionality and reporting rates than GLP-1 receptor agonists, but drug-level analysis revealed marked within-class heterogeneity. Conclusion: Drug standardization and event harmonization reduced key sources of inconsistency in FAERS, while exposure-normalized reporting rates placed case counts in the context of drug utilization. Linked through RxNorm concepts and aligned by event year, these components work together to improve the reproducibility and interpretability of FAERS analysis.
title: Strengthening Reproducibility and Interpretability in FAERS Analysis through Drug Standardization, Event Harmonization, and Exposure Normalization

abstract: Background: Coronary artery disease (CAD), a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, negatively impacts psychological well-being. Depressive and anxiety symptoms are commonly reported by patients with CAD, but little is known about symptom interconnectedness in this population. Insight into this interconnectedness may improve our understanding of how comorbidity arises and persists. Therefore, our aim was to gain new insights into the comorbidity of anxiety and depression symptoms in patients with CAD by estimating psychological networks at multiple time points. Methods: 2241 patients who had undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (22.2% women; mean age = 65.0, SD= 10.3) were included. With five cross-sectional psychological networks measured at five timepoints over two years, the symptom-level dynamics of depressive and anxiety symptoms were studied. Besides the overall network structure, network communities, centrality measures and sub-group differences were explored. Results: The estimated Bayesian Gaussian graphical models showed predominantly positive associations, and symptoms were mostly connected within their own domain of depression or anxiety. Two symptom clusters remained relatively stable: Depressed mood, feelings of worthlessness, and suicidal ideation consistently clustered together, while in the first month post PCI, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and appetite disturbance tended to co-occur. Fatigue, depressed mood, difficulty relaxing, and restlessness showed high connectivity and acted as bridging symptoms between different symptom groups. Conclusion: These findings suggest that both symptoms related to depression and to anxiety should be targeted within cardiac rehabilitation programs to reduce patients' psychological burden.
title: Mapping the Dynamics of Depressive and Anxiety symptoms in Coronary Artery Disease over two years: A Network Analysis

abstract: Background: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TTC) is a stress-induced cardiomyopathy characterized by acute cardiac dysfunction, inflammation, and hypertrophy, yet no therapy directly targets the underlying myocardial injury. Clinical studies have reported elevated circulating Angiotensin II (Ang II) levels in TTC patients, suggesting dysregulation of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS). Given the established cardioprotective effects of Angiotensin-(1-7) [Ang-(1–7)] in other cardiovascular diseases, we hypothesized that oral administration of Ang-(1–7) could attenuate acute cardiac remodeling during TTC. Methods Female C57BL/6J mice were subjected to a single high-dose isoproterenol (ISO) injection (300 mg/Kg, intraperitoneal) to induce TTC and received daily oral treatment with Ang-(1-7) complexed with hydroxypropyl β-cyclodextrin [Ang-(1-7)-CD] or vehicle (CD), for 4 days, beginning one day before ISO administration. Cardiac proteome alterations were characterized by tandem mass tag (TMT)-based quantitative proteomics. Cardiac hypertrophy was assessed by heart weight normalized to tibial length and cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area. Myocardial inflammation was evaluated by histopathology, CD68 immunostaining, and flow cytometric analysis of infiltrating leukocyte populations. Results We observed a distinct cardiac proteome signature in Ang-(1-7)-treated ISO mice, predicting inhibition of pathways associated with cardiac hypertrophy and adverse remodeling. These molecular changes were accompanied by reduced heart weight normalized to tibial length and smaller cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area compared with vehicle-treated ISO mice. Oral Ang-(1-7) also attenuated myocardial inflammation, as evidenced by lower inflammatory scores, reduced CD68+ macrophage infiltration, decreased numbers of CD45+ leukocytes, and marked suppression of Ly6G+ neutrophil and CCR2+ monocyte recruitment to the heart. These protective effects were associated with improved survival following ISO challenge. MS data are available via ProteomeXchange (PXD082872). Conclusions Oral administration of Ang-(1–7) attenuated acute cardiac hypertrophy and inflammation in experimental TTC while inducing cardiac proteome changes consistent with reduced adverse remodeling. These findings identify activation of the protective RAS axis as a promising therapeutic strategy for limiting myocardial injury during TTC.
title: Oral administration of Angiotensin-(1–7) included in hydroxypropyl β-cyclodextrin attenuates cardiac hypertrophy and inflammation in a mouse model of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy

abstract: Background: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is the most common valvular heart disease in older adults and currently has no approved pharmacological therapy to prevent or slow disease progression. Aortic valve replacement, either surgically or by transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), therefore remains the only effective treatment for severe CAVD. Monocytes play an important role in driving inflammation and disease progression in CAVD. As the disease progresses and the aortic valve becomes increasingly stenotic, circulating monocytes passing through the narrowed valve are repeatedly exposed to pathological haemodynamic forces, including markedly elevated shear stress, before their recruitment into the valve tissue. However, how exposure to these mechanical forces reprograms circulating monocytes influences their subsequent responses within the valve remain poorly understood. Methods and Results: In this study, we used an engineered model of aortic valve stenosis combined with phosphoproteomic profiling to investigate how prolonged exposure to pathological shear stress reprograms circulating monocytes and influences their subsequent phenotype and function following recruitment into the valve matrix. We further used TAVI as a unique clinical model to determine whether restoration of physiological haemodynamics in patients with severe aortic stenosis reverses the shear-induced monocyte phenotype observed in our experimental model. We found that prolonged exposure of monocytes to pathological shear stress induced extensive remodelling of the proteomic and phosphoproteomic landscape, with enrichment of pathways associated with cellular metabolism, cytoskeletal organisation, and inflammatory signalling. Kinase activity analysis further identified increased protein kinase C (PKC) activity accompanied by suppression of AKT signalling. Consistent with these molecular changes, pathological shear stress increased actin polymerisation, mitochondrial membrane potential, intracellular calcium signalling, and PKC activity. Using a bioengineered extracellular matrix model that recapitulates the glycosaminoglycan-rich microenvironment of the stenotic aortic valve we found that prior exposure to pathological shear stress altered monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation, reducing oxidised LDL uptake and foam-cell formation while promoting co-expression of CD80 and CD163, indicative of a mixed macrophage phenotype. Finally, using a myeloid-specific Piezo1 knockout mouse model, we identified Piezo1 as a key mechanosensor linking pathological shear stress to PKC activation, mitochondrial responses, and persistent changes in monocyte phenotype following migration into the extracellular matrix. Conclusions: These findings establish a mechanistic link between abnormal valve haemodynamics, metabolic and inflammatory reprogramming of circulating monocytes, extracellular matrix remodelling, and immune dysregulation during CAVD progression, highlighting monocyte mechanotransduction and downstream PKC/Piezo1 signalling as potential therapeutic targets.
title: Phosphoproteomics profiling of the monocytes uncovers the mechanosensory pathways regulating monocytes responses to pathologic level of shear stress

abstract: Background Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) has emerged as a prognostic biomarker in patients with non-ST-segment-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). Our study evaluated the temporal evolution of GDF-15 in the acute phase and its association with recurrent ischemic events. Methods Serum samples were collected from patients with NSTE-ACS at admission and at 1 and 3 hours after admission. GDF-15 levels, along with other prognostic biomarkers, NT-proBNP and hs-cTnT, were measured. Spearman’s rank-correlation coefficients and linear regression models were used to identify the variables associated with GDF-15 levels at admission and with their temporal changes. Associations between GDF-15 and clinical outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. To assess incremental prognostic value, the areas under the curve (AUC) were calculated for each model. Results GDF-15 levels showed a slight increasing trend within 3 hours of admission. The 1-hour change in GDF-15 was correlated with hs-cTnT changes. Increased 1-hour GDF-15 levels, compared with the admission levels, were associated with a higher risk of recurrent ischemic events during the 1-year follow-up (1.9% vs. 17.5%, P =0.019) and were an independent predictor after adjusting for established clinical variables and biomarkers (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.71 [1.28 to 228.75], P =0.03). Furthermore, serial measurements of GDF-15 provided additional prognostic information beyond traditional risk factors. Conclusions Serial measurements of GDF-15 of NSTE-ACS patients provided independent and incremental prognostic value for predicting recurrent ischemic events. These findings support the potential utility of GDF-15 as a dynamic biomarker for early risk stratification in the acute management of NSTE-ACS.
title: Serial measurements of Growth Differentiation Factor-15 in patients with Non-ST-Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome and recurrent ischemic events

abstract: Heart failure remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with cardiac fibrosis contributing to disease progression. Following myocardial injury, activated cardiac fibroblasts orchestrate adverse extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, which leads to tissue stiffening and compromised contractility. Despite the clinical importance of cardiac fibrosis, current pharmacological interventions modulate disease progression without directly eliminating activated fibrogenic cells. To target these cells directly, we engineered human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived neutrophils expressing a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) directed against fibroblast activation protein (FAP). In vitro, FAP CAR neutrophils exhibited increased reactive oxygen species-associated fluorescence during fibroblast co-culture and dose-dependent cytotoxicity in 2D cultures, while reducing fibroblast-associated fluorescence in 3D cardiac organoids without a significant reduction in cardiomyocyte-associated cardiac troponin T staining. FAP CAR neutrophils also showed increased iNOS and decreased Arginase-1 expression compared with unmodified neutrophils, consistent with a shift toward an N1-associated polarization profile. Analysis of public cardiac single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets identified temporal patterns of immune-associated expression and fibroblast activation that informed treatment timing. In a murine myocardial infarction (MI) model, mice treated systemically with FAP CAR neutrophils showed higher day 7 left ventricular ejection fraction than PBS-treated mice in an exploratory comparison. Together, these findings support further evaluation of hPSC-derived FAP CAR neutrophils as an immunotherapeutic approach to cardiac fibrosis.
title: Targeting Cardiac Fibrosis with Chimeric Antigen Receptor Neutrophils Derived from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells

abstract: Introduction In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), wall stress and subclinical myocardial injury related in part to pathological hypercontractility, which in turn are associated with worse outcomes. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is released from cardiomyocytes (cfDNA-CM) through irreversible cellular injury and death. We investigated the feasibility of quantifying cfDNA-CM and its relationship to HCM patient characteristics. Methods We analyzed 57 plasma samples from stable patients with HCM and 10 plasma samples from patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Plasma cfDNA was isolated from both groups. Whole genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) libraries were generated and sequenced with short-read sequencing. Methylation patterns were used for tissue deconvolution analysis and cell-specific cfDNA quantification. Results Yields of cfDNA (p = 0.003) and cfDNA-CM (p = 0.002) fractions were higher in AMI controls than HCM, supporting the validity of the assay. Within the HCM cohort, the median cfDNA yield was 12.22 ng [IQR: 7.77, 18.94]. The cfDNA-CM fraction in this cohort ranged from 0% to 6.4% of total cfDNA. Higher cfDNA-CM tertiles were associated with higher body mass index (BMI, p=0.001), a greater prevalence of BMI ≥30 kg/m² (p Conclusion Isolation and quantification of cfDNA as well as detection of cfDNA-CM in chronic stable patients with HCM are feasible. Higher cfDNA-CM fraction was associated with increasing BMI and cardiometabolic comorbidity burden. The absence of association with traditional circulating biomarkers suggests that cfDNA-CM may reflect a distinct domain of myocardial health, injury, and adverse remodeling.
title: Cardiomyocyte-Derived Cell-Free DNA in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

abstract: Background Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) provides non-pharmacological stroke prevention for non-valvular atrial fibrillation patients with contraindications to long-term oral anticoagulation. National long-term data on age-adjusted utilization trends and demographic adoption disparities remain limited. Objectives To evaluate national temporal trends, hospital characteristics, clinical acuity shifts, and demographic adoption patterns of percutaneous LAAO procedures. Methods Using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 through 2022, percutaneous LAAO procedures were identified using ICD-10-PCS code 02L73DK. Weighted national estimates were used to evaluate patient demographics, hospital factors, clinical acuity, and overall in-hospital mortality. Age-adjusted rates per 100,000 population were calculated using direct standardization to the 2000 U.S. standard population. Results A total of 190,020 weighted LAAO procedures were identified increasing from 4,875 in 2016 to 60,445 in 2022. The mean patient age was 76.3 ± 7.6 years, and 58.5% were male. Most patients were White (90.4%), while Hispanic (4.3%), Black (3.9%), and Asian/Pacific Islander (1.3%) patients accounted for smaller proportions of procedures. Most procedures were performed at urban teaching hospitals (87.0%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 0.1% (n = 225, p = 0.582). Minor APR-DRG risk of mortality increased from 43.5% to 55.5%, while all others decreased ( p Conclusions Percutaneous LAAO utilization expanded rapidly with exceptionally low inpatient mortality. Persistent gaps in age-adjusted rates highlight key racial, sex, and geographic disparities in structural heart care. Condensed Abstract Using the 2016–2022 National Inpatient Sample, this study evaluated temporal trends and demographic adoption patterns of percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). Among 190,020 weighted procedures, annual volume increased from 4,875 to 60,445. In-hospital mortality was exceptionally low (0.1%). Age-adjusted procedural rates rose from 34.19 to 379.87 per 100,000 population. However, significant disparities persisted, characterized by heavy centralization in urban teaching hospitals (87.0%) and disproportionately lower absolute age-adjusted utilization among female, Black, Hispanic, and Asian/Pacific Islander patients compared to male and White cohorts. Targeted initiatives are needed to ensure equitable access to structural heart interventions.
title: Temporal Trends and Demographic Disparities in Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Utilization in the United States, 2016–2022

abstract: Cardiac damage in the aftermath of myocardial ischemia / reperfusion (MI/R) compromises both electrical and mechanical function, predisposing patients to arrhythmia and heart failure. Microvascular obstruction (MVO) is increasingly recognized as a sequela of MI/R and a contributor to proarrhythmic cardiac remodeling. While transvalvular unloading (TVU) using a percutaneously delivered pump is garnering appreciation as a means of limiting infarct size and preserving mechanical function following percutaneous coronary intervention, its benefits for arrhythmia prevention remain unclear. We used a porcine model to test the hypothesis that cardiac unloading prior to and through reperfusion mitigates MVO, preserves cardiomyocyte nanostructure, and alleviates arrhythmias following MI/R. Anesthetized domestic swine undergoing acute ischemia (LAD occlusion, 90 mins) and reperfusion (120 mins) were randomized to TVU (n=5) and no treatment (control; n=6) treatments. Thioflavin-S was infused into the mid-LAD to assess coronary microcirculation and quantify MVO. Arrhythmia burden was assessed by in vivo electrocardiography using 3 lead EKG. Cardiac tissues were preserved for histology and optical microscopy studies. Compared to no treatment controls, TVU hearts evidenced significantly reduced infarct area (48 +/- 5 % vs. 59 +/- 11 % p = 0.03) and MVO (19 +/- 4 % vs. 27 +/- 5% , p = 0.03) normalized to area at risk and a higher myocardial salvage index (52 +/- 5 % vs. 41 +/- 11% p = 0.03). Extensive perivascular edema, and neutrophil infiltration observed in controls was markedly reduced in TVU hearts. Confocal microscopy and spatial pattern analysis revealed significantly mitigated disruption of gap junctions and NaV1.5 dissociation from N-cadherin in TVU hearts compared to controls. Importantly, severity-adjusted arrhythmia burden during reperfusion was significantly lower in TV-P hearts (8+/-8 vs. 12+/-5 episodes lasting greater than 5seconds in controls). Our results demonstrate that TVU effectively prevents arrhythmias during reperfusion by preserving coronary microvasculature and cardiomyocyte nanostructure.
title: Cardiac unloading via a transvalvular pump prevents arrhythmias following myocardial ischemia / reperfusion by preserving coronary microcirculation and cardiomyocyte nanostructure

abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but its impact on human diagnostic performance, the added value of visual explanations, and differences by reader background and experience remain uncertain. MethodsUsing 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) images from two hospitals, we developed and externally validated an ensemble of three deep learning models after self-supervised pretraining and fine-tuning. The diagnostic task used ECGs recorded within 14 days after symptom onset, regardless of reperfusion status. We conducted a four-phase reader study. Phases 1-3 compared unaided interpretation, a reference sheet, and additional AI assistance. In Phase 4, readers evaluated a new ECG set after randomization to reference-sheet support alone, with AI predictions, or with AI predictions plus gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) heatmaps. Diagnostic correctness was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models. Exploratory analyses examined differences by cardiologist status and experience. ResultsDevelopment and external-validation cohorts, including healthy controls, comprised 832 and 95 participants, respectively. For Takotsubo-STEMI discrimination, external-validation accuracy was 0.914, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic and precision-recall curves of 0.970 and 0.984. Seventy healthcare providers completed the reader study. The estimated probability of correct diagnosis increased from 0.632 without assistance to 0.864 with AI assistance (odds ratio [OR], 3.71; P<0.001). In randomized Phase 4, AI assistance improved accuracy vs reference-sheet support alone (OR, 4.28; 95% CI, 3.08-5.95; P<0.001), and Grad-CAM provided additional benefit (OR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.04-2.25; P=0.033). Exploratory analyses showed greater improvement among less experienced readers; with AI assistance, non-cardiologists outperformed cardiologists. AI-assisted readers remained less accurate overall than the model alone. ConclusionsAn ECG image-based ensemble differentiated Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI and improved reader accuracy. Visual explanations provided additional benefit, while experience-related differences highlight the importance of effective human-AI interaction. C_LIO_LIIn a human diagnostic test, displaying the models prediction improved readers diagnostic performance, and adding gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) explanation produced further gains. C_LIO_LIExploratory analyses showed greater improvement and higher AI-assisted accuracy among less experienced readers, with reversal of cardiologists unaided advantage under AI assistance, motivating a utilization bias hypothesis. C_LIO_LIAI assistance improved reader diagnostic accuracy, with further benefit from Grad-CAM visualizations, supporting further evaluation of these tools in clinical practice. title: Deep learning-based electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction: explainability, human-AI interaction, and a utilization bias hypothesis

abstract: Aims: Rosuvastatin is commonly co-administered with ticagrelor in patients with acute coronary syndrome. Ticagrelor inhibits breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP/ABCG2), increasing rosuvastatin exposure and potentially the risk of rhabdomyolysis. This risk may be further influenced by age and the ABCG2 c.421C>A variant. We aimed to predict optimal rosuvastatin dosing with ticagrelor in elderly patients stratified by ABCG2 genotype using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modelling Methods PBPK models for rosuvastatin and ticagrelor were developed and validated in PK-Sim using clinical data from healthy adults, elderly patients, and individuals with wild-type or homozygous ABCG2 c.421C>A genotypes. Key parameters, including BCRP catalytic activity and age-dependent declines in CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 activity, were optimized. The drug-drug interaction model incorporated competitive BCRP inhibition by ticagrelor. Rosuvastatin steady-state exposure was simulated with half or quarter standard doses during ticagrelor co-administration, and exposure matching approach was used to identify optimal dosing. Results The PBPK models demonstrated good predictive performance across populations and genotypes. In young adults with the wild-type genotype, halving the rosuvastatin dose resulted in an AUC fold change of 1.44, supporting a half-dose strategy. In young homozygous variant carriers, half-dose co-administration produced comparable exposure (AUC fold change 0.78). In elderly wild-type individuals, a four-fold dose reduction achieved comparable exposure (AUC fold change 1.06), whereas elderly variant carriers required only a half-dose reduction (1.12). Conclusions PBPK modelling supported age- and ABCG2 genotype-specific rosuvastatin dosing with ticagrelor. Elderly wild-type patients may require a further dose reduction to minimise toxicity while maintaining therapeutic exposure.
title: PBPK Model-Based Prediction of Optimal Rosuvastatin Dosing with Concomitant Ticagrelor in Elderly Patients Considering ABCG2 Genetic Variant

abstract: Background: The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a routinely available blood-derived marker with potential prognostic relevance after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). We evaluated associations between preoperative SII and postoperative outcomes. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched to 1 October 2026, with supplementary searches through 14 October 2026. Peer-reviewed observational studies evaluating preoperative SII in adults undergoing CABG were eligible. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Compatible categorical associations and exploratory adjusted continuous mortality effects were pooled separately using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models; other findings were summarized descriptively. Results: Thirty-one reports were included, with an aggregate sample of 30,976 and possible cohort overlap; five contributed to meta-analysis. Two off-pump cohorts comprising 1,378 patients and 180 atrial-fibrillation events yielded an imprecise crude association with postoperative atrial fibrillation (OR 1.60, 95%CI 0.53-4.82; I2=68%). An exploratory crude synthesis indicated greater intra-aortic balloon pump use with higher SII (OR 2.45, 95%CI 1.16-5.18; I2=51%). Two cohorts with differing follow-up yielded an exploratory adjusted mortality HR of 1.11 (95% Wald CI 1.05-1.18) per study-specific SD increase in log-SII. In one 624-patient cohort, high SII was associated with postoperative acute kidney injury after adjustment (OR 3.35, 95% CI 2.25-4.97).Apparent atrial-fibrillation discrimination varied (AUC 0.587-0.946). Conclusions: Preoperative SII showed associations with selected adverse outcomes after CABG, supporting further evaluation as an accessible prognostic marker. Its incremental value beyond established clinical risk models requires validation. Keywords: Systemic immune-inflammation index; Coronary artery bypass grafting; Atrial fibrillation; Prognosis; Systematic review
title: Preoperative Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index and Clinical Outcomes After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
